55.name: Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole
55.stored: perKg 5 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 800 mg, maxDaily 1600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 10 mg/kg/day; adult ceiling allowed = 800 mg/dose, 1600 mg/day.
55.source: FDA label, BACTRIM / BACTRIM DS (sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim) tablets, DailyMed
55.note: The per-kg number and the ceilings are expressed in two different components of the combination, so the caps are 5x too high. The 5 mg/kg q12h rule is clearly the TRIMETHOPRIM component: the label's paediatric dose is '40 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg trimethoprim per 24 hours, given in two divided doses every 12 hours', i.e. 4 mg TMP/kg/dose; 5 mg/kg q12h = 10 mg TMP/kg/day, which is acceptable (Medscape/AAP quote 8-12 mg TMP/kg/day divided q12h), so the per-kg value itself is not the defect. But maxSingle 800 / maxDaily 1600 are the SULFAMETHOXAZOLE contents of one and two DS tablets. The label's adult dose for UTI/shigellosis is '1 BACTRIM DS tablet or 2 BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours' = 160 mg TMP per dose, 320 mg TMP/day. With the stored rule a 70 kg adult is shown 350 mg q12h (700 mg TMP/day, ~4.4 DS tablets/day) and a 100 kg adult 500 mg q12h, with no clamp, because the cap is set at the SMX number. That is 2-3x the routine adult dose and approaches PCP-treatment exposure (label PCP dose is 15-20 mg TMP/kg/day), with the associated hyperkalaemia, AKI and marrow-suppression risk. Two further gaps: the label carries an explicit renal table (CrCl >30 usual regimen; CrCl 15-30 half the usual regimen; CrCl <15 use not recommended) and renalAdj is empty; and the drug is contraindicated in infants under 2 months, but ageAdj is empty (the dataset does use factor-0 ageAdj elsewhere, e.g. Aspirin 0-12 and Levofloxacin 0-18, so the omission is a real gap, not a convention). If instead the app intends 'dose' to be the combined TMP+SMX milligrams, the rule is wrong the other way: combined paediatric dose is 48 mg/kg/day = 24 mg/kg/dose q12h, so 5 mg/kg would under-dose ~5x. Either reading is a mismatch; the unit field should state which component it means.
55.suggestedFix: Label the unit explicitly as 'mg trimethoprim component'. Keep kind=perKg, dose 5 (mg TMP/kg), freq q12h, but set maxSingle 160 and maxDaily 320 (= 1 DS tablet q12h). Add renalAdj [[30,999,1],[15,30,0.5],[0,15,0]] and ageAdj [[0,0.167,0]] (contraindicated <2 months). If PCP dosing is wanted, add it as a separate record: 5 mg TMP/kg q6h (15-20 mg/kg/day), no 160 mg cap.
55.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED (could not refute). I retrieved the Bactrim label and a second generic co-trimoxazole label myself. The label states adult UTI dosing as '1 BACTRIM DS (double strength) tablet or 2 BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours' (= 160 mg TMP / 800 mg SMX per dose) and paediatric as '40 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg trimethoprim per 24 hours, given in two divided doses every 12 hours'. Decisively, the generic label states verbatim: 'The total daily dose should not exceed 1600 mg sulfamethoxazole and 320 mg trimethoprim.' That single sentence shows the stored ceilings (maxSingle 800, maxDaily 1600) are the SULFAMETHOXAZOLE figures, while a 5 mg/kg per-dose value can only be the TRIMETHOPRIM component. The record is internally inconsistent under every possible reading: (a) dose = TMP -> 10 mg TMP/kg/day; a 70 kg adult is shown 350 mg q12h = 700 mg TMP/day, 2.2x the labelled 320 mg TMP/day maximum, and the 800/1600 caps never clamp because they are 5x the correct TMP ceilings; (b) dose = SMX -> the caps are right but 10 mg SMX/kg/day against a labelled 40 mg/kg/day is a 4x under-dose; (c) dose = combined -> 10 vs 48 mg/kg/day, ~5x under-dose, and the caps do not match a DS tablet's 960 mg combined either. I also confirm the two omissions: the label carries an explicit renal table (CrCl >30 usual regimen; 15-30 half the regimen; <15 not recommended) and renalAdj is empty, and CONTRAINDICATIONS lists 'pediatric patients less than 2 months of age' while ageAdj is empty. One correction that makes the claim slightly UNDERSTATED rather than overstated: the claim concedes 10 mg TMP/kg/day is 'acceptable', but the FDA label's paediatric default is 8 mg TMP/kg/day, so the stored per-kg value is itself ~25% above the labelled default (it sits inside the 8-12 mg/kg/day range only for more serious infections, which is not what a default should show). Verdict MISMATCH, severity high: ~2x the labelled adult TMP exposure with no clamp, approaching PCP-range dosing, with hyperkalaemia/AKI/marrow-suppression risk, plus no renal or neonatal guard. Suggested fix: declare the unit as 'mg TMP', store perKg 4 mg/kg q12h (8 mg TMP/kg/day), maxSingle 160 mg, maxDaily 320 mg; ageAdj [0, 0.167, 0] (contraindicated <2 months); renalAdj [[30, 999, 1.0], [15, 30, 0.5], [0, 15, 0]].
55.fix: 4 mg TMP (kg başına), q12h, tek doz tavanı 160, günlük tavan 320; 2 yaş bandı; 3 böbrek bandı. Kaynak: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f59d0c04-9c66-4d53-a0e1-cb55570deb62 (kaynaktan türetildi; tek red gerekçesi olan motor hatası giderildi)

56.name: Nitrofurantoin
56.stored: fixed 100 mg q6h, maxSingle 100 mg, maxDaily 400 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 400 mg regardless of weight or age.
56.source: FDA label, MACRODANTIN (nitrofurantoin, macrocrystalline) capsules, DailyMed
56.note: The number is right for an adult and wrong for every child, and the two contraindications that make this drug dangerous are not encoded. The label's adult dose is '50-100 mg four times a day' (lower dose for uncomplicated infection), so fixed 100 mg q6h = 400 mg/day is the labelled adult maximum - no daily-total multiplication error here. But the paediatric dose is '5-7 mg/kg of body weight per 24 hours, given in four divided doses', i.e. 1.25-1.75 mg/kg per dose. Because kind=fixed ignores weight and there is no ageAdj, a 15 kg child is shown 100 mg q6h = 400 mg/day against a labelled 75-105 mg/day: a 4-5x overdose, and worse in infants. The label contraindicates the drug in 'neonates under one month of age' (haemolytic anaemia from immature erythrocyte enzyme systems) and where there is 'significant impairment of renal function (creatinine clearance under 60 mL per minute or clinically significant elevated serum creatinine)'; both renalAdj and ageAdj are empty, so the app gives a full adult dose to a neonate and to an anuric patient. In renal impairment nitrofurantoin fails to reach the urine (treatment failure) while systemic accumulation drives neuropathy and pulmonary toxicity.
56.suggestedFix: kind=perKg, dose 1.5 mg/kg, freq q6h, maxSingle 100, maxDaily 400 (adult 70 kg then lands at ~100 mg q6h, matching the label). ageAdj [[0,0.083,0]] (contraindicated <1 month). renalAdj [[0,60,0]] (contraindicated CrCl <60 per the US label; if the app prefers current practice, [[0,30,0]] with a warning band 30-60). Optionally add a second record for the monohydrate/macrocrystal product (Macrobid): fixed 100 mg q12h, maxDaily 200.
56.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED (could not refute). I retrieved the label myself (Macrodantin, nitrofurantoin macrocrystals). It states the adult dose as '50-100 mg four times a day -- the lower dosage level is recommended for uncomplicated urinary tract infections' and the paediatric dose as '5-7 mg/kg of body weight per 24 hours, given in four divided doses (contraindicated under one month of age)'. So the stored 100 mg q6h = 400 mg/day is the labelled adult maximum and there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error, exactly as the claim concedes. The defect is that kind=fixed ignores weight with no ageAdj: for a 15 kg child the label gives 75-105 mg/DAY, while the app shows 400 mg/day, a 4-5x overdose, and proportionally worse in infants. An independent paediatric reference corroborates 5-7 mg/kg/day divided in 4 doses with a 100 mg/dose maximum. I also confirm both missing guards verbatim from CONTRAINDICATIONS: 'Anuria, oliguria, or significant impairment of renal function (creatinine clearance under 60 mL per minute or clinically significant elevated serum creatinine) are contraindications', and contraindication in neonates under one month of age due to haemolytic anaemia from immature erythrocyte enzyme systems; both renalAdj and ageAdj are empty. A further point the claim did not make, which strengthens it: even the adult default is the upper end of the range, since the label reserves the lower 50 mg dose for uncomplicated UTI, which is the commonest use of this drug. Verdict MISMATCH, severity high: multi-fold paediatric overdose, full adult dosing to a neonate (haemolysis) and to a patient in renal failure (treatment failure from inadequate urinary concentration plus systemic accumulation causing neuropathy and pulmonary toxicity). Suggested fix: split by age, or store perKg 1.5 mg/kg q6h (6 mg/kg/day) with maxSingle 100 mg and maxDaily 400 mg so adults clamp to the labelled 100 mg q6h; ageAdj [0, 0.083, 0] (contraindicated <1 month); renalAdj [[60, 999, 1.0], [0, 60, 0]] (contraindicated below CrCl 60).
56.fix: 1.25 (kg başına), q6h, tek doz tavanı 50, günlük tavan 400; 2 yaş bandı; 2 böbrek bandı. Kaynak: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=89d8696b-f9ce-9691-6222-8416ca143bba&type=display (kaynaktan türetildi; tek red gerekçesi olan motor hatası giderildi)

57.name: Fosfomycin
57.stored: fixed 3000 mg q24h, maxSingle 3000 mg, maxDaily 3000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. The q24h frequency presents it as a once-daily repeating regimen.
57.source: FDA label, fosfomycin tromethamine granules for oral solution (Monurol), DailyMed
57.note: The milligram amount is correct but the regimen cannot be expressed as dose x frequency: this is one-off therapy, not a daily drug. The label states the dose for 'women 18 years of age and older for uncomplicated urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) is one sachet' (3 g of fosfomycin) and, under Precautions, 'Do not use more than one single dose of Fosfomycin Tromethamine to treat a single episode of acute cystitis. Repeated daily doses of Fosfomycin Tromethamine did not improve the clinical success or microbiological eradication rates compared to single dose therapy, but did increase the incidence of adverse events.' Storing freq=q24h makes the calculator display a daily regimen the label explicitly warns against; a clinician following a 3-5 day 'course' at 3 g/day is giving 3-5x the labelled exposure with no added benefit. Secondary problems: the indication is restricted to women (not indicated in men), and 'safety and effectiveness in children age 12 years and under have not been established', yet ageAdj is empty, so a 15 kg child would be shown the full 3 g adult sachet. Harm from a repeated 3 g dose is mainly gastrointestinal rather than life-threatening, hence moderate rather than high.
57.suggestedFix: Keep dose 3000 mg but change freq to a single-administration value (e.g. 'once' / x1) so no daily multiplication occurs, maxSingle 3000, maxDaily 3000, and attach the label text 'single dose only - do not repeat for the same episode'. Add ageAdj [[0,12,0]] (not established <=12 years) and a note that the indication is uncomplicated cystitis in women. If a multi-dose off-label regimen is wanted for complicated UTI, store it separately as 3 g every 48-72 hours x3 doses and flag it as off-label.
57.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED (could not refute), though it is the mildest of the four. I retrieved the Monurol label myself and it carries the quoted precaution verbatim: 'Do not use more than one single dose of Fosfomycin Tromethamine to treat a single episode of acute cystitis. Repeated daily doses of Fosfomycin Tromethamine did not improve the clinical success or microbiological eradication rates compared to single dose therapy, but did increase the incidence of adverse events.' The dose statement is also as quoted ('one sachet' for 'women 18 years of age and older'), the indication is restricted to women, and 'Safety and effectiveness in children age 12 years and under have not been established'. So the 3000 mg amount is right and the defect is purely the model: freq=q24h with the engine treating freq as a repeating schedule presents a once-daily course for a drug that is one-off therapy. I looked specifically for a labelled repeating regimen that would rescue q24h and found only a narrow one: the European SmPC for Monuril 3 g gives 3 g once for acute uncomplicated cystitis in women and female adolescents >12 years, and a second 3 g dose 24 hours later ONLY for perioperative prophylaxis in transrectal prostate biopsy (it also advises against use at CrCl <10 mL/min). Multi-dose regimens in the literature for complicated UTI are 3 g every 48-72 hours, not q24h, and are off-label. None of that makes a repeating q24h default defensible for the cystitis indication this record represents. I also confirm the age gap: kind=fixed with empty ageAdj would show a 15 kg child the full 3 g adult sachet, against 'not established' at <=12 years in the US label and >12 years only in the EU SmPC. Verdict MODEL_WRONG, severity moderate: harm from repeated 3 g doses is predominantly gastrointestinal with no efficacy gain, not life-threatening. Suggested fix: represent as a single dose (freq 'once'/'stat' rather than q24h, or a flag stating 'single dose only - do not repeat for one episode of cystitis'), keep fixed 3000 mg with maxSingle 3000 and maxDaily 3000; ageAdj [0, 12, 0]; renalAdj [[10, 999, 1.0], [0, 10, 0]]; note the indication is limited to women.
57.blockNote: Fosfomisin trometamol, komplike olmayan sistitte yalnızca tek seferlik 3 g olarak verilir ve aynı atak için tekrarlanmaz. Hesaplayıcı tek seferlik dozu ifade edemediği ve dozu her gün tekrarlanacakmış gibi göstermek hatalı olacağı için doz gösterilmiyor.

58.name: Rifampin
58.stored: perKg 10 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 600 mg, maxDaily 600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 10 mg/kg/day, clamped at 600 mg.
58.note: Exact match to the label for the default (TB) indication. The label gives adults '10 mg/kg, in a single daily administration, not to exceed 600 mg/day, orally' and paediatric patients '10 to 20 mg/kg, not to exceed 600 mg/day'. Stored 10 mg/kg q24h with both ceilings at 600 mg reproduces the adult figure exactly and sits at the bottom of the paediatric range; since freq is q24h, maxSingle = maxDaily = 600 is internally consistent and no daily-total multiplication error exists. Two non-defect caveats worth surfacing in the app rather than changing the numbers: (1) WHO/ATS paediatric practice now uses 15 mg/kg (range 10-20) for children, so 10 mg/kg is the conservative end for a child; (2) the other common indication has a completely different regimen - meningococcal carrier state is '600 mg rifampin administered twice daily for two days' in adults, '10 mg/kg (not to exceed 600 mg per dose) every 12 hours for two days' in children >=1 month, and '5 mg/kg every 12 hours for two days' under 1 month - which this single record cannot represent.
58.suggestedFix: No change required to the default. Optionally add ageAdj [[0,15,1.5]] to reach the WHO paediatric 15 mg/kg (still clamped at 600 mg), and add a separate record for meningococcal prophylaxis: 10 mg/kg q12h x 2 days, maxSingle 600, with ageAdj [[0,0.083,0.5]] for neonates under 1 month.

59.name: Isoniazid
59.stored: perKg 5 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 300 mg, maxDaily 300 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 5 mg/kg/day for every patient, child or adult.
59.note: This is the adult dose applied to children, and it under-doses them by 2-3x. The label separates the two populations explicitly: for TB treatment, adults '5 mg/kg up to 300 mg daily in a single dose', children '10 - 15 mg/kg up to 300 mg daily in a single dose'. For latent TB it gives infants and children '10 mg/kg (up to 300 mg daily)'. With the stored flat 5 mg/kg, a 20 kg child is shown 100 mg/day against a labelled 200-300 mg/day, and a 10 kg toddler 50 mg against 100-150 mg. Sub-therapeutic isoniazid in tuberculosis means treatment failure and selection of INH-resistant organisms - a delayed but serious harm, and one a clinician is unlikely to catch because the number looks like a textbook isoniazid dose. The adult default itself (5 mg/kg, max 300 mg once daily) is correct, and there is no daily-total multiplication error. Also missing: the label's advice that 'concomitant administration of pyridoxine (B6) is recommended in malnourished and in those predisposed to neuropathy (e.g., alcoholics and diabetics)', and there is no hepatotoxicity/monitoring flag despite the boxed warning for severe and fatal hepatitis.
59.suggestedFix: Keep perKg 5 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 300, maxDaily 300 for adults, and add ageAdj [[0,15,2.4]] so children receive ~12 mg/kg (mid of the labelled 10-15 mg/kg) still clamped at 300 mg. Add a pyridoxine co-administration note and a hepatotoxicity/LFT-monitoring flag (set flag=true). Intermittent regimens (adults 15 mg/kg up to 900 mg two or three times weekly; children 20-40 mg/kg up to 900 mg) need a separate record.
59.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED (could not refute). I retrieved the isoniazid label myself and it does separate the two populations exactly as claimed. For treatment of tuberculosis: adults '5 mg/kg up to 300 mg daily in a single dose', children '10 - 15 mg/kg up to 300 mg daily in a single dose'. For preventive therapy: infants and children '10 mg/kg (up to 300 mg daily) in a single dose', adults over 30 kg '300 mg per day in a single dose'. CDC and AAP independently corroborate 10-15 mg/kg daily for children. The stored flat perKg 5 mg/kg q24h therefore applies the adult figure to every patient: a 20 kg child is shown 100 mg/day against a labelled 200-300 mg/day, and a 10 kg toddler 50 mg against 100-150 mg, a 2-3x under-dose. The adult default itself (5 mg/kg, max 300 mg once daily) is correct and there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error, so the claim is precisely scoped rather than overreaching. I also verified the two missing safety items in the label text: 'Concomitant administration of pyridoxine (B6) is recommended in malnourished and in those predisposed to neuropathy (e.g., alcoholics and diabetics)', and the boxed warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatitis with monthly liver-enzyme monitoring advised in patients 35 and older, while the record has flag=false. Verdict MISMATCH, severity high: sub-therapeutic isoniazid causes treatment failure and selects INH-resistant M. tuberculosis, a delayed but serious harm that a clinician is unlikely to catch because 5 mg/kg looks like the textbook isoniazid number. Suggested fix: ageAdj-split dosing, 10 mg/kg q24h for children (paediatric range 10-15 mg/kg) and 5 mg/kg q24h for adults, maxSingle 300 mg and maxDaily 300 mg for both; set flag=true with a hepatotoxicity/LFT-monitoring note and a pyridoxine co-administration prompt.
59.fix: 5 (kg başına), q24h, tek doz tavanı 300, günlük tavan 300; 2 yaş bandı. Kaynak: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9c34d487-693b-43e3-803e-45d87425e3d6&type=display (kaynaktan türetildi, bağımsız kontrolden geçti)

60.name: Ethambutol
60.stored: perKg 15 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 1600 mg, maxDaily 1600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 15 mg/kg/day, clamped at 1600 mg.
60.source: FDA label, MYAMBUTOL (ethambutol hydrochloride) tablets, DailyMed (dose confirmed against StatPearls for the renal interval)
60.note: The default dose matches the label: 'administer MYAMBUTOL 15 mg/kg (7 mg/lb) of body weight, as a single oral dose once every 24 hours' for initial treatment (retreatment is 25 mg/kg daily, reduced to 15 mg/kg after 60 days). Because freq is q24h, maxSingle = maxDaily = 1600 is internally consistent, and 1600 mg is the ATS/CDC weight-band daily dose for 76-90 kg, so the cap is a sensible ceiling rather than an arbitrary one; it only starts to bite above ~107 kg, where ATS bands would allow more, so this is at most a marginal under-dose in very heavy adults, not a CAP_UNDERDOSES defect. The low severity is for two encoded omissions rather than the number: (1) renalAdj is empty although ethambutol is renally cleared and the label states 'patients with decreased renal function need the dosage reduced as determined by serum levels of MYAMBUTOL' - StatPearls (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559050/) specifies that for CrCl below 30 mL/min or haemodialysis the drug should be given three times a week instead of daily; accumulation over a months-long course is what causes dose-dependent optic neuritis; (2) the US label says it 'is not recommended for use in pediatric patients under thirteen years of age since safe conditions for use have not been established', whereas ATS/WHO do use 15-25 mg/kg (20 mg/kg typical) in children - the record has no ageAdj either way, so the app silently gives 15 mg/kg to a 2-year-old with no note that this is outside the US label.
60.suggestedFix: Keep perKg 15 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 1600, maxDaily 1600. Add renalAdj covering CrCl <30 (dose given three times weekly rather than daily - if the model cannot express an interval change, set a factor of ~0.43 with an explicit warning, or flag the record). Add a visual-acuity/colour-vision monitoring flag (set flag=true) and an age note that use under 13 years is outside the US label though ATS/WHO use 15-25 mg/kg. Retreatment at 25 mg/kg belongs in a separate record.

42.name: Cefuroxime
42.stored: perKg 25 mg/kg q8h = 75 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 1500 mg; maxDaily 3000 mg; no ageAdj/renalAdj
42.source: FDA label, Cefuroxime for Injection USP (DailyMed)
42.note: The per-kg rule itself is correct and shows no daily/per-dose confusion: 25 mg/kg q8h = 75 mg/kg/day, squarely inside the labelled paediatric range 'above 3 months of age... 50 to 100 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses every 6 to 8 hours'. The defect is in the ceilings, which are internally contradictory: maxSingle 1500 x 3 doses = 4500 mg/day, but maxDaily is set to 3000 mg. The label's adult regimen is 750 mg q8h (2.25 g/day) for uncomplicated and '1.5 gram dose every 8 hours' (4.5 g/day) for severe/complicated and for bone and joint infections; up to 6 g/day q6h for life-threatening infection and 'not exceed 3 grams every 8 hours' (9 g/day) for meningitis. So a 70 kg adult (25 x 70 = 1750 mg, clamped to 1500 mg q8h) produces the labelled severe-infection regimen of 4.5 g/day, which the 3000 mg maxDaily then clamps or flags as an overdose. Even a 40 kg adolescent at 1000 mg q8h hits exactly 3000 mg and trips the warning. Net effect is a spurious warning and, if maxDaily clamps, an adult under-dosed at 3 g/day when 4.5 g/day is labelled. Secondary gaps: the label gives no paediatric dosing below 3 months, and cefuroxime is renally cleared (label reduces to 750 mg q12h at CrCl 10-20 and 750 mg q24h at CrCl <10) while renalAdj is empty.
42.suggestedFix: Keep kind=perKg, dose 25 mg/kg, freq q8h (75 mg/kg/day). Raise maxDaily to 4500 mg so it is consistent with maxSingle 1500 mg x 3; keep maxSingle 1500 mg. Optionally allow 6000 mg/day for life-threatening infection. Add ageAdj for neonates/<3 months (label gives no paediatric dose there) and renalAdj approximating the label: CrCl 10-20 -> effective daily factor ~0.67 (same 750-1500 mg unit dose q12h), CrCl <10 -> ~0.33 (unit dose q24h).
42.refuteReason: REFUTED. The claim concedes the per-kg rule is correct, and I confirm it: the label states 'Administration of 50 to 100 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses every 6 to 8 hours has been successful for most infections' for patients above 3 months, and the stored 25 mg/kg q8h = 75 mg/kg/day sits mid-range. The claim's entire harm mechanism is the conditional 'if maxDaily clamps, an adult under-dosed at 3 g/day'. I tested that against the engine rather than assuming it: in /Users/erdemgokmuharremoglu/Desktop/dozzzzz/DosageCalculator/src/features/dosage/calculations.ts (lines 618-629) maxDailyDose NEVER clamps — exceeding it only sets exceedsDailyMax and pushes a 'safety.exceedsDailyMax' warning, while the displayed dose stays capped only by maxSingleDose (lines 560-571). So a 70 kg adult is shown 1500 mg q8h, which is precisely the label's severe/complicated and bone-and-joint regimen, and is inside the label's stated envelope: 'The usual adult dosage range for Cefuroxime for Injection is 750 mg to 1.5 grams every 8 hours, usually for 5 to 10 days.' No adult is ever under-dosed, and no output falls outside the label — CAP_UNDERDOSES is not established. Even the hypothetical clamped value the claim fears (1 g q8h = 3 g/day) lies inside that same 750 mg-1.5 g q8h range. The 4.5 g/day the claim treats as mandatory is the severe-infection regimen, which by this review's own rule must not be the default. Residual, real but NOT supporting the claimed verdict: above ~60 kg the record fires a false-positive CRITICAL alert on a correctly labelled dose (alarm fatigue) — raising maxDaily to 6000 mg (label: 1.5 g q6h for life-threatening) would fix it; and the empty renalAdj (label: 750 mg q12h at CrCl 10-20, 750 mg q24h at CrCl <10) plus missing <3-month gate ('Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients below 3 months of age have not been established') are genuine separate omissions worth filing on their own.

43.name: Cefazolin
43.stored: perKg 25 mg/kg q8h = 75 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 2000 mg; maxDaily 6000 mg; no ageAdj/renalAdj
43.source: FDA label, Cefazolin for Injection USP (DailyMed)
43.note: Daily-total check passes: 25 mg/kg x 3 = 75 mg/kg/day, inside the label's overall paediatric envelope of 25-100 mg/kg/day. This one superficially looks like the recurring per-dose/per-day confusion (the label's figure '25 to 50 mg per kg... of body weight, divided into 3 or 4 equal doses' uses the same number 25), but 25 mg/kg per dose q8h is a genuine, widely used paediatric cefazolin dose, so I am not calling it an error. Two calibration caveats worth recording. (1) 75 mg/kg/day sits above the label's stated default band for 'most mild to moderately severe infections' (25-50 mg/kg/day) and three-quarters of the way to the severe-infection figure ('total daily dosage may be increased to 100 mg per kg of body weight for severe infections'). (2) On the adult side the per-kg rule over-shoots the fixed adult table: a 70 kg adult gets 1750 mg q8h = 5.25 g/day, whereas the labelled adult doses are 250-500 mg q8h (mild), 500 mg-1 g q6-8h (moderate to severe), and 1-1.5 g q6h (4-6 g/day) only for 'severe, life-threatening infections (e.g., endocarditis, septicemia)'. So the app's default hands an average adult the endocarditis-level dose. Cefazolin has a wide therapeutic margin and maxDaily 6000 mg matches the commonly cited 6 g/day ceiling (the label notes up to 12 g/day has rarely been used), so this is a calibration issue rather than a safety one. Gaps: label says safety in premature infants and neonates is not established, and cefazolin needs renal dose reduction; both ageAdj and renalAdj are empty.
43.suggestedFix: Acceptable as stored. If the app's default is meant to be mild-to-moderate infection, lower to ~16.7 mg/kg q8h (50 mg/kg/day) and offer 33 mg/kg q8h (100 mg/kg/day) as the severe-infection option; keep maxSingle 2000 mg and maxDaily 6000 mg. Add ageAdj marking premature infants/neonates as not established, and renalAdj for reduced clearance (roughly: CrCl 35-54 full dose at q8h minimum interval; CrCl 11-34 factor 0.5; CrCl <=10 factor 0.5 given q18-24h).

44.name: Cefoxitin
44.stored: perKg 40 mg/kg q6h = 160 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 2000 mg; maxDaily 12000 mg; no ageAdj/renalAdj
44.source: FDA label, Cefoxitin for Injection USP (DailyMed)
44.note: Daily-total check passes and there is no per-dose/per-day inversion here: 40 mg/kg x 4 = 160 mg/kg/day, which is the top of the labelled paediatric range, 'the recommended dosage in pediatric patients three months of age and older is 80 to 160 mg/kg of body weight per day divided into four to six equal doses'. 47.stored: perKg 5 mg/kg q12h = 10 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 400 mg; maxDaily 800 mg; ageAdj empty; renalAdj empty
