The dose required to maintain stable concentrations is 1.9 mg/kg/24 h'. That is the 1.9 mg/kg/24 h figure the claim cited, and it is roughly 24x below the 45 mg/kg/day the stored rule computes - so a record with renalAdj empty and flag=false genuinely shows an anuric patient the same dose as a patient with normal renal function, for a drug whose label makes adjustment mandatory and monitoring routine. The label's other stated doses also confirm the claim's framing: adults 'The usual daily intravenous dose is 2 g divided either as 500 mg every six hours or 1 g every 12 hours', paediatric patients '10 mg/kg per dose given every six hours' with 'Close monitoring of serum concentrations of vancomycin is recommended', and a separate neonatal regimen (15 mg/kg initial, then 10 mg/kg q12h in week 1 and q8h to 1 month) that the record ignores. The claim is fair in conceding the per-dose 15 mg/kg is itself reasonable (the 2020 ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP consensus supports 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h in adults targeting AUC24 400-600), so the defect is the model, not the number - which is exactly what MODEL_WRONG denotes. maxSingle 1000 mg also truncates a 100 kg adult below the 1500-2000 mg that 15-20 mg/kg implies. suggestedFix: do not express vancomycin as a single dose x frequency. Store 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h as an initial/loading estimate only, maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 4500 mg (label's anephric maintenance 1.9 mg/kg/24 h as a floor case), set flag=true with mandatory serum-level/AUC monitoring text, add renalAdj scaled to the Moellering table (daily mg ~= 15 x CrCL), and add a separate neonatal rule (<1 month: 15 mg/kg initial then 10 mg/kg q12h week 1, q8h thereafter).
22.blockNote: Vankomisin dozu her hastada böbrek fonksiyonuna ve ölçülen serum vankomisin düzeyine göre ayarlanmalıdır; yenidoğanlarda ayrıca yükleme dozu ve doğum sonrası yaşa göre değişen doz aralığı gerekir. Serum düzeyi takibiyle belirlenen bu dozlama sabit bir doz kuralıyla gösterilemediği için doz hesaplanmıyor.

24.name: Levofloxacin
24.stored: perKg 10 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 750 mg, maxDaily 750 mg, ageAdj [0,18,0] (contraindicated under 18), no renal adjustment
24.source: FDA prescribing information, levofloxacin tablets (DailyMed), section 2 Dosage and Administration, Table 1 (adults, CLCR at least 50 mL/min), Table 2 (paediatric patients 30 kg or greater) and Table 3 (renal impairment)
24.note: Levofloxacin has no weight-based adult dosing anywhere in the label - Table 1 is entirely fixed and indication-dependent: 250 mg q24h (uncomplicated UTI, 10-day complicated UTI), 500 mg q24h (CAP 7-14 day, uncomplicated skin, prostatitis, ABECB, sinusitis) or 750 mg q24h (nosocomial pneumonia, complicated skin, 5-day CAP, 5-day complicated UTI). The stored 10 mg/kg figure appears in no label table; the only paediatric dosing is anthrax/plague at 8 mg/kg q12h capped at 250 mg per dose (or 250 mg q12h for 30 to under 50 kg, 500 mg q24h at 50 kg or more). Consequences of the wrong model: a 45 kg adult is shown 450 mg, below the 500 mg minimum for CAP or skin infection and well below the 750 mg nosocomial-pneumonia dose - fluoroquinolone under-dosing risks treatment failure and resistance selection; and intermediate results such as 600 mg or 720 mg are not dispensable, since tablets exist only as 250, 500 and 750 mg. renalAdj is also empty although Table 3 requires major changes below CLCR 50 (750 mg q24h becomes 750 mg q48h at CLCR 20-49; 500 mg q24h becomes 500 mg once then 250 mg q24h), and accumulation drives tendon, CNS and QT toxicity. Separately the ageAdj [0,18,0] blanket contraindication is over-broad - the label does permit paediatric use for inhalational anthrax post-exposure and plague from 6 months of age - though that direction is at least fail-safe.
24.suggestedFix: Change kind to fixed. Default 500 mg q24h, maxSingle 750, maxDaily 750, with selectable indication presets 250 / 500 / 750 mg q24h per label Table 1. renalAdj per Table 3: CLCR 20-49 factor 0.5 (or interval to q48h for the 750 mg regimen), CLCR 10-19 factor 0.33, haemodialysis/CAPD factor 0.33. Replace the blanket under-18 zero factor with: permitted from 6 months for anthrax/plague only at 8 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 250 mg (fixed 500 mg q24h at 50 kg or more), and a warning flag for all other paediatric use rather than a hard contraindication.
24.refuteReason: Could not refute. I extracted LEVAQUIN's FDA label (Reference ID 4053557, rev. 2/2017) and section 2.1 states 'The usual dose of LEVAQUIN Tablets or Oral Solution is 250 mg, 500 mg, or 750 mg administered orally every 24 hours, as indicated by infection and described in Table 1' - entirely fixed, entirely indication-driven, with no weight-based adult dosing anywhere. Table 1 verbatim: nosocomial pneumonia 750 mg; CAP 500 mg (7-14 d) or 750 mg (5 d); complicated SSSI 750 mg; uncomplicated SSSI 500 mg; chronic bacterial prostatitis 500 mg; cUTI/acute pyelonephritis 750 mg (5 d) or 250 mg (10 d); uncomplicated UTI 250 mg; ABECB 500 mg; acute bacterial sinusitis 750 mg (5 d) or 500 mg (10-14 d). The only mg/kg dosing in the whole label is Table 2, paediatric inhalational anthrax post-exposure and plague: patients <50 kg and >=6 months get '8 mg/kg (not to exceed 250 mg per dose)' every 12 hours, and >50 kg get 500 mg q24h. The stored 10 mg/kg q24h therefore corresponds to no labelled regimen at all, and the claim's consequence analysis is arithmetically right: a 45 kg adult is shown 450 mg, below the 500 mg minimum for CAP or uncomplicated SSSI and far below the 750 mg nosocomial-pneumonia dose, and intermediate outputs like 600 or 720 mg are not dispensable from the 250/500/750 mg tablet strengths. Section 2.3 confirms the missing renal rule: 'In patients with impaired renal function (creatinine clearance < 50 mL/min), adjustment of the dosage regimen is necessary to avoid the accumulation of levofloxacin due to decreased clearance', against an empty stored renalAdj, and the label carries a boxed warning for tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy and CNS effects. The claim's own caveat is also correct - the label permits paediatric use from 6 months for anthrax and plague, so ageAdj [0,18,0] is over-broad but errs safe. suggestedFix: convert to kind=fixed, indication-selected: 250 mg q24h (uncomplicated UTI, 10-day cUTI), 500 mg q24h (CAP 7-14 d, uncomplicated SSSI, prostatitis, ABECB, sinusitis 10-14 d), 750 mg q24h (nosocomial pneumonia, complicated SSSI, 5-day CAP, 5-day cUTI, sinusitis 5 d); maxSingle/maxDaily 750 mg; add renalAdj for CrCL <50 (750 mg -> q48h at CrCL 20-49; 500 mg -> 500 mg once then 250 mg q24h); replace the blanket under-18 block with a paediatric anthrax/plague rule of 8 mg/kg q12h capped at 250 mg per dose from 6 months.
24.blockNote: Levofloksasinin erişkin dozu enfeksiyon türüne göre 250, 500 veya 750 mg olarak seçilir ve böbrek yetmezliğinde ilk tam dozdan sonra azaltılmış doz ya da uzatılmış aralıkla sürdürülür; çocuklarda yalnızca şarbon ve veba için kiloya göre kullanılır. Bu rejim tek bir doz ve sıklık kuralıyla doğru ifade edilemediği için doz gösterilmiyor.

26.name: Amikacin
26.stored: perKg 15 mg/kg q24h (= 15 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 1500 mg, no renal adjustment, flag=false
26.source: FDA prescribing information, amikacin sulfate injection (DailyMed), Dosage and Administration
26.note: Daily-total check passes - this is the one record of the six where the mg/kg/day versus per-dose conflation is NOT present. The label states 15 mg/kg/day and the stored q24h rule produces exactly 15 mg/kg/day (the label divides it as 7.5 mg/kg q12h or 5 mg/kg q8h, while once-daily extended-interval administration is standard off-label practice; either way the daily total is correct). The defect is the ceiling: on a q24h schedule the single dose IS the daily dose, so maxSingle 1000 mg clamps every patient to 1000 mg/day even though maxDaily and the label both permit 1.5 g/day ("Treatment of patients in the heavier weight classes should not exceed 1.5 gram/day"). Anyone above roughly 67 kg is silently truncated - a 90 kg patient needs 1350 mg and is shown 1000 mg, 26% under. Amikacin efficacy is concentration-dependent (peak/MIC), so truncating the peak is a direct treatment-failure and resistance risk, and the two ceilings contradict each other. Secondary gaps: renalAdj is empty and flag is false although the label requires dose or interval adjustment in impaired renal function and says peaks above 35 mcg/mL and troughs above 10 mcg/mL should be avoided - untreated, that is the nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity pathway for this drug.
26.suggestedFix: Keep 15 mg/kg q24h (extended interval) but set maxSingle = 1500 to match maxDaily 1500, so the two ceilings agree; if the record is instead stored as the label's divided regimen, use 7.5 mg/kg q12h with maxSingle 750 and maxDaily 1500. Add renalAdj by CrCL (interval extension: CrCL 40-59 factor 0.67, CrCL 20-39 factor 0.5, CrCL under 20 - loading dose then level-guided only) and set flag=true requiring peak/trough monitoring (peak under 35 mcg/mL, trough under 10 mcg/mL) and a usual course of 7-10 days. Add the neonatal rule (10 mg/kg loading then 7.5 mg/kg q12h) and the uncomplicated-UTI rule (250 mg q12h).
26.refuteReason: Could not refute. The DailyMed amikacin sulfate injection label gives verbatim '15 mg/kg/day divided into 2 or 3 equal doses administered at equally-divided intervals, i.e., 7.5 mg/kg q12h or 5 mg/kg q8h' and 'Treatment of patients in the heavier weight classes should not exceed 1.5 gram/day'. The claim's central concession is right - this is the one record where the per-dose/per-day conflation is absent, since 15 mg/kg q24h does produce exactly the labelled 15 mg/kg/day - and its central objection is right too. On a q24h schedule the single dose IS the daily dose, so maxSingle 1000 mg binds before maxDaily 1500 mg ever can, and the two ceilings genuinely contradict each other: every patient above ~67 kg is silently clamped to 1000 mg/day even though the label permits 1.5 g/day. I checked the arithmetic in the claim and it holds: 90 kg x 15 mg/kg = 1350 mg, shown as 1000 mg, 26% under. Note this cap would never bind on the label's own divided schedule (90 kg at 7.5 mg/kg q12h = 675 mg per dose), which is precisely why storing the daily dose on a q24h frequency while keeping a per-dose ceiling is the defect. Amikacin is concentration-dependent (peak/MIC), so truncating the peak is a real treatment-failure and resistance risk rather than a cosmetic one. The secondary gaps are confirmed by the same label: it directs dose or interval adjustment in impaired renal function (e.g. with serum creatinine 2 mg/100 mL the 7.5 mg/kg dose is given every 18 hours) and states 'Peak concentrations (30 to 90 minutes after injection) above 35 micrograms per mL and trough concentrations (just prior to the next dose) above 10 micrograms per mL should be avoided', while renalAdj is empty and flag=false. suggestedFix: keep perKg 15 mg/kg q24h but raise maxSingle to 1500 mg so it matches maxDaily 1500 mg (or store the label's divided regimen, 7.5 mg/kg q12h with maxSingle 750 mg and maxDaily 1500 mg); add renalAdj by CrCL with interval extension; set flag=true requiring peak/trough monitoring (avoid peak >35 mcg/mL, trough >10 mcg/mL) and note the separate neonatal loading dose of 10 mg/kg then 7.5 mg/kg q12h.
26.blockNote: Amikasin dozu serum pik ve dip düzeylerine göre ayarlanır; yenidoğanda ve böbrek yetmezliğinde önce yükleme dozu verilir, idame dozu kreatinin klerensiyle orantılı olarak azaltılır. Tek doz ve sıklık modeli bu rejimi karşılamadığı için doz gösterilmiyor.

27.name: Azithromycin
27.stored: fixed 500 mg q24h, maxSingle 500 mg, maxDaily 500 mg, no ageAdj, no weight-based rule
27.source: FDA prescribing information, ZITHROMAX (azithromycin) tablets and oral suspension (DailyMed), Dosage and Administration - adult and paediatric dosage tables
27.note: In a calculator that serves paediatric patients, kind=fixed with no ageAdj and no weight rule means a 10 kg toddler is shown the full adult 500 mg - that is 50 mg/kg, about 5x the labelled paediatric dose of 10 mg/kg once daily, and above the 30 mg/kg single-dose maximum used for acute otitis media; an infant or neonate would be shown the same 500 mg, an even larger multiple. The label's paediatric dosing is entirely weight-based from 6 months of age: CAP 10 mg/kg on Day 1 then 5 mg/kg on Days 2-5; acute otitis media 30 mg/kg as a single dose, or 10 mg/kg once daily for 3 days, or 10 mg/kg Day 1 then 5 mg/kg Days 2-5; pharyngitis/tonsillitis (2 years and over) 12 mg/kg once daily for 5 days. The adult side is also not expressible as one dose x frequency: the commonest adult regimen is a 500 mg loading dose on Day 1 followed by 250 mg once daily on Days 2-5 (CAP, pharyngitis, skin), with 500 mg q24h for 3 days applying only to ABECB and sinusitis, and single 1 g or 2 g doses for genital infections. The stored 500 mg q24h is therefore defensible only as the adult 3-day regimen and is wrong as a universal default. Rated high because the error is systematic across the whole paediatric weight range (5x at 10 kg and worse below that) for a drug with QT-prolongation and hepatotoxicity liability, even though azithromycin's therapeutic margin makes a single excess dose unlikely to be fatal.
27.suggestedFix: Split into weight-banded rules. Paediatric (6 months and over, under about 45 kg): perKg 10 mg/kg q24h Day 1 with maxSingle 500 mg, then 5 mg/kg q24h Days 2-5 with maxSingle 250 mg; alternative AOM preset 30 mg/kg single dose (maxSingle 1500 mg) or 10 mg/kg q24h x 3 days; pharyngitis preset (2 years and over) 12 mg/kg q24h x 5 days, maxSingle 500 mg. Adults/adolescents: fixed 500 mg q24h x 3 days (maxSingle 500, maxDaily 500) as the default, plus presets for 500 mg Day 1 then 250 mg q24h Days 2-5, and 1 g single dose for chlamydial urethritis/cervicitis. Add ageAdj flagging under 6 months as not established, and set flag=true noting QT prolongation risk and that the regimen is a loading dose followed by a lower maintenance dose, not a flat daily dose.
27.refuteReason: Could not refute. I extracted the ZITHROMAX FDA label (Reference ID 4891781) and both halves of the claim are confirmed verbatim. Section 2.2 paediatric dosing is entirely weight-based: acute otitis media '30 mg/kg as a single dose or 10 mg/kg once daily for 3 days or 10 mg/kg as a single dose on Day 1 followed by 5 mg/kg/day on Days 2 through 5'; acute bacterial sinusitis '10 mg/kg once daily for 3 days'; community-acquired pneumonia '10 mg/kg as a single dose on Day 1 followed by 5 mg/kg once daily on Days 2 through 5'; pharyngitis/tonsillitis '12 mg/kg once daily for 5 days' (age 2 years and above; the other indications are 6 months and above). The label's own weight tables put a 10 kg child at 300 mg total for a whole 5-day OM/CAP course and at 300 mg for the single-dose 30 mg/kg OM regimen - so the stored fixed 500 mg exceeds even the highest single paediatric dose the label evaluates at that weight, and at 10 kg it is 50 mg/kg against a labelled 10 mg/kg first dose, the 5x the claim states. Section 2.1 confirms the adult side is not one-dose-x-frequency either: CAP, second-line pharyngitis/tonsillitis and uncomplicated skin/skin structure are '500 mg as a single dose on Day 1, followed by 250 mg once daily on Days 2 through 5'; only acute bacterial sinusitis and ABECB use '500 mg once daily for 3 days'; and genital indications are single 1 g or 2 g doses. So kind=fixed 500 mg q24h is defensible only as the adult 3-day sinusitis/ABECB regimen and is wrong as a universal default in a calculator that serves children, which has no ageAdj and no weight rule to stop it. MODEL_WRONG is the correct verdict, since a Day-1-loading-then-halved-maintenance schedule cannot be expressed as one dose x frequency. The claim's own hedge on severity (azithromycin's margin makes a single excess dose unlikely to be fatal, but the error is systematic across the whole paediatric weight range) is a reasonable judgement, not a factual defect. suggestedFix: split into indication-specific records rather than one fixed dose. Paediatric (>=6 months): perKg 10 mg/kg q24h Day 1 then 5 mg/kg q24h Days 2-5 for CAP/OM, or 10 mg/kg q24h x3 days for OM/sinusitis, or 30 mg/kg single dose for OM; pharyngitis/tonsillitis (>=2 years) 12 mg/kg q24h x5 days, maxSingle 500 mg for the multi-day regimens and 1500 mg for the 30 mg/kg single dose. Adult: 500 mg Day 1 then 250 mg Days 2-5 (CAP, pharyngitis, skin) or 500 mg q24h x3 days (ABECB, sinusitis); separate 1 g and 2 g single-dose entries for genital infections. Add ageAdj so no fixed adult dose is ever shown to a child.
27.blockNote: Azitromisin endikasyona göre farklı kürlerle verilir: çoğu enfeksiyonda ilk gün yüksek doz, sonraki 4 gün yarım doz (erişkinde 500 mg sonra 250 mg, çocukta 10 mg/kg sonra 5 mg/kg), bazı enfeksiyonlarda ise 3 günlük ya da tek seferlik doz uygulanır. Yükleme dozu ve kür süresi sabit bir günlük doz kuralıyla gösterilemediği için doz hesaplanmıyor.

28.name: Clarithromycin
28.stored: perKg 7.5 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 500 mg, maxDaily 1000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
28.source: FDA label (DailyMed) - clarithromycin for oral suspension / tablets
28.note: Daily-total check passes: 7.5 mg/kg x 2 doses/day = 15 mg/kg/day, which is exactly the labelled paediatric regimen ('15 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours for 10 days', up to the adult dose). The MAC regimen is separately stated as '7.5 mg/kg up to 500 mg every 12 hours', so the per-dose number, the q12h frequency and the 500 mg single-dose ceiling all agree with the label. maxDaily 1000 mg equals the maximum labelled adult regimen (500 mg q12h); a 70 kg adult computes 525 mg and is correctly clamped to 500 mg q12h. The dose rule itself is correct - the only gap is the missing renal rule: the same label directs that for CLcr <30 mL/min the dose be reduced by 50% (and by 75% with concomitant atazanavir/ritonavir). No contraindication/age flag is needed for the default paediatric indication. Severity is low because the number shown is right; only the renal edge case is unhandled.
28.suggestedFix: Keep perKg 7.5 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 500, maxDaily 1000. Add renalAdj [[0,30,0.5]] (50% dose reduction for CrCl <30 mL/min per the FDA label). Optionally add a note that the 75% reduction applies with concomitant atazanavir or ritonavir.

29.name: Doxycycline
29.stored: fixed 100 mg q12h, maxSingle 100 mg, maxDaily 200 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
29.note: kind=fixed makes the engine give 100 mg q12h to a patient of ANY weight, but the label dosesnchildren by weight: 'Pediatric patients weighing less than 45 kg... 2.2 mg per kg of body weight administered every 12 hours' (severe/life-threatening), and '4.4 mg/kg divided into two doses on the first day... followed by a maintenance dose of 2.2 mg/kg' for less severe disease; only 'pediatric patients weighing 45 kg or more should receive the adult dose'. A 15 kg child should get 33 mg q12h - this record shows 100 mg q12h, a 3x per-dose overdose; a 25 kg child gets ~1.8x. The adult arm is defensible but sits at the top of the label: the usual adult regimen is '200 mg on the first day of treatment (administered 100 mg every 12 hours) followed by a maintenance dose of 100 mg daily', with 100 mg q12h reserved for 'more severe infections'. There is also no age rule for the labelled caution: 'Use doxycycline hyclate in pediatric patients 8 years of age or less only when the potential benefits are expected to outweigh the risks in severe or life-threatening conditions.' Daily-total check: 100 x 2 = 200 mg/day, which matches the label's day-1 total but is twice the usual adult maintenance.
29.suggestedFix: Change kind to perKg: dose 2.2 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 100 mg, maxDaily 200 mg (the cap automatically delivers the adult 100 mg q12h at >=45 kg, matching the label's 45 kg switchover). Add ageAdj entry flagging <=8 years as caution/benefit-risk only (e.g. [0,8,1] with a warning, not factor 0, since doxycycline is still first-line for RMSF at any age). Note in the record that day 1 is a doubled loading total (4.4 mg/kg or 200 mg) and that usual maintenance for less severe adult infection is 100 mg once daily.
29.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED — I could not refute it. I retrieved the doxycycline hyclate FDA label myself and it dose children by weight, exactly as claimed: for all paediatric patients weighing less than 45 kg with severe or life-threatening infections the dose is '2.2 mg per kg of body weight administered every 12 hours'; for less severe disease '4.4 mg per kg of body weight divided into two doses on the first day' followed by 'a maintenance dose of 2.2 mg per kg of body weight'; only patients 45 kg or more receive the adult dose. The record is kind=fixed 100 mg with maxSingle 100, so it can never scale down: a 15 kg child is shown 100 mg q12h against a labelled 33 mg (6.7 vs 2.2 mg/kg = 3.0x per dose); a 25 kg child 100 mg vs 55 mg (1.8x). Daily-total check: 100 x 2 = 200 mg/day, which equals the label's day-1 total ('200 mg on the first day') but is twice the usual adult maintenance, since the label continues 'a maintenance dose of 100 mg daily' and reserves '100 mg every 12 hours' for severe infections, particularly chronic urinary tract infections. The label's paediatric caution is also present and unrepresented in the record ('Use doxycycline hyclate in pediatric patients 8 years of age or less only when the potential benefits are expected to outweigh the risks in severe or life-threatening conditions'), and ageAdj is empty. Every factual element of the claim checked out against the primary label; nothing in it misread per-dose vs per-day. Suggested fix: kind=perKg 2.2 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 100 mg, maxDaily 200 mg, with the day-1 load expressed as 4.4 mg/kg/day divided q12h; adults >=45 kg 100 mg q12h day 1 then 100 mg q24h maintenance (100 mg q12h only for severe infection); ageAdj warn/justify for age <=8 years.
29.fixRejected: REJECT, so the record stays blocked. I checked two FDA labels with the same dosing text: Pfizer Vibramycin/Vibra-Tabs (accessdata.fda.gov, rev 08/2025) and the Lupin doxycycline hyclate tablets label on DailyMed (the one cited, now showing rev 9/2025, not 4/2025). The proposer quotes them accurately. WHAT THE LABEL SAYS: - Adults: 'The usual dose of oral doxycycline is 200 mg on the first day of treatment (administered 100 mg every 12 hours) followed by a maintenance dose of 100 mg/day.' 100 mg every 12 hours is for 'more severe infections'. - Children under 45 kg: 2.2 mg/kg every 12 hours is limited to 'severe or life-threatening infections (e.g., anthrax, Rocky Mountain spotted fever)'. -
29.blockNote: Doksisiklin dozu enfeksiyonun ağırlığına göre değişir: olağan şemada ilk gün 200 mg, sonra günde 100 mg; ağır enfeksiyonlarda 12 saatte bir 100 mg. 8 yaş ve altında yalnızca ağır veya hayatı tehdit eden durumlarda kullanılır. Uygulama enfeksiyonun ağırlığını ve yükleme dozunu ifade edemediği için doz gösterilmemektedir.

30.name: Clindamycin
30.stored: perKg 10 mg/kg q6h, maxSingle 900 mg, maxDaily 2700 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
30.source: FDA label - Cleocin Phosphate injection (Pfizer) and Cleocin HCl capsules (DailyMed)
30.note: Daily-total check: 10 mg/kg x 4 doses/day = 40 mg/kg/day. That is the absolute ceiling of the parenteral paediatric range ('20 to 40 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses', the top reserved for more severe infections - https://www.pfizermedical.com/cleocin-phosphate-injection/dosage-admin) and it is 60% ABOVE the entire oral paediatric range: the oral capsule label gives 8-16 mg/kg/day (serious) and 16-20 mg/kg/day (more severe), and the paediatric oral solution label tops out at '17 to 25 mg/kg/day... divided into 3 or 4 equal doses'. Since the record carries no route, the default shown will overdose every oral course. The adult arm also breaks: a 70 kg adult computes 700 mg q6h = 2800 mg/day, which exceeds the labelled adult parenteral maximum of 2700 mg/day (4800 mg/day only 'in life-threatening situations') so the engine warns on a routine adult case, and it is more than 50% above the adult oral maximum of 450 mg q6h = 1800 mg/day ('Serious infections - 150 to 300 mg every 6 hours. More severe infections - 300 to 450 mg every 6 hours'). Clindamycin carries a boxed warning for C. difficile-associated colitis, so defaulting to the maximum is not a neutral choice.
30.suggestedFix: Set the default to the mid-range: perKg 7.5 mg/kg q6h (or 10 mg/kg q8h) = 30 mg/kg/day. Oral route: maxSingle 450 mg, maxDaily 1800 mg. IV route: maxSingle 900 mg, maxDaily 2700 mg. If the app cannot distinguish route, use the oral ceilings (450/1800) as the safe default and document 40 mg/kg/day + 2700 mg/day as the severe-IV-infection escalation rather than the default.
30.refuteReason: CLAIM REFUTED — the stored rule is defensible as a default. I retrieved the FDA Cleocin Phosphate (clindamycin injection) label directly: paediatric patients 1 month to 16 years get '20 to 40 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses'. Daily-total check: stored 10 mg/kg x 4 doses/day = 40 mg/kg/day, which is INSIDE that labelled range — at its top, but within it. The claim itself concedes this ('the absolute ceiling of the parenteral paediatric range'), and a value inside the labelled range is MATCHES, not MISMATCH, under the verdict definitions. This is not the recurring per-day-entered-as-per-dose error. I also checked it against an independent guideline rather than the label alone: the IDSA MRSA guideline recommends for hospitalized children 'clindamycin 10-13 mg/kg/dose IV every 6-8 h (to administer 40 mg/kg/day)' for complicated skin and soft tissue infection, pneumonia and bone/joint infection (https://academic.oup.com/cid/article/52/3/e18/306145) — the stored 10 mg/kg/dose is the BOTTOM of the mainstream per-dose range, so it is a standard regimen, not a life-threatening-infection-only extreme. The claim's strongest argument, the oral comparison (Cleocin HCl capsules 8-16 and 16-20 mg/kg/day; Cleocin Pediatric granules '8-12 mg/kg/day' and '17-25 mg/kg/day divided into 3 or 4 equal doses'), imports a route the record does not assert; the record's own ceilings are unambiguously parenteral (maxSingle 900 mg and maxDaily 2700 mg have no oral counterpart — oral tops out at 450 mg q6h = 1800 mg/day), and no record in this dataset carries a route field, so this is a schema gap, not a wrong stored number. The adult objection also fails: maxDaily 2700 is precisely the labelled adult parenteral maximum for more severe infections ('1200-2700 mg/day in 2, 3 or 4 equal doses', with 4800 mg/day only in life-threatening situations), so a 70 kg adult's 2800 mg/day extrapolation triggering a warn/clamp is the ceiling doing its job and steering back to the label, not the engine breaking. Residual, non-claim observations worth logging separately at low/moderate severity: the value sits at the ceiling of the paediatric band, so 7.5 mg/kg q6h (30 mg/kg/day, mid-range) would be a more conservative default; neonates <1 month are outside the stored rule ('15 to 20 mg/kg/day in 3 to 4 equal doses'; 5 mg/kg q8h at PMA <=32 weeks, 7 mg/kg q8h at >32 to <=40 weeks); and a route field plus surfacing the boxed C. difficile colitis warning would improve safety. None of that makes the stored default wrong.

32.name: Linezolid
32.stored: perKg 10 mg/kg q12h, maxSingle 600 mg, maxDaily 1200 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
32.source: FDA label (DailyMed) - ZYVOX (linezolid) injection, granules, tablets
32.note: This is the recurring error running in the opposite direction - a frequency that is too INFREQUENT for children. Daily-total check: 10 mg/kg x 2 = 20 mg/kg/day, but the label's dosing table gives paediatric patients birth through 11 years '10 mg/kg intravenously or oral every 8 hours' = 30 mg/kg/day for nosocomial pneumonia, community-acquired pneumonia, complicated skin and skin structure infections and vancomycin-resistant E. faecium infection. The stored q12h therefore under-doses every child under 12 by one third for exactly the serious MRSA/VRE indications linezolid is used for - a treatment-failure and resistance-selection risk, not a theoretical one. q12h is correct only for patients 12 years and older ('600 mg intravenously or oral every 12 hours'), for uncomplicated skin infection in 5-11 year olds ('10 mg/kg oral every 12 hours'), and as the starting regimen for pre-term neonates <7 days old, who must move to q8h by 7 days of life. The adult arm happens to come out right because maxSingle 600 / maxDaily 1200 clamp a 70 kg adult to the labelled 600 mg q12h.
32.suggestedFix: Make the rule age-dependent. <12 years: perKg 10 mg/kg q8h, maxSingle 600 mg, maxDaily 1800 mg (raise maxDaily or the engine will clamp a legitimate 30 mg/kg/day paediatric course). >=12 years and adults: fixed 600 mg q12h, maxDaily 1200 mg. Add ageAdj to encode the switchover at 12 years, plus a note that pre-term neonates <7 days start at 10 mg/kg q12h and advance to q8h by day 7, and that 5-11 year olds with UNcomplicated skin infection use 10 mg/kg q12h. No renal adjustment is required.
32.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED — I could not refute it. I retrieved the ZYVOX (linezolid) label's Table 1 myself. For nosocomial pneumonia, community-acquired pneumonia, complicated skin and skin structure infections and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium infection, paediatric patients birth through 11 years receive '10 mg/kg intravenously or oral every 8 hours', while patients 12 years and older receive '600 mg intravenously or oral every 12 hours'. Daily-total check: stored 10 mg/kg x 2 = 20 mg/kg/day against a labelled 30 mg/kg/day — the stored q12h under-doses every child under 12 by one third for precisely the serious MRSA/VRE indications linezolid is reserved for, a treatment-failure and resistance-selection risk. The claim's list of the genuine q12h exceptions also checks out: the label gives q12h for >=12 years, and for uncomplicated skin and skin structure infection it gives '10 mg/kg oral every 12 hours' for 5-11 year olds (but '10 mg/kg oral every 8 hours' for children under 5), plus the pre-term neonate <7 days starting regimen that moves to q8h. The adult arm is incidentally correct only because maxSingle 600 / maxDaily 1200 clamp a 70 kg adult (700 mg computed) down to the labelled 600 mg q12h. Nothing in the claim misread per-dose vs per-day; it is the same error running in the under-dosing direction. Suggested fix: ageAdj band age <12 years -> 10 mg/kg q8h with maxSingle 600 mg and maxDaily 1800 mg; age >=12 years -> fixed 600 mg q12h, maxDaily 1200 mg; optionally a separate uncomplicated-SSSI entry (5-11 years 10 mg/kg q12h, adults 400 mg q12h) and the pre-term neonate <7 days q12h start moving to q8h by day 7. No renal adjustment is required by the label.
32.blockNote: Linezolid doğumdan 11 yaşına kadar 8 saatte bir 10 mg/kg, 12 yaş ve üzerinde ise 12 saatte bir 600 mg verilir; doz aralığı yaşa göre değiştiği için tek bir kuralla doğru doz gösterilemiyor. Yedi günlükten küçük prematüre yenidoğanlarda başlangıç aralığı da farklıdır (12 saatte bir 10 mg/kg).

33.name: Daptomycin
33.stored: perKg 4 mg/kg q24h, maxSingle 600 mg, maxDaily 600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
33.note: 4 mg/kg q24h is the correct ADULT dose for complicated skin and skin structure infection ('4 mg/kg to adult patients intravenously... once every 24 hours for 7 to 14 days'), but it is below every paediatric band in the label, because children clear daptomycin faster and the labelled mg/kg rises as age falls. Paediatric cSSSI: 12-17 yr 5 mg/kg, 7-11 yr 7 mg/kg, 2-6 yr 9 mg/kg, 1 to <2 yr 10 mg/kg once every 24 hours. Paediatric S. aureus bacteraemia: 12-17 yr 7 mg/kg, 7-11 yr 9 mg/kg, 1-6 yr 12 mg/kg once every 24 hours. A 3-year-old with cSSSI is therefore shown 4 mg/kg instead of 9 mg/kg - a 55% under-dose in an MRSA infection. Adults with S. aureus bloodstream infection also need 6 mg/kg q24h, not 4. Two further gaps: renalAdj is empty although the label extends the interval for CrCl <30 mL/min including haemodialysis and CAPD ('4 mg/kg (cSSSI) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infections) once every 48 hours', given after dialysis on dialysis days) - at q24h these patients accumulate drug and risk rhabdomyolysis; and there is no age block although CUBICIN is not recommended below 1 year of age because of effects on muscular, neuromuscular and/or nervous systems seen in neonatal dogs. The 600 mg maxSingle/maxDaily is not label-derived (the label sets no fixed adult ceiling) and would truncate a large adolescent or a heavy adult once the dose is corrected upward. Daily-total check passes trivially (q24h), so the defect here is the per-kg value and the missing age/renal logic.
33.suggestedFix: Encode age bands for the default cSSSI indication: ageAdj 1-<2 yr 10 mg/kg, 2-6 yr 9 mg/kg, 7-11 yr 7 mg/kg, 12-17 yr 5 mg/kg, >=18 yr 4 mg/kg, all q24h; add a contraindication entry [0,1,0] for <1 year (not recommended). Add renalAdj for CrCl <30 mL/min (including HD/CAPD) as an interval extension to q48h, not a dose-fraction multiplier - a 0.5 factor at q24h is not equivalent. Record the S. aureus bacteraemia alternative (adult 6 mg/kg; 12-17 yr 7, 7-11 yr 9, 1-6 yr 12 mg/kg q24h). Remove or substantially raise the 600 mg cap so heavy adolescents/adults are not truncated.
33.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED — I could not refute it, with one fairness note. I retrieved the CUBICIN/daptomycin label tables myself. The stored 4 mg/kg q24h is a real labelled figure — 'Administer daptomycin for injection 4 mg/kg to adult patients intravenously ... once every 24 hours for 7 to 14 days' for complicated skin and skin structure infection — so the ADULT cSSSI arm is defensible and the claim slightly oversells by calling the whole record a mismatch. But with ageAdj empty the same number is handed to children, and every paediatric band in the label is higher: cSSSI 12-17 yr 5 mg/kg, 7-11 yr 7 mg/kg, 2-6 yr 9 mg/kg, 1-<2 yr 10 mg/kg once every 24 hours; S. aureus bacteraemia 12-17 yr 7 mg/kg, 7-11 yr 9 mg/kg, 1-6 yr 12 mg/kg once every 24 hours (adults 6 mg/kg q24h for bloodstream infection). A 3-year-old with cSSSI is therefore shown 4 mg/kg where the label says 9 mg/kg — a 56% under-dose in an MRSA infection, confirmed against the primary table, so the record really is wrong as a paediatric default. The two further gaps also verified: renalAdj is empty although the label directs '4 mg/kg (cSSSI) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infections) once every 48 hours' for CrCl <30 mL/min including haemodialysis and CAPD, given after the completion of haemodialysis on dialysis days — at q24h these patients accumulate drug (rhabdomyolysis/CPK risk); and there is no age block although the label says to avoid use in paediatric patients younger than 12 months because of potential effects on muscular, neuromuscular and/or nervous systems. Daily-total check passes trivially at q24h, so the defect is the per-kg value plus the missing age and renal logic, exactly as claimed. Suggested fix: ageAdj for cSSSI 1-<2 yr 10, 2-6 yr 9, 7-11 yr 7, 12-17 yr 5, adult 4 mg/kg q24h (separate bacteraemia entry 1-6 yr 12, 7-11 yr 9, 12-17 yr 7, adult 6 mg/kg q24h); ageAdj [0,1,0] to block under 12 months; renalAdj CrCl <30 -> interval q48h (factor 0.5 daily exposure), dosed post-dialysis; drop or substantially raise the 600 mg maxSingle/maxDaily, which is not label-derived and would truncate a heavy adolescent or adult once the mg/kg is corrected upward.
33.blockNote: Daptomisin dozu endikasyona göre değişir (erişkinde komplike deri ve yumuşak doku enfeksiyonunda 4 mg/kg, S. aureus bakteriyemisinde 6 mg/kg; çocukta yaşa ve endikasyona göre 5-12 mg/kg) ve kreatinin klirensi 30 mL/dk altında aynı doz 48 saatte bir verilir. Bu şema tek bir doz ve sıklık kuralıyla gösterilemediği için doz hesaplanmıyor; 1 yaşından küçük çocuklarda kullanılmamalıdır.

35.name: Tigecycline
35.stored: fixed 50 mg q12h, maxSingle 100 mg, maxDaily 100 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
35.source: FDA label - TYGACIL (tigecycline), Pfizer prescribing information
35.note: Tigecycline cannot be expressed as one dose x frequency: the label is a loading dose plus maintenance - 'The recommended dosage regimen for TYGACIL is an initial dose of 100 mg, followed by 50 mg every 12 hours.' The stored record drops the 100 mg load entirely, so day-1 exposure is about half the labelled exposure at the point when it matters most. The daily-total check on the maintenance arm passes (50 x 2 = 100 mg/day, matching the label), which is why this reads as correct at a glance. Two further defects: kind=fixed means an 8-11 year old is shown 50 mg q12h, but the label says 'Pediatric patients aged 8 to 11 years should receive 1.2 mg/kg of TYGACIL every 12 hours intravenously to a maximum dose of 50 mg' - a 25 kg child should get 30 mg, so the record over-doses by roughly 1.7x until the child reaches ~42 kg; 12-17 year olds do take the flat 50 mg q12h, and safety/efficacy below 8 years is not established. And there is no hepatic rule, although 'In patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child Pugh C), the initial dose of TYGACIL should be 100 mg followed by a reduced maintenance dose of 25 mg every 12 hours.' Tigecycline also carries a boxed warning for increased all-cause mortality and should be reserved for situations in which alternative treatments are not suitable - worth surfacing on the default screen. No renal adjustment is needed.
35.suggestedFix: Model as loading + maintenance: loading 100 mg IV once, then maintenance 50 mg q12h (maxSingle 50 mg after the load, maxDaily 100 mg). Paediatric: 8-11 years perKg 1.2 mg/kg q12h with maxSingle 50 mg; 12-17 years fixed 50 mg q12h; ageAdj [0,8,0] - not established below 8 years. Add a hepatic rule for Child-Pugh C: 100 mg load then 25 mg q12h (maxDaily 50 mg). Attach the boxed-warning note (increased all-cause mortality; reserve for when alternative treatments are unsuitable). No renalAdj.
35.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED — I could not refute it. I retrieved the TYGACIL (tigecycline) label on DailyMed myself. Section 2.1 gives 'Initial dose of 100 mg followed by 50 mg every 12 hours' — a loading dose plus maintenance, which a single dose x frequency record cannot express, so MODEL_WRONG is the right verdict. The stored record drops the 100 mg load entirely, roughly halving day-1 exposure at the point it matters most; the daily-total check on the maintenance arm passes (50 x 2 = 100 mg/day, matching the label), which is exactly why the record reads as correct at a glance. The paediatric objection also holds: section 2.3 says patients aged 8 to 11 years should receive '1.2 mg/kg of TYGACIL every 12 hours intravenously to a maximum dose of 50 mg every 12 hours', so kind=fixed over-doses a 25 kg child (50 mg shown vs 30 mg labelled, ~1.7x) and keeps over-dosing until roughly 42 kg; 12-17 year olds do take the flat 50 mg q12h, and use below 8 years is not established. The hepatic gap is real: 'Initial dose of 100 mg followed by a reduced maintenance dose of 25 mg every 12 hours' in severe hepatic impairment (Child Pugh C), with nothing in the record to represent it. The boxed warning is confirmed ('All-cause mortality was higher in patients treated with TYGACIL than comparators in a meta-analysis of clinical trials'), which makes a bare default screen with no reservation language a genuine safety gap. The one part of the claim I set out to overturn — 'No renal adjustment is needed' — also holds: the label states no dosage adjustment is necessary in renal impairment or haemodialysis, so the empty renalAdj is correct. Suggested fix: model as a loading dose of 100 mg once followed by 50 mg q12h maintenance (maxSingle 100 mg for the load, 50 mg for maintenance, maxDaily 100 mg); ages 8-11 perKg 1.2 mg/kg q12h capped at 50 mg per dose; block or flag age <8 years as not established; hepatic rule Child Pugh C -> 100 mg load then 25 mg q12h; surface the boxed all-cause-mortality warning and reserve-for-no-alternative language on the default screen; leave renalAdj empty.
35.blockNote: Tigesiklin erişkinde 100 mg yükleme dozunun ardından 12 saatte bir 50 mg olarak verilir, ağır karaciğer yetmezliğinde idame dozu 25 mg'a iner ve 18 yaş altında kullanımı önerilmez. Yükleme dozu ve karaciğer yetmezliği ayarı tek doz ve sıklık modeliyle ifade edilemediği için doz gösterilmiyor.

36.name: Ceftazidime
36.stored: perKg 50 mg/kg q8h (=150 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 6000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
36.source: FDA label, FORTAZ (ceftazidime for injection), Table 3 Recommended Dosage Schedule; Table 4 renal insufficiency
36.note: Daily-total check: 50 mg/kg x 3 = 150 mg/kg/day. The label's paediatric band is 30-50 mg/kg IV q8h (90-150 mg/kg/day) to a maximum of 6 g/day, with an explicit footnote: 'The higher dose should be reserved for immunocompromised pediatric patients or pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis or meningitis.' The record hard-codes the reserved top of the band as the default, so the app always shows the CF/meningitis/immunocompromised dose. The adult path is worse: the 2000 mg single cap makes every adult >=40 kg receive 2 g q8h = 6 g/day, which the label lists only for meningitis, serious gynaecological/intra-abdominal infection and 'very severe life-threatening infections, especially in immunocompromised patients'. The usual adult dose is 1 g IV/IM q8-12h (2-3 g/day), i.e. the record defaults to 2-3x the usual adult dose. Neonates 0-4 weeks are labelled 30 mg/kg q12h (60 mg/kg/day); with no ageAdj a neonate would be shown 150 mg/kg/day, 2.5x label. Separately, renalAdj is empty although the label mandates reduction at GFR <50 (1 g q12h at CrCl 31-50, 1 g q24h at 16-30, 500 mg q24h at 6-15, 500 mg q48h at <5) and warns that accumulation causes 'seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), encephalopathy, coma, asterixis, neuromuscular excitability, and myoclonia'. A CrCl-20 adult would be shown 6 g/day against a labelled 1 g/day - a 6-fold overdose.
36.suggestedFix: dose 30 mg/kg, freq q8h (90 mg/kg/day default, mild-moderate); maxSingle 1000 mg so adults default to 1 g q8h; maxDaily 6000 mg. ageAdj [0, 0.0767, 0.5] (neonate 0-4 weeks -> 30 mg/kg q12h; ideally a separate q12h neonatal rule). Add a severe/meningitis/CF toggle raising to 50 mg/kg q8h with maxSingle 2000. renalAdj required: [31,50,0.5], [16,30,0.25], [6,15,0.125], [0,5,0.0625] (label expresses these as interval extension, so prefer explicit CrCl-band regimens over a plain multiplier).
36.refuteReason: Could not refute — I extracted the FORTAZ label text myself and Table 3 confirms the claim. Adult: 'The usual adult dosage is 1 gram administered intravenously or intramuscularly every 8 to 12 hours' (2–3 g/day); 2 g q8h appears ONLY for meningitis, serious gynecological/intra-abdominal infection, and 'Very severe life-threatening infections, especially in immunocompromised patients'. The record's maxSingle 2000 forces exactly that 6 g/day regimen on every adult ≥40 kg, i.e. 2–3x the usual adult dose. Paediatric 1 month–12 years is '30 to 50 mg/kg intravenous to a maximum of 6 grams per day' q8h with footnote †: 'The higher dose should be reserved for immunocompromised pediatric patients or pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis or meningitis' — the stored 50 is that reserved ceiling as the default. Neonates (0–4 weeks) are '30 mg/kg intravenous every 12 hours' (60 mg/kg/day); with ageAdj empty a neonate is shown 150 mg/kg/day, 2.5x label. Table 4 confirms the renal bands verbatim (50–31: 1 g q12h; 30–16: 1 g q24h; 15–6: 500 mg q24h; <5: 500 mg q48h), and WARNINGS states 'Elevated levels of ceftazidime in patients with renal insufficiency can lead to seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), encephalopathy, coma, asterixis, neuromuscular excitability, and myoclonia'. One fair nuance: 50 mg/kg q8h is the top boundary of a labelled paediatric band, so the paediatric limb alone could be argued as 'within range'. But the adult default (2 g q8h = the life-threatening-infection regimen), the un-adjusted neonate, and the entirely absent renalAdj against a label-mandated table are each independently wrong, so the record is not defensible as shipped. Suggested fix: perKg 30 mg/kg q8h (90 mg/kg/day) as default, maxSingle 1000 mg / maxDaily 3000 mg for the usual adult regimen (allow an explicit severe-infection option at 50 mg/kg q8h, maxSingle 2000, maxDaily 6000); ageAdj [0, 0.077 yr, 0.6] with q12h for neonates 0–4 weeks (30 mg/kg q12h); renalAdj bands CrCl 31–50 → 1 g q12h, 16–30 → 1 g q24h, 6–15 → 500 mg q24h, <6 → 500 mg q48h.
36.blockNote: Seftazidimin idame dozu kreatinin klerensi 50 mL/dk altına indiğinde erişkinde sabit miktar ve uzatılmış aralıkla verilir (ör. 1 g 12 veya 24 saatte bir, 500 mg 24 veya 48 saatte bir); kiloya dayalı kural erişkin üst doz sınırıyla birlikte bu azaltmayı doğru hesaplayamıyor. Böbrek yetmezliğinde birikim nöbet ve ensefalopatiye yol açabildiği için doz gösterilmiyor.

37.name: Cefotaxime
37.stored: perKg 50 mg/kg q6h (=200 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 12000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
37.source: FDA label, CLAFORAN (cefotaxime for injection), DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Adults table and 'Neonates, Infants, and Children'
37.note: This is the recurring per-day-entered-as-per-dose error. Daily-total check: 50 mg/kg x 4 = 200 mg/kg/day. The label for infants and children 1 month to 12 years under 50 kg reads: 'the recommended daily dose is 50 to 180 mg/kg IM or IV body weight divided into four to six equal doses. The higher dosages should be used for more severe or serious infections, including meningitis.' 200 mg/kg/day therefore exceeds the labelled daily ceiling of 180 mg/kg/day outright, and the per-dose figure is also above the label maximum per dose (180/4 = 45 mg/kg q6h). 50 mg/kg per dose appears in the label only for neonates (q12h in week 1, q8h at 1-4 weeks, i.e. 100-150 mg/kg/day) - the number was lifted and a q6h frequency applied on top. The adult path also defaults high: the 2000 mg cap gives every adult >=40 kg 2 g q6h = 8 g/day, which the label assigns to 'infections commonly needing antibiotics in higher dosage (e.g., septicemia)'; usual moderate-to-severe adult dosing is 1-2 g q8h (3-6 g/day) and the absolute maximum is 12 g/day. renalAdj is empty although the label states the dose should be halved at estimated creatinine clearance below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2, and warns cephalosporins trigger seizures 'particularly in patients with renal impairment when the dosage was not reduced'.
37.suggestedFix: dose 50 mg/kg, freq q8h (150 mg/kg/day, within the 50-180 band); maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 12000 mg. Optional severe/meningitis setting 50 mg/kg q6h capped at the labelled 180 mg/kg/day for under-50 kg patients. For adults prefer maxSingle 1000-2000 with q8h so the default reads 1-2 g q8h rather than 8 g/day. ageAdj for neonates: 0-1 week 50 mg/kg q12h, 1-4 weeks 50 mg/kg q8h. renalAdj [0,19,0.5].
37.refuteReason: Could not refute — the CLAFORAN label text I extracted confirms the claim exactly, and this is the per-day-entered-as-per-dose error. 'Infants and Children (1 month to 12 years): For body weights less than 50 kg, the recommended daily dose is 50 to 180 mg/kg IM or IV body weight divided into four to six equal doses. The higher dosages should be used for more severe or serious infections, including meningitis.' Stored 50 mg/kg q6h = 200 mg/kg/day, which exceeds the labelled daily ceiling of 180 mg/kg/day outright; the implied per-dose maximum at q6h is 180/4 = 45 mg/kg, so 50 mg/kg is above the per-dose maximum too. The 50 mg/kg per-dose figure exists in the label only for neonates — '0-1 week of age 50 mg/kg per dose every 12 hours IV' and '1-4 weeks of age 50 mg/kg per dose every 8 hours IV' (100–150 mg/kg/day) — confirming the number was lifted from the neonatal row and a q6h frequency applied on top. Adult guideline table confirms moderate to severe = '1-2 grams every 8 hours' (3–6 g/day) while 2 g q6h (8 g/day) falls in 'Infections commonly needing antibiotics in higher dosage (e.g., septicemia) 6-8'; 'The maximum daily dosage should not exceed 12 grams' (so maxDaily 12000 is a correct absolute ceiling, but the default is wrong). Renal: 'it is suggested that... the dose of cefotaxime sodium be halved in patients with estimated creatinine clearances of less than 20 mL/min/1.73 m2', and the class labelling warns 'Several cephalosporins have been implicated in triggering seizures, particularly in patients with renal impairment when the dosage was not reduced.' Suggested fix: perKg 25 mg/kg q6h (100 mg/kg/day, mid-band default), maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 12000 mg with a soft warning above 180 mg/kg/day in children <50 kg; ageAdj for neonates — 50 mg/kg q12h birth to 1 week and 50 mg/kg q8h at 1–4 weeks; renalAdj factor 0.5 for CrCl <20.
37.fixRejected: REJECT. I checked the label myself: the FDA Claforan label (rev. 2/2015), with text pulled from the PDF, and a current DailyMed generic cefotaxime label (Rev. 05/2021), which says the same. Children 1 month to 12 years under 50 kg: 50-180 mg/kg/day split into 4-6 equal doses. Children 50 kg or more take the adult dose. Adults: uncomplicated 1 g q12h (2 g/day); moderate to severe 1-2 g q8h (3-6 g/day); septicaemia 2 g q6-8h (6-8 g/day); life-threatening 2 g q4h (up to 12 g/day); never more than 12 g/day. Neonates: 0-1 week 50 mg/kg q12h, 1-4 weeks 50 mg/kg q8h, with preterm and term dosed the same. Renal: the dose is halved at CrCl <20 mL/min/1.73 m2. Arithmetic, confirmed by running the rule
37.blockNote: Sefotaksim çocuklarda günlük dozun 4-6 eşit doza bölünmesiyle, erişkinlerde 8-12 saatte bir verilir ve doz enfeksiyonun ağırlığına göre günde 2-12 g arasında değişir. Tek bir doz ve sıklık bu şemaları karşılayamadığı için doz gösterilmemektedir.

38.name: Ceftazidime/Avibactam
38.stored: perKg 50 mg/kg q8h (=150 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 2500 mg, maxDaily 7500 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
38.source: FDA label, AVYCAZ (ceftazidime and avibactam) for injection, rev. 2/2025 - 2.1 Adults, Table 2 paediatric dosage, Tables 3 and 4 renal impairment
38.note: The 2500 mg single cap is the combination-product figure (AVYCAZ 2.5 g = ceftazidime 2 g + avibactam 0.5 g), so the record is denominated in combination mg - and on that basis 50 mg/kg is 20% below label. Table 2 gives, for 2 years to <18 years and for 6 months to <2 years, 'AVYCAZ 62.5 mg/kg to a maximum of 2.5 grams (ceftazidime 50 mg/kg and avibactam 12.5 mg/kg)' q8h. The stored 50 is the ceftazidime component only; the avibactam half was dropped. Every patient under ~50 kg is under-dosed by 20% (at 40 kg: 2000 mg stored vs 2500 mg labelled), and the cap is reached only at 50 kg instead of the labelled 40 kg. This is a last-line agent for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negatives, where a 20% shortfall in %fT>MIC risks failure and resistance selection. In the opposite direction, with no ageAdj the same 50 mg/kg is shown to infants: label is 50 mg/kg for 3 to <6 months, 37.5 mg/kg for >28 days to <3 months, and 25 mg/kg for neonates <=28 days with GA >=31 weeks - a 2x overdose in a neonate, against labelled CNS reactions (5.4). renalAdj is empty although Table 3/4 require reduction from eGFR/CrCl 50 downward, and Warning 5.1 flags decreased clinical response in cIAI at CrCl 30-50; the label also says there is insufficient information to dose renally impaired children under 2 years.
38.suggestedFix: dose 62.5 mg/kg (combination mg) q8h, maxSingle 2500 mg, maxDaily 7500 mg, with the unit label stated explicitly as combined ceftazidime+avibactam. ageAdj: [0.25,0.5,0.8] (3-<6 months -> 50 mg/kg), [0.077,0.25,0.6] (>28 days-<3 months -> 37.5 mg/kg), [0,0.077,0.4] (<=28 days -> 25 mg/kg). renalAdj [31,50,0.5] (31.25 mg/kg q8h, max 1.25 g), [16,30,0.38] and [6,15,0.38] and [0,5,0.38] at extended intervals q12h/q24h/q48h (23.75 mg/kg, max 0.94 g) - the interval changes cannot be expressed by a factor alone, so store them as explicit CrCl-band regimens. Infusion is over 2 hours.
38.refuteReason: Could not refute — I pulled Table 2 of the 2025 AVYCAZ label directly and it reads, for '2 years to less than 18 years': 'AVYCAZ 62.5 mg/kg to a maximum of 2.5 grams (ceftazidime 50 mg/kg and avibactam 12.5 mg/kg to a maximum dose of ceftazidime 2 grams and avibactam 0.5 grams)' every 8 hours, and the same 62.5 mg/kg for '6 months to less than 2 years'. Section 2.1 confirms the adult dose is 'AVYCAZ is 2.5 grams (ceftazidime 2 grams and avibactam 0.5 grams)... every 8 hours'. The record's maxSingle 2500 is therefore unambiguously the combination-product figure, and on that same basis the stored 50 mg/kg is 20% below the labelled 62.5 mg/kg — the claim's reading is correct, the stored 50 is the ceftazidime component with the avibactam half dropped. A 40 kg child gets 2000 mg stored against 2500 mg labelled, and the cap binds at 50 kg instead of 40 kg. The record is internally inconsistent either way: if 50 were meant as ceftazidime component, the cap would have to be 2000/6000, not 2500/7500. Downward age bands confirmed verbatim: '3 months to less than 6 months AVYCAZ 50 mg/kg (ceftazidime 40 mg/kg and avibactam 10 mg/kg)', 'Greater than 28 days to less than 3 months AVYCAZ 37.5 mg/kg', 'Less than or equal to 28 days with GA 31 weeks and older AVYCAZ 25 mg/kg' — so with ageAdj empty a term neonate is shown 2.5x the labelled dose. Warning 5.4 confirmed: 'Seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), encephalopathy, coma, asterixis, neuromuscular excitability, and myoclonia have been reported in patients treated with ceftazidime, particularly in the setting of renal impairment.' Warning 5.1 confirmed as 'Decreased Clinical Response in Adult cIAI Patients with Baseline CrCl of 30 to Less Than or Equal to 50 mL/min', and section 2.3 states 'There is insufficient information to recommend a dosing regimen for pediatric patients less than 2 years of age with renal impairment.' Suggested fix: perKg 62.5 mg/kg q8h on the combination basis, maxSingle 2500 mg, maxDaily 7500 mg; ageAdj 3–<6 months 50 mg/kg, >28 days–<3 months 37.5 mg/kg, ≤28 days (GA ≥31 wk) 25 mg/kg; renalAdj (age ≥2 yr / adult) eGFR 31–50 → 31.25 mg/kg (max 1.25 g) q8h, 16–30 → 23.75 mg/kg (max 0.94 g) q12h, 6–15 → q24h, ≤5 → q48h, with a block on renal dosing under 2 years.
38.blockNote: Seftazidim/avibaktamın dozu böbrek fonksiyonuna göre yalnızca miktar olarak değil doz aralığı olarak da değişir (kreatinin klirensi 30 mL/dk ve altında 0,94 g 12, 24 veya 48 saatte bir) ve yenidoğanlarda doğumdaki gebelik haftasına ve düzeltilmiş yaşa bağlıdır. 39.name: Cefiderocol
39.stored: perKg 50 mg/kg q8h, maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 6000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
39.source: FDA label, FETROJA (cefiderocol) for injection, current DailyMed version rev. March 2026 - 2.1 Recommended Dosage, 2.2 renal adjustments, 8.4 Pediatric Use, 5.1 warning
39.note: Cefiderocol is a fixed-dose, adults-only drug and modelling it perKg fabricates a paediatric dose that no label supports. Section 2.1: 'The recommended dosage of FETROJA is 2 grams administered every 8 hours by intravenous (IV) infusion over 3 hours in adults with a creatinine clearance (CLcr) of 60 to 119 mL/min.' Section 8.4 of the current (March 2026) label still reads: 'Safety and effectiveness of FETROJA in pediatric patients younger than 18 years of age have not been established' - there is no mg/kg figure anywhere in it. The 2000 mg cap accidentally produces the correct adult regimen at >=40 kg, but any patient below 40 kg is shown an invented, sub-label dose (a 20 kg child gets 1 g q8h, half the only dose the drug has ever been shown to work at). The bigger gap is renalAdj being empty: the label requires adjustment in BOTH directions - 1.5 g q8h at CLcr 30-59, 1 g q8h at 15-29, 0.75 g q12h at <15 or on intermittent HD, versus 2 g q6h at CLcr >=120 mL/min (augmented renal clearance). A dialysis patient would be shown 6 g/day against a labelled 1.5 g/day (4x overdose); an ICU patient with ARC would be under-dosed by a quarter. The label also carries a boxed-level Warning 5.1 on increased all-cause mortality in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections, so neither direction of error is benign. The infusion must run over 3 hours, which the record cannot express.
39.suggestedFix: Change kind to fixed: dose 2000 mg q8h, adults 18 years and older only (ageAdj [0,18,0] = not established, with a note rather than a silent zero). maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 8000 mg to accommodate the augmented-renal-clearance regimen. renalAdj as explicit CrCl bands, not factors: >=120 -> 2 g q6h; 60-119 -> 2 g q8h; 30-59 -> 1.5 g q8h; 15-29 -> 1 g q8h; <15 or intermittent HD -> 0.75 g q12h after dialysis. Flag: 3-hour infusion; CRRT dosing by effluent flow rate.
39.refuteReason: Could not refute — the current FETROJA label confirms every element. Section 2.1: 'The recommended dosage of FETROJA is 2 grams administered every 8 hours by intravenous (IV) infusion over 3 hours in adults with a creatinine clearance (CLcr) of 60 to 119 mL/min.' Section 8.4: 'Safety and effectiveness of FETROJA in pediatric patients younger than 18 years of age have not been established.' There is no mg/kg figure in the label, so modelling this perKg at 50 mg/kg fabricates a paediatric regimen with no labelled basis: a 20 kg child is shown 1 g q8h, half the only dose the drug has been shown to work at, and the 2000 mg cap reproduces the correct adult regimen only by accident at ≥40 kg. Table 1 confirms bidirectional renal adjustment: CLcr 30–59 → 1.5 g q8h; 15–29 → 1 g q8h; <15 → 0.75 g q12h; intermittent haemodialysis → 0.75 g q12h given immediately after HD; and for CLcr ≥120 mL/min 'FETROJA 2 grams administered every 6 hours by IV infusion over 3 hours is recommended.' With renalAdj empty a dialysis patient is shown 6 g/day against a labelled 1.5 g/day (4x), while an augmented-renal-clearance patient is under-dosed by a quarter. Warning 5.1 confirmed: an increase in all-cause mortality versus best available therapy in critically ill patients with carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections (28-day mortality 24.8% vs 18.4%), so neither direction of error is benign. The 3-hour infusion is also not expressible in this record. Verdict is best characterised as MODEL_WRONG plus MISMATCH. Suggested fix: kind=fixed 2000 mg q8h, adults ≥18 years only (ageAdj factor 0 below 18), maxDaily 8000 mg to accommodate the ARC regimen; renalAdj CLcr ≥120 → 2000 mg q6h, 60–119 → 2000 mg q8h, 30–59 → 1500 mg q8h, 15–29 → 1000 mg q8h, <15 or HD → 750 mg q12h; carry a note that each dose infuses over 3 hours.

40.name: Ampicillin/Sulbactam
40.stored: perKg 50 mg/kg q6h (=200 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 3000 mg, maxDaily 12000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj
40.source: FDA label, UNASYN (ampicillin sodium and sulbactam sodium) for injection, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION (DailyMed full prescribing information)
40.note: Unit-basis inconsistency producing a one-third paediatric under-dose. The caps are unambiguously combination-product figures - adult label is 'UNASYN 1.5 g (ampicillin 1 g and sulbactam 0.5 g) to 3 g (ampicillin 2 g and sulbactam 1 g) every six hours', total sulbactam not to exceed 4 g/day, i.e. 12 g UNASYN/day - which matches maxSingle 3000 and maxDaily 12000 exactly. Daily-total check: stored 50 x 4 = 200 mg/kg/day versus the labelled 300 mg/kg/day - 33% low for every child under 40 kg. (If the 50 was meant as ampicillin component it would be correct, but then the 3000/12000 caps are wrong by 50%; the record mixes the two conventions either way, which is exactly the kind of ambiguity that produces a dosing error at the bedside.) Also missing: the label restricts paediatric dosing to patients 1 year and older (IM route not established in children), directs patients >=40 kg to adult dosing, and requires interval extension in renal impairment - 1.5-3 g q12h at CrCl 15-29 and q24h at CrCl 5-14 - which with renalAdj empty leaves a CrCl-10 adult shown 12 g/day against a labelled 3 g/day, against ampicillin's known neurotoxicity/seizure risk on accumulation.

40.refuteReason: Could not refute — the UNASYN label confirms the unit-basis inconsistency and the resulting under-dose. 17.name: Imipenem/Cilastatin
17.stored: kind=perKg, 15 mg/kg q6h -> 60 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 4000 mg; ageAdj EMPTY; renalAdj EMPTY
17.source: FDA label (DailyMed) - PRIMAXIN IV (imipenem and cilastatin sodium) for injection, Dosage and Administration and Warnings (seizures / renal function)
17.note: Daily-total check PASSES on the paediatric side: the label gives '15-25 mg/kg' 'every 6 hours' for pediatric patients 3 months and older with non-CNS infections, so the stored 15 mg/kg q6h (60 mg/kg/day) is the per-dose value used correctly at the low end of the labelled band - no inversion. 6.name: Warfarin
6.stored: kind=fixed, dose 5 mg, freq q24h, maxSingle 10 mg, maxDaily 10 mg, ageAdj [65-120 x0.8] -> 4 mg. Weight- and INR-independent: the same 5 mg is shown for a 10 kg toddler and a 100 kg adult.
6.source: FDA label (DailyMed), WARFARIN SODIUM tablet - Dosage and Administration 2.1/2.3, Boxed Warning, 8.4 Pediatric Use
6.note:
Warfarin cannot be expressed as dose x frequency. The label states dosing "must be individualized for each patient according to the patient's INR response to the drug", with the initial dose "usually 2 to 5 mg once daily", maintenance "2 to 10 mg once daily", and a target INR of 2.5 (range 2.0-3.0). The boxed warning states warfarin "can cause major or fatal bleeding" and to "Perform regular monitoring of INR in all treated patients". A calculator that emits a single number with no INR input is misrepresenting the drug.

Two concrete problems on top of the model error: (1) 5 mg is the TOP of the labelled 2-5 mg initiation range, so it is the least safe default of the permitted set - the elderly, low body weight, hepatic impairment and interacting-drug groups all need the bottom of the range, and a flat x0.8 age factor (4 mg) is not a substitute for that. (2) This is a paediatric/adult calculator and 5 mg fixed is a gross paediatric overdose: section 8.4 says "the optimum dosing, safety, and efficacy in pediatric patients is unknown", and the accepted paediatric practice figure is ~0.2 mg/kg on day 1 (maintenance ~0.09-0.33 mg/kg/day). For a 10 kg child the app shows 0.5 mg/kg - about 2.5x the loading dose and 1.5-5x the maintenance range - sustained daily, which is a plausible route to life-threatening haemorrhage. Daily-total check is not the failure mode here (q24h, so daily = single dose); the failure is the model itself.
6.suggestedFix: Preferred: remove warfarin from dose-calculation and show an INR-titration note instead (no computed number). If it must stay: kind=fixed, dose 5 mg q24h ONLY for an adult with no risk modifiers, maxSingle 10 mg, maxDaily 10 mg, plus a mandatory non-dismissable warning "Titrate to INR 2.0-3.0; check INR daily until stable". Replace ageAdj [65,120,0.8] with an explicit starting dose of 2.5 mg q24h for age >=65, low body weight, hepatic impairment or interacting drugs. Add ageAdj [0,18,0] (or a hard 'not label-approved in children; specialist dosing ~0.2 mg/kg once daily day 1, max 10 mg' block) so a fixed 5 mg is never shown to a child.
6.refuteReason: Could not refute - I independently confirmed the claim from the FDA label itself. The DailyMed warfarin label states verbatim: "The dosage and administration of warfarin sodium must be individualized for each patient according to the patient's INR response to the drug"; initial dose "usually 2 to 5 mg once daily"; "Typical maintenance doses are 2 to 10 mg once daily"; "Obtain daily INR determinations upon initiation until stable in the therapeutic range"; boxed warning "Warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding. Perform regular monitoring of INR in all treated patients." A dose x frequency record with no INR input cannot express this - MODEL_WRONG is correct. I also verified the two secondary points. (1) 5 mg is the top of the labelled 2-5 mg initiation range, and section 8.5 states "Consider lower initiation and maintenance doses of warfarin sodium in elderly patients" - a flat x0.8 age factor yielding 4 mg does not implement that, and nothing in the record handles hepatic impairment, low body weight or interacting drugs. (2) The paediatric point is real and is the most serious part: section 8.4 states "Adequate and well-controlled studies with warfarin sodium have not been conducted in any pediatric population, and the optimum dosing, safety, and efficacy in pediatric patients is unknown." I separately confirmed the ACCP paediatric figures - day 1 loading 0.2 mg/kg (baseline INR 1-1.3), with maintenance averaging 0.33 mg/kg in infants and 0.09 mg/kg in teenagers to hold INR 2-3. Because the record is kind=fixed, a 10 kg toddler is shown 5 mg = 0.5 mg/kg/day, i.e. 2.5x the loading dose and 1.5-5.5x the maintenance requirement, given every day with no titration. The claim's arithmetic and its verdict both hold. Suggested fix: do not emit a computed number - convert to an INR-titrated advisory record (adult initiation 2-5 mg once daily, default to the LOW end, maintenance 2-10 mg once daily titrated to INR 2-3; explicit lower start for age >=65, low body weight, hepatic impairment or interacting drugs; paediatric flagged as specialist-only, 0.2 mg/kg day 1, max 10 mg, with a hard requirement for INR monitoring).
6.blockNote: Varfarin dozu her hasta için INR sonucuna göre ayrı ayrı ayarlanır; hedef INR genellikle 2,0-3,0 olup prospektüs başlangıçta 2-5 mg, idamede 2-10 mg gibi bir aralık verir, sabit bir doz vermez. Uygulama INR değerini hesaba katamadığı ve çocuklarda güvenli doz belirlenmemiş olduğu için doz gösterilmemektedir.

7.name: Insulin Regular
7.stored: kind=perKg, dose 0.5 units/kg, freq q8h, maxSingle 20 units, maxDaily 100 units, ageAdj [0-5 x0.8]. Engine daily total = 0.5 x 3 = 1.5 units/kg/day before caps.
7.source: FDA label (DailyMed), HUMULIN R (insulin human injection) - Dosage and Administration
7.note:
THIS IS THE RECURRING DAILY-DOSE-AS-PER-DOSE ERROR, and it is the most dangerous record of the six. The label says: "The average range of total daily insulin requirement for maintenance therapy in insulin-treated patients without severe insulin resistance lies between 0.5 and 1 unit/kg/day" and "In pre-pubertal children it usually varies from 0.7 to 1 unit/kg/day, but can be much lower during the period of partial remission." The 0.5 units/kg figure is the TOTAL DAILY dose; it has been entered as the per-dose value and q8h applied on top.

Daily-total check: stored 0.5 x 3 = 1.5 units/kg/day vs labelled 0.5-1 units/kg/day = 3x the bottom of the range and 1.5x the top. Worse, that labelled total daily dose is the whole insulin requirement including basal; delivering 1.5 units/kg/day as REGULAR insulin alone is far beyond any prandial component.

The caps only partly mask it and do so unpredictably: a 20 kg child gets 10 units q8h = 30 units/day = 1.5 units/kg/day (uncapped, ~2x label); a 30 kg child gets 15 units q8h = 45 units/day = 1.5 units/kg/day; a 70 kg adult is clamped at maxSingle 20 units -> 60 units/day, still ~0.86 units/kg/day of regular insulin alone with no basal accounted for, and maxDaily 100 units never fires. The 0-5 years x0.8 factor still leaves 1.2 units/kg/day in the age group least able to tolerate it (infant/toddler requirements are nearer 0.3-0.5 units/kg/day). Outcome of one use: severe hypoglycaemia, seizure, coma, death - hours, not days.

Secondary point: insulin is titrated to blood glucose, so dose x frequency is a weak model for it even at the correct number; the record should not present an unqualified computed dose.
7.suggestedFix: Do not emit a single computed regular-insulin dose. If the record must exist, store it as a TOTAL DAILY requirement: kind=perKg, dose 0.5 units/kg, freq q24h, labelled 'total daily dose - split basal/bolus, do not give as one injection', range 0.5-1 units/kg/day (0.7-1 pre-pubertal), maxDaily 1 unit/kg/day, and a mandatory 'titrate to blood glucose' warning. If a prandial regular-insulin dose is wanted instead: ~0.1 units/kg per meal q8h (derived as ~50% of a 0.5-0.6 units/kg/day TDD split over three meals), maxSingle 10 units for the default, plus a separate correction-factor input. Replace ageAdj [0,5,0.8] with [0,5,0.6-0.7] against a 0.5 units/kg/day total (infants ~0.3-0.5 units/kg/day), and add a renal rule (reduce ~25% at CrCl 10-50, ~50% below 10).

The 0.5 units/kg is explicitly a TOTAL DAILY figure; the record stores it as the per-dose value with freq q8h. The aggravating factor the claim raises is correct and important: the labelled 0.5-1 unit/kg/day is the patient's ENTIRE insulin requirement including basal, so delivering 1.5 units/kg/day as regular (short-acting) insulin alone exceeds any plausible prandial component by a wide margin. I re-derived the cap behaviour from the stored record and the claim's figures are right: a 20 kg child gets 10 units q8h = 30 units/day = 1.5 units/kg/day (maxSingle 20 never binds); a 70 kg adult is clamped at maxSingle 20 units = 60 units/day = 0.86 units/kg/day of regular insulin with no basal accounted for; maxDaily 100 units never fires at any weight the caps allow, so the engine issues no warning. The [0,5,x0.8] factor still leaves 1.2 units/kg/day in the age group least able to tolerate it. Severe hypoglycaemia, seizure, coma and death are plausible from a single administration, so critical severity is justified. The secondary point also stands - insulin is titrated to blood glucose and split basal/bolus, so dose x frequency is a poor model even at the right number. Suggested fix: do not present an unqualified computed dose. If retained at all, store the TOTAL DAILY requirement (adult/adolescent 0.5-1 unit/kg/day; pre-pubertal 0.7-1 unit/kg/day, lower in partial remission) as an advisory starting-point split into basal plus prandial components, with regular insulin representing only the prandial share, explicit glucose-monitoring and titration requirements, and no engine multiplication of a daily figure by a frequency.

8.name: Prednisolone
8.stored: kind=perKg, dose 1 mg/kg, freq q24h, maxSingle 40 mg, maxDaily 80 mg, ageAdj [65-120 x0.9]. Engine daily total = 1 x 1 = 1 mg/kg/day, clamped to 40 mg.

8.note:
Daily-total check passes - this record does NOT have the daily-vs-per-dose error. The label gives the paediatric range as "0.14 to 2 mg/kg/day in three or four divided doses (4 to 60 mg/m2bsa/day)" and the adult initial dose as "5 to 60 mg prednisolone base per day". Stored 1 mg/kg q24h = 1 mg/kg/day sits mid-range for children; the 40 mg maxSingle clamps a 70 kg adult to 40 mg/day, inside the labelled 5-60 mg/day. Once-daily morning administration is standard practice (BNF: give the total daily dose as a single dose after breakfast) even though the US label text says three or four divided doses, and the 1-2 mg/kg once daily, max 40 mg pattern is the conventional paediatric default.

One cosmetic inconsistency worth cleaning up, not a dosing error: with freq q24h and maxSingle 40, maxDaily 80 is unreachable, so the maxDaily ceiling is dead code and will never produce the warning a reviewer would expect it to. There is also no duration/taper representation - acceptable for a dose calculator, but the record silently implies indefinite daily dosing.
8.suggestedFix: Keep dose 1 mg/kg, kind=perKg, freq q24h, maxSingle 40 mg. Set maxDaily to 40 mg so the two ceilings agree (or 60 mg if adult indications up to the labelled 60 mg/day are to be reachable, in which case raise maxSingle to 60 mg too). Optionally widen the documented range to 0.5-2 mg/kg/day for indications that need it, and add a 'short course; taper if >2-3 weeks' note. The x0.9 elderly factor is harmless but not label-derived - it can be dropped or replaced with a bone/glucose-monitoring warning.

9.name: Furosemide
9.stored: kind=perKg, dose 1 mg/kg, freq q12h, maxSingle 200 mg, maxDaily 600 mg, ageAdj [0-1 x0.5], [65-120 x0.8]. Engine daily total = 1 x 2 = 2 mg/kg/day.
9.source: FDA label (DailyMed), LASIX (furosemide) tablet - Dosage and Administration
9.note:
Daily-total check passes - no daily-vs-per-dose error here either. The label states for children: "The usual initial dose of oral LASIX in pediatric patients is 2 mg/kg body weight, given as a single dose", increments of "1 or 2 mg/kg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours after the previous dose", and "Doses greater than 6 mg/kg body weight are not recommended". Stored 1 mg/kg q12h = 2 mg/kg/day, i.e. exactly the labelled initial daily amount, split - well inside the 6 mg/kg/day ceiling. The 0-1 year x0.5 factor gives 1 mg/kg/day, consistent with cautious neonatal/infant practice.

For adults the label says "The usual initial dose of LASIX is 20 mg to 80 mg given as a single dose", that "the same dose can be administered 6 to 8 hours later", for hypertension "80 mg, usually divided into 40 mg twice a day", and that it "may be carefully titrated up to 600 mg/day in patients with clinically severe edematous states". A 70 kg adult gets 70 mg q12h = 140 mg/day: the single dose is inside the 20-80 mg initial range and repeat dosing is explicitly contemplated, so this is within label, but it is roughly double the 80 mg/day hypertension starting dose and 3.5-7x the 20-40 mg once-daily start most adults actually get. Defensible as a default, but at the aggressive end.

The real gap is the ceilings, which are adult-only. maxDaily 600 mg means no warning can ever fire for a child: a 10 kg infant would have to reach 60 mg/kg/day - ten times the labelled 6 mg/kg limit - before the engine complained. Same for maxSingle 200 mg (20 mg/kg in that infant). Today the default dose never approaches those numbers, so nothing is mis-dosed; the guard-rail simply does not exist for paediatric patients.
9.suggestedFix: Keep dose 1 mg/kg, kind=perKg, freq q12h. Add a weight-scaled ceiling alongside the fixed ones: maxDaily = min(600 mg, 6 mg/kg/day) and maxSingle = min(200 mg, 2 mg/kg per dose for routine use) so the paediatric limit from the label is actually enforced. Consider switching adults (>=40-50 kg) to a fixed default of 20-40 mg once daily, titrated, rather than extrapolating 1 mg/kg to 140 mg/day. Add a renalAdj/monitoring note (electrolytes, renal function, ototoxicity with rapid high-dose IV) - renalAdj is currently empty.

10.name: Omeprazole
10.stored: kind=fixed, dose 20 mg, freq q24h, maxSingle 40 mg, maxDaily 80 mg, ageAdj [65-120 x1]. Same 20 mg is shown for a 4 kg infant and a 90 kg adult.
10.source: FDA label (DailyMed), PRILOSEC (omeprazole magnesium) - Dosage and Administration, paediatric weight-band tables
10.note:
Correct for adults, over-dosed for every small child - and this is a paediatric/adult calculator, so the default is wrong for the paediatric half of its users. The label's adult dose is "20 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks" for symptomatic GERD and "20 mg once daily for 4 weeks" for active duodenal ulcer, which the stored value matches. But paediatric dosing is by weight band, not fixed: for patients 1 to 16 years, "5 to less than 10 kg: 5 mg", "10 to less than 20 kg: 10 mg", "20 kg and greater: 20 mg" once daily; and for infants 1 month to less than 1 year (erosive oesophagitis), "3 to less than 5 kg: 2.5 mg", "5 to less than 10 kg: 5 mg", "10 kg and greater: 10 mg" once daily.

Against those bands the stored fixed 20 mg is 2x over for a 10-20 kg child, 4x over for a 5-10 kg child, and 8x over for a 3-5 kg infant. Daily-total check is clean (q24h, daily = single dose) - the error is that a band-structured dose has been flattened into one fixed number.

Severity is moderate rather than high because omeprazole is well tolerated acutely: a single 20 mg dose in a toddler will not cause immediate harm. The harm is from sustained over-suppression - hypomagnesaemia, B12 deficiency, increased C. difficile and enteric infection risk, fracture risk on prolonged therapy, and masking of symptoms - in exactly the age group where the label went to the trouble of defining bands. The ageAdj entry [65,120,1] is a no-op and adds nothing.
10.suggestedFix: Replace the single fixed value with the label's weight bands, all q24h: infants 1 month to <1 year (EE) 3-<5 kg 2.5 mg, 5-<10 kg 5 mg, >=10 kg 10 mg; children 1-16 years 5-<10 kg 5 mg, 10-<20 kg 10 mg, >=20 kg 20 mg; adults 20 mg once daily (40 mg once daily where the indication calls for it, e.g. erosive oesophagitis healing or H. pylori regimens). Set maxSingle 40 mg and maxDaily 40 mg for routine indications; if Zollinger-Ellison dosing (60 mg+ daily) is needed it should be a separate record rather than an 80 mg ceiling on the general one. If the engine cannot express bands, the closest safe single rule is kind=perKg, dose 0.7 mg/kg q24h with maxSingle 20 mg, which reproduces the bands to within about 1.4x. Drop the no-op ageAdj [65,120,1].
10.refuteReason: Could not refute - the label's paediatric weight bands are exactly as the claim describes, and I retrieved them myself.
