11.name: Aspirin
11.stored: kind=perKg, dose 10 mg/kg, freq q6h, maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 4000 mg, ageAdj [0-12 x0] (contraindicated), [12-16 x0.8]. Engine daily total = 10 x 4 = 40 mg/kg/day.
11.source: FDA OTC Drug Facts (DailyMed), ASPIRIN 325 MG tablet - Warnings and Directions; corroborated by Medsafe NZ / NZ Formulary for Children
11.note:
The dangerous part is the age rule, not the arithmetic. The ageAdj [12,16,0.8] entry actively PERMITS analgesic/antipyretic aspirin in 12-15 year olds at 0.8 x 10 mg/kg q6h = 8 mg/kg q6h = 32 mg/kg/day - for a 50 kg 14-year-old that is 400 mg four times a day, 1600 mg/day. That is precisely the Reye's syndrome exposure national formularies prohibit. The US Drug Facts carries the warning "Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use this product" with "if changes in behavior with nausea and vomiting occur, consult a doctor because these symptoms could be an early sign of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious illness", and Medsafe (NZ regulator) records that the NZ Formulary for Children contraindicates aspirin under 16 years unless it is for Kawasaki disease or prevention of thrombus formation after cardiac surgery - the same position as the BNF/BNFc. Reye's syndrome is rare but frequently fatal or disabling, hence high severity. The 0-12 x0 entry is right in spirit but stops five years short.

Secondary, smaller problem: the per-kg model over-doses adults per dose. Drug Facts directs "adults and children 12 years and over: take 1 or 2 tablets every 4 hours or 3 tablets every 6 hours, not to exceed 12 tablets in 24 hours" - 325-650 mg per dose, max 3900 mg/day on 325 mg tablets. At 10 mg/kg a 70 kg adult gets 700 mg per dose (above the 650 mg OTC ceiling) and a 100 kg adult hits the 1000 mg maxSingle. Daily-total check: 40 mg/kg/day = 2800 mg at 70 kg, under the 4000 mg cap, so no warning fires - i.e. the ceilings do not catch the per-dose excess. Adult analgesic aspirin is conventionally fixed-dose, not weight-based.

Note also that 40 mg/kg/day is in the anti-inflammatory/Kawasaki range rather than the simple-analgesic range, which is a further sign the record is modelling the wrong indication for a default.
11.suggestedFix: Change ageAdj to [[0,16,0]] - contraindicated below 16 - with an explicit 'Reye's syndrome: do not use for fever or analgesia under 16 years' warning; delete the [12,16,0.8] entry. Change the adult analgesic record to kind=fixed: 325-650 mg q4-6h (store dose 650 mg, freq q6h), maxSingle 650 mg (1000 mg only under a prescription-analgesic indication), maxDaily 4000 mg (3900 mg if modelling the 325 mg OTC tablet regimen). Keep any weight-based rule out of the default: Kawasaki disease high-dose aspirin and post-cardiac-surgery antiplatelet dosing should each be their own explicitly-labelled record with its own source check (do not carry 10 mg/kg q6h over into them unverified), and low-dose antiplatelet aspirin 75-100 mg once daily should be a third, separate record. Add a GI-bleed/anticoagulant-interaction warning and a renalAdj entry (renalAdj is currently empty; avoid at CrCl <30 for analgesic doses).
11.refuteReason: REFUTED as stated - the claim's headline finding rests on a misreading of the very label it cites, and two of its supporting statements are factually wrong. (1) I fetched the cited DailyMed Drug Facts. Its Directions read: "adults and children 12 years and over: 1-2 tablets every 4 hours while symptoms last, not more than 12 tablets in 24 hours" and "children under 12 years: ask a doctor". The FDA-approved labelling therefore AFFIRMATIVELY PERMITS analgesic aspirin from age 12, so a [12,16,x0.8] entry is not a deviation from the top-priority source - it is what that source directs. The claim also mis-quotes these Directions, inserting "or 3 tablets every 6 hours", which does not appear on this label. (2) The claim presents the Reye's warning as an age bar. It is not: the actual text is conditional - "Children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chicken pox or flu-like symptoms should not use this product" - a viral-illness restriction, not an under-16 contraindication. (3) The claim's closing note that "40 mg/kg/day is in the anti-inflammatory/Kawasaki range" is wrong: AHA high-dose Kawasaki therapy is 80-100 mg/kg/day and anti-inflammatory/rheumatic dosing is roughly 60-100 mg/kg/day, so 40 mg/kg/day sits below both and within conventional analgesic/antipyretic dosing (10-15 mg/kg/dose q4-6h). The stored 10 mg/kg/dose is at the LOW end of that range, and the x0.8 factor lowers it to 8 mg/kg - the age entry the claim calls dangerous reduces exposure rather than increasing it. What I did confirm is that the claim's Medsafe citation is accurate - the NZ Formulary for Children does contraindicate aspirin under 16 years except for Kawasaki disease and prevention of thrombus after cardiac surgery, matching the BNF/BNFc position. So the age rule is a genuine jurisdictional split (FDA permits 12+, UK/NZ formularies do not), not an established error; under the stated source hierarchy the FDA label ranks first, and a defensible default cannot be called wrong on a lower-ranked formulary alone. Marking refuted=true so an unproven high-severity Reye's finding does not reach a clinician as fact. One narrower, genuinely valid point does survive and should be raised separately on its own merits rather than as validation of this claim: StatPearls gives adult analgesic aspirin as "325 to 650 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, with a maximum daily dose of 4 g", and the cited Drug Facts caps a dose at 2 x 325 mg = 650 mg. The stored maxSingle of 1000 mg exceeds that per-dose ceiling, so a 70 kg adult is shown 700 mg and a 100 kg adult 1000 mg per dose - modestly over-label per dose (moderate, not high, severity; well below the ~150 mg/kg acute-toxicity threshold), while maxDaily 4000 mg is only trivially above the 3900 mg the Drug Facts allows. Suggested fix if the record is revised: keep ageAdj [0,12,0]; either keep [12,16,0.8] with an explicit "avoid in febrile/viral illness - Reye's syndrome" warning (US labelling) or set it to 0 with Kawasaki/antiplatelet carve-outs (BNF/BNFc/NZFC) as a documented jurisdiction choice; lower maxSingle from 1000 mg to 650 mg and maxDaily to 3900 mg for the analgesic default; and consider fixed adult dosing of 325-650 mg q4-6h rather than per-kg.

48.name: Norfloxacin
48.stored: kind=fixed, 400 mg q12h -> 800 mg/day; maxSingle 400, maxDaily 800; ageAdj [] ; renalAdj []
48.source: FDA NOROXIN (norfloxacin) prescribing information, Dosage and Administration + Pediatric Use (RxList mirror of the Merck FDA label; accessdata PDF 019384s062 retrieved but font-encoded and unreadable)
48.note: The mg number itself is right: the label gives 400 mg q12h for every UTI/prostatitis indication with an 800 mg maximum daily dose, so the daily-total check passes (400 x 2 = 800 = maxDaily). There is no per-dose/per-day inversion here. The record fails on the two guards it omits. (1) ageAdj is empty. The label states 'The safety and effectiveness of oral norfloxacin in pediatric patients and adolescents below the age of 18 years have not been established', and the FDA label carries the fluoroquinolone arthropathy data (permanent weight-bearing cartilage lesions in immature dogs at 6x the human mg/kg dose). Because kind=fixed, a paediatric/adult calculator with no age rule hands a clinician the full adult 400 mg q12h for a child of any weight - roughly 40 mg/kg/day in a 20 kg child versus about 11 mg/kg/day in an adult - for a drug class not established below 18. (2) renalAdj is empty, but the label requires 'one 400-mg tablet once daily' at creatinine clearance <=30 mL/min/1.73 m2, i.e. half the stored daily total; norfloxacin accumulation in renal impairment drives CNS toxicity and seizures. Separately worth flagging to the product owner: Noroxin was withdrawn from the US market in 2016 and norfloxacin is suspended/restricted across the EU, so listing it as a default antibiotic is questionable independent of the numbers. Note also that uncomplicated gonorrhoea uses 800 mg as a SINGLE dose, which the stored q12h rule would wrongly turn into 1600 mg/day if a clinician picked that indication.
48.suggestedFix: Keep dose 400 mg, freq q12h, maxSingle 400, maxDaily 800. Add ageAdj [[0,18,0]] (not established / effectively contraindicated below 18 years - fluoroquinolone arthropathy). Add renalAdj [[0,30,0.5]] (CrCl <=30 mL/min/1.73 m2 -> 400 mg ONCE daily). Flag the gonorrhoea 800 mg single-dose regimen as a separate entry rather than letting q12h apply to it, and consider retiring the drug given worldwide withdrawal.
48.refuteReason: CLAIM STANDS (refuted=false). I did not take rxlist on trust — I pulled the FDA Noroxin label (Reference ID 3356550) and extracted its text directly. The dosing chart reads, verbatim: Urinary Tract / uncomplicated UTI (cystitis) 400 mg, q12h, 3 days, Daily Dose 800 mg; uncomplicated UTI other organisms 400 mg q12h 7-10 days, 800 mg; complicated UTI 400 mg q12h 10-21 days, 800 mg; Prostatitis acute or chronic 400 mg q12h 28 days, 800 mg; Uncomplicated Gonorrhea 800 mg single dose, 800 mg. So the daily-total check passes exactly as the claim concedes (400 x 2 = 800 = maxDaily) and there is NO per-dose/per-day inversion. One small wording correction to the claim: the label never uses the phrase 'maximum recommended daily dose' — I searched the extracted text and it does not occur; 800 mg is the 'Daily Dose' column value, identical for every row. That is cosmetic and does not rescue the record. Both omitted guards are real and both are label-mandated. (1) Renal: verbatim, 'In patients with a creatinine clearance rate of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or less, the recommended dosage is one 400-mg tablet once daily for the duration given above.' The label also states that in those patients 'the renal elimination of norfloxacin decreases so that the effective serum half-life is 6.5 hours. In these patients, alteration of dosage is necessary.' renalAdj=[] therefore delivers exactly double the labelled dose to a CrCl<=30 patient, with no warning. (2) Paediatric: verbatim, 'THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF ORAL NORFLOXACIN IN PEDIATRIC PATIENTS, ADOLESCENTS (UNDER THE AGE OF 18), PREGNANT WOMEN, AND NURSING MOTHERS HAVE NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED,' immediately followed by the arthropathy data the claim describes: single doses 'norfloxacin, 6 times the recommended human clinical dose (on a mg/kg basis), caused lameness in immature dogs. Histologic examination of the weight-bearing joints of these dogs revealed permanent lesions of the cartilage.' Because kind=fixed, the engine hands a clinician 400 mg q12h irrespective of weight, so a 20 kg child is shown ~40 mg/kg/day against ~11 mg/kg/day in a 70 kg adult. The claim's gonorrhoea point is also confirmed by the chart above: 800 mg is a SINGLE dose, not q12h. NOTE ON VERDICT LABEL: the taxonomy fit is imperfect — the stored mg value MATCHES the label, so 'MISMATCH' is the wrong bucket; the defect is two omitted guards, not a wrong number. I am nonetheless returning refuted=false because the record as stored is genuinely unsafe and must not be signed off as correct. SEVERITY: high (fluoroquinolone arthropathy/tendinopathy in a child; accumulation and CNS toxicity/seizures at CrCl<=30). SUGGESTED FIX: keep kind=fixed, dose 400 mg q12h, maxSingle 400, maxDaily 800; add renalAdj [[0,30,0.5]] (i.e. 400 mg q24h at CrCl<=30 mL/min/1.73 m2, which is the labelled regimen, not a factor applied to the single dose — if the engine can only scale the single dose, store it as frequency q24h under that branch); add ageAdj [[0,18,0]] to mark not-established/contraindicated below 18 years. Separately worth raising with the product owner, and independently true: Noroxin was withdrawn from the US market and norfloxacin is restricted in the EU, so its presence as a default antibiotic is questionable regardless of the numbers.
48.fix: 400 mg sabit, q12h, tek doz tavanı 400, günlük 800; 18 yaş altı reddediliyor; CrCl ≤30'da 400 mg günde bir kez (sıklık değişikliği, doz aynı). 50.name: Netilmicin
50.stored: kind=perKg, 4 mg/kg q24h -> 4 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 300, maxDaily 400; renalAdj []
50.source: Netromycin (netilmicin sulfate) CPS monograph, Dosage and Administration - adult, paediatric and neonatal regimens plus peak/trough targets
50.note: Daily-total check: stored gives 4 mg/kg/day. For ADULTS that is defensible - the monograph gives '4.0 to 6.0 mg/kg/day divided into 2 or 3 equal doses' for serious systemic infection and exactly '4.0 mg/kg/day divided into 2 equal doses' for UTI. But this is a paediatric calculator, and for CHILDREN the monograph specifies '6.0 to 7.5 mg/kg/day divided into 3 equal doses and administered every 8 hours', with infants/neonates over 1 week at '7.5 to 9.0 mg/kg/day'. The stored 4 mg/kg/day therefore UNDER-doses every child by 33-47% against the paediatric floor, and a neonate by more than half - treatment failure in serious gram-negative sepsis, which is what netilmicin is reserved for. Three further defects. (a) The q24h interval is not the labelled interval (the monograph divides the daily dose q8h or q12h throughout); once-daily extended-interval aminoglycoside dosing is accepted modern practice in adults but is off-label for netilmicin and is not appropriate for neonates, where the record would silently apply it. (b) maxSingle 300 and maxDaily 400 are mutually inconsistent under a q24h rule - single dose equals daily dose, so the effective ceiling is 300 mg/day and maxDaily 400 is dead code that will never fire a warning. (c) renalAdj is empty. This is the most dangerous omission: netilmicin is nephrotoxic and ototoxic, is not metabolised and is cleared entirely by glomerular filtration, and the monograph requires dosage be titrated to serum levels - peak 4-12 mcg/mL avoiding sustained peaks above 16, trough kept below 4 and ideally 0.5-2 mcg/mL. A fixed mg/kg rule with no renal factor will accumulate to deafness or acute kidney injury in a patient with reduced clearance. Also worth telling the product owner that netilmicin has been discontinued in the US, UK and most other markets.
50.suggestedFix: Split by age. Children: dose 2.5 mg/kg q8h (7.5 mg/kg/day) or 2 mg/kg q8h (6 mg/kg/day) for the conservative default. Neonates over 1 week: 2.5-3 mg/kg q8h; neonates under 1 week: 3 mg/kg q12h (6 mg/kg/day). Adults: 2 mg/kg q12h (4 mg/kg/day, UTI) up to 2 mg/kg q8h (6 mg/kg/day, serious systemic). Cap any individual dose at 3.25 mg/kg. Set maxSingle 200 and maxDaily 400 so the two are consistent under a q8-12h rule. Add renalAdj, e.g. [[0,10,0.25],[10,30,0.5],[30,60,0.75]], and attach a hard non-dismissible warning that the dose must be adjusted to measured peak and trough serum concentrations.
50.refuteReason: CLAIM STANDS ON ITS CORE POINT (refuted=false), BUT ONE OF ITS FOUR SUB-CLAIMS IS WRONG AND SHOULD NOT BE PASSED ON. I deliberately did not rely on the cited rxmed CPS monograph; I extracted an independent MIMS-derived monograph verbatim. It reads: 'Adult: 4-6 mg/kg once daily or in equally divided doses given every 8 or 12 hr. Life-threatening infections: Increase to up to 7.5 mg/kg daily every 8 hr.' and 'Child: Premature infants and neonates <1 wk: 6 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 12 hr. Infants and neonates >1 wk: 7.5-9 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 8 hr. Older children: 6-7.5 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 8 hr. Alternative regimen: Neonates <6 wk: 4-6.5 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 12 hr. Older infants and children: 5.5-8 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 8 or 12 hr.' The CPS monograph I also retrieved agrees on the paediatric figures (6.0-7.5 mg/kg/day q8h for children; 7.5-9.0 mg/kg/day for neonates >1 week). CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: sub-claim (a) is not supportable. Once-daily administration is an explicitly labelled adult option — 'Adult: 4-6 mg/kg once daily' — so q24h is NOT off-label for netilmicin in adults, and 4 mg/kg q24h sits exactly on the bottom of the labelled adult once-daily range. For an adult the stored default is defensible. Do not tell the product owner once-daily is off-label. WHAT SURVIVES, and why the record is still wrong for a paediatric calculator: the stored 4 mg/kg/day is below EVERY paediatric range in the monograph. Older children 6-7.5 (stored is 33-47% low), neonates >1 wk 7.5-9 (stored is 47-56% low), neonates <1 wk 6 (33% low); even the permissive alternative regimen floors are 5.5 (older infants/children) and 4.0 for neonates <6 wk only, and that one is q12h, not q24h. Netilmicin is reserved for serious gram-negative sepsis, where under-dosing is treatment failure. Sub-claim (b) is arithmetically correct and I confirmed it by inspection: with freq=q24h the single dose IS the daily dose, so maxSingle 300 binds first and maxDaily 400 is dead code that can never fire a warning; worse, maxSingle 300 silently caps any patient above 75 kg below even 4 mg/kg/day (a 100 kg adult gets 3 mg/kg/day), a CAP_UNDERDOSES defect the claim under-states. Sub-claim (c) is confirmed: the monograph's Renal Impairment section reads 'Dose reduction or lengthening of interval between doses may be necessary,' Special Precautions require 'Renal impairment; monitor renal, vestibular and auditory function. Monitor peak serum levels,' and Adverse Reactions lists 'Potentially Fatal: Nephrotoxicity; ototoxicity; anaphylaxis.' renalAdj=[] on a drug excreted 80% unchanged in urine within 24 hr is the most dangerous omission in the record. SEVERITY: high (paediatric treatment failure in gram-negative sepsis; accumulation to ototoxicity/AKI in renal impairment). SUGGESTED FIX: this record is arguably MODEL_WRONG as well — netilmicin is titrated to serum peak/trough, which one dose x frequency cannot express — so the first fix is a mandatory 'adjust to serum levels' warning (peak 5-10 mcg/mL, trough <2 mcg/mL; avoid sustained peaks >16 and troughs >4). Failing that: split by age — neonates <1 wk 2 mg/kg q12h (6 mg/kg/day); infants/neonates >1 wk 2.5-3 mg/kg q8h (7.5-9 mg/kg/day); older children 2-2.5 mg/kg q8h (6-7.5 mg/kg/day); adults 4-6 mg/kg q24h or 2 mg/kg q8h, up to 7.5 mg/kg/day q8h in life-threatening infection. Raise maxDaily to 7.5 mg/kg-equivalent and make maxSingle interval-aware so it stops capping heavy adults. Add renalAdj, e.g. [[50,90,0.75],[10,50,0.5],[0,10,0.25]] as a starting frame, flagged as level-guided. The product owner should also be told netilmicin is discontinued in the US, UK and most markets — independently true.
50.blockNote: Netilmisin yaşa göre farklı şemalarla verilir (erişkinde günde 4-6 mg/kg, 2-3 doza bölünerek; çocukta 8 saatte bir 2-2,5 mg/kg) ve böbrek yetmezliğinde 2 mg/kg yükleme dozundan sonraki dozlar serum kreatininine göre hesaplanıp kan düzeyi ölçümüyle (dip düzey 2 mcg/mL altında olacak şekilde) ayarlanmalıdır. Bu şema tek bir sabit kuralla güvenle ifade edilemediği için doz gösterilmez.

52.name: Roxithromycin
52.stored: kind=perKg, 5 mg/kg q12h -> 10 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 300, maxDaily 600
52.source: Medsafe New Zealand Data Sheet, Arrow-Roxithromycin 150/300 mg coated tablets, section 4.2 Dose and method of administration and section 4.4 Special warnings (text extracted directly from the retrieved PDF)
52.note: This is a textbook instance of the recurring error in this data set. The datasheet states: 'Paediatric population: Roxithromycin is administered twice daily at a dose of 5 to 8 mg/kg/day', and reinforces it under warnings: 'It is recommended that the approved paediatric dosage regimen (i.e. 5 to 8 mg/kg/day for a maximum of ten days) be adhered to strictly.' The figure 5 is a mg/kg/DAY total, and the record has stored it as the PER-DOSE value with q12h applied on top, so the engine computes 10 mg/kg/day - 1.25x above the labelled ceiling of 8 and 2x the labelled floor. The correct per-dose value is 2.5-4 mg/kg; the datasheet's own pharmacokinetics section confirms the unit of administration is 'repeated administration of 2.5 mg/kg every twelve hours to children'. The ceilings are doubled by the same mistake and so cannot rescue the calculation: the label says for adults 'The recommended dosage is 300 mg per day' (one 300 mg tablet daily, or 150 mg twice daily), and for children 40 kg and over 'One roxithromycin 150 mg tablet morning and evening' - a 300 mg/day total. Stored maxSingle 300 is 2x the 150 mg per-dose and maxDaily 600 is 2x the labelled 300 mg/day adult maximum, so any patient at or above 60 kg is clamped to 300 mg q12h = 600 mg/day, exactly double the label, with no warning fired. Consequence is not theoretical: the same datasheet reports neutropenia in children (31.6% of 402 children in clinical trials ended therapy with a neutrophil count below the normal range, 4% below 1,500/mm3 and 1.2% below 1,000/mm3), macrolide QT prolongation, and a higher incidence of gastrointestinal events at the higher 300 mg regimen - which is why it tells prescribers to adhere strictly.
52.suggestedFix: Store the PER-DOSE value, not the daily total: kind=perKg, dose 3 mg/kg, freq q12h (= 6 mg/kg/day, mid of the labelled 5-8 range; acceptable per-dose band 2.5-4 mg/kg). Set maxSingle 150 and maxDaily 300 to match the labelled adult/>=40 kg ceiling. Add a fixed-dose branch for children >=40 kg and adults: 150 mg q12h (or 300 mg q24h). Add a hepatic rule - documented cirrhotic liver disease -> 150 mg ONCE daily, and severe hepatic impairment is a contraindication. Cap treatment duration at 10 days and surface the paediatric neutropenia and QT warnings.
52.refuteReason: CLAIM FULLY CONFIRMED (refuted=false). This is the dataset's signature per-day-entered-as-per-dose error and I verified it against a DIFFERENT source from the one cited — the Roxithromycin 150 Summary of Product Characteristics, version 1_2024, from the Thai FDA medicines register — extracting the text myself rather than trusting a summary. Section 4.2 Posology, Children, verbatim: 'The recommended dose and duration of treatment should not be exceeded in children (see Section 4.4). Roxithromycin is administered twice daily at a dose of 5 to 8 mg/kg/day.' The figure 5 is unambiguously a mg/kg/DAY total and the '5 to 8' band is the whole daily allowance. The record stores 5 as the PER-DOSE value with q12h layered on top, so the engine computes 10 mg/kg/day — 1.25x the labelled ceiling of 8 and 2x the labelled floor. Three independent lines in the same SmPC confirm the unit of administration is half that: (i) the pharmacokinetics section states 'After repeated administration of 2.5 mg/kg every 12 hours to children, the average peak plasma concentration at steady state was 9 mg/L'; (ii) Section 4.4 repeats 'It is recommended that the approved paediatric dosage regimen (i.e. 5 to 8 mg/kg/day for a maximum of ten days) be adhered to strictly'; (iii) '40 kg and over: one Roxithromycin 150 mg tablet morning and evening,' a 300 mg/day total. The correct per-dose value is 2.5-4 mg/kg, exactly as the claim states. The ceilings carry the same doubling and so cannot rescue the calculation: Adults, verbatim, 'The recommended dosage is 300 mg per day... Usual dosage: one tablet twice daily or two tablets once daily.' Stored maxSingle 300 is 2x the labelled 150 mg per dose and maxDaily 600 is 2x the labelled 300 mg/day, so every patient at or above 60 kg is clamped to 300 mg q12h = 600 mg/day, precisely double the label, and maxDaily never fires. The harm context in the claim is also verbatim accurate: 'Neutropenia was observed in children treated with roxithromycin. 31.6% of 402 children in clinical trials had a neutrophil count below the lower limit of the normal range (3,500/mm3) at the conclusion of therapy... Of these, 4% had a neutrophil count of less than 1,500/mm3 and 1.2% had a count of less than 1,000/mm3,' and 'the incidence of gastrointestinal events was higher with the 300 mg once daily dosage regimen than with 150 mg twice daily.' TWO THINGS I FOUND THAT THE CLAIM MISSED, one of which cuts in the record's favour: (1) the same SmPC states 'Roxithromycin is not recommended for children of under 40 kg' for the 150 mg tablet, so a smooth per-kg rule is additionally inappropriate for small children on this strength and the record should carry a formulation/weight note. (2) renalAdj=[] is actually CORRECT here and should not be flagged — Section 4.2 states 'Dosage adjustment in: - Renal impairment: one tablet twice daily or two tablets once daily. - Elderly: one tablet twice daily or two tablets once daily,' i.e. no reduction. SEVERITY: high (2x the labelled daily dose in children with documented dose-related neutropenia and macrolide QT prolongation, and a silent 2x clamp in adults, with the label expressly demanding strict adherence). SUGGESTED FIX: kind=perKg, dose 2.5-4 mg/kg (store 3 as the default), freq q12h, giving 5-8 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 150, maxDaily 300; add a >=40 kg rule switching to fixed 150 mg q12h and a note that the 150 mg tablet is not recommended under 40 kg; cap duration at 10 days; leave renalAdj empty, which the label supports.

53.name: Tetracycline
53.stored: kind=perKg, 5 mg/kg q6h -> 20 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 500, maxDaily 2000; ageAdj []
53.source: DailyMed / FDA - Tetracycline Hydrochloride Capsules USP 250 mg and 500 mg, Dosage and Administration and Warnings (tooth development)
53.note: Two separate defects, and unusually the dose error points the under-dosing way. Daily-total check: stored 5 mg/kg q6h = 20 mg/kg/day, but the label for children above 8 years reads 'Usual daily dose, 10 mg/lb to 20 mg/lb (25 mg/kg to 50 mg/kg) body weight divided in four equal doses'. 20 mg/kg/day falls BELOW the 25 mg/kg/day floor and is 60% below the top of the range, so the default under-treats every child - sub-therapeutic tetracycline risks treatment failure and resistance selection in the rickettsial and atypical infections it is chosen for. The correct per-dose value for q6h is 6.25-12.5 mg/kg. The second and more serious defect is that ageAdj is empty. The label warns that tetracyclines used 'during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown)' and states plainly that 'Tetracycline drugs should not be used in this age group, except for anthrax, unless other drugs are not likely to be effective or are contraindicated'. With no age rule, this paediatric calculator will compute and display a tetracycline dose for a 2-year-old without objection, causing permanent enamel hypoplasia and tooth staining. The single per-kg rule also serves adults badly in the opposite direction: 5 mg/kg x 70 kg = 350 mg q6h = 1400 mg/day, which never trips maxSingle 500, against a labelled adult 'Usual daily dose, 1 gram as 500 mg twice a day or 250 mg four times a day' - so children get less than the paediatric floor while adults get about 1.4x the usual adult daily dose. Note too that tetracycline (unlike doxycycline and minocycline) is renally cleared and accumulates to hepatotoxic and azotaemic levels in renal impairment, yet renalAdj is empty.
53.suggestedFix: Children over 8 years: kind=perKg, dose 6.25 mg/kg q6h (= 25 mg/kg/day, labelled floor; range 6.25-12.5 mg/kg per dose for 25-50 mg/kg/day), maxSingle 500, maxDaily 2000. Adults: fixed 500 mg q12h or 250 mg q6h (1 g/day usual), maxDaily 2000 reserved for severe infection. Add ageAdj [[0,8,0]] - contraindicated below 8 years (permanent tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia), with an anthrax-only override if the app supports indication-specific exceptions. Add a renal rule or hard warning: avoid in renal impairment, reduce dose and extend the interval, and prefer doxycycline. Also add the pregnancy contraindication (second and third trimester).
53.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED (refuted=false), with one nuance that slightly softens its adult argument. Rather than trust the cited DailyMed rendering I fetched the FDA-approved label PDF for tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Reference ID 3740369) and extracted the text. DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, verbatim: 'Adults: Usual daily dose, 1 gram as 500 mg twice a day or 250 mg four times a day. Higher doses such as 500 mg four times a day may be required for severe infections or for those infections which do not respond to the smaller doses. For pediatric patients above eight years of age: Usual daily dose, 10 mg/lb to 20 mg/lb (25 mg/kg to 50 mg/kg) body weight divided in four equal doses.' DAILY-TOTAL CHECK: stored 5 mg/kg x 4 doses = 20 mg/kg/day, which falls BELOW the 25 mg/kg/day floor and is 60% below the 50 mg/kg/day top. The under-dose is confirmed. Correct per-dose value for q6h is 6.25-12.5 mg/kg, exactly as claimed. Tetracycline is chosen for rickettsial and atypical infections where sub-therapeutic exposure means treatment failure in conditions that can kill. AGE GUARD: confirmed verbatim in WARNINGS, Tooth Development: 'The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown). This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses. Enamel hypoplasia has also been reported. Tetracycline drugs should not be used in this age group, except for anthrax, unless other drugs are not likely to be effective or are contraindicated.' With ageAdj=[] the calculator will compute and display a tetracycline dose for a 2-year-old without objection, and the harm — permanent staining and enamel hypoplasia — is irreversible. RENAL: also confirmed, and the label is stronger than the claim implies. WARNINGS states 'in patients with significantly impaired renal function, higher serum levels of tetracycline may lead to azotemia, hyperphosphatemia and acidosis,' and 'If renal impairment exists, even usual oral or parenteral doses may lead to excessive systemic accumulation of the drug and possible liver toxicity. Under such conditions, lower than usual total doses are indicated, and, if therapy is prolonged, serum level determinations of the drug may be advisable.' ADVERSE REACTIONS adds 'hepatotoxicity and liver failure have been observed in... tetracycline-treated patients with renal impairment.' renalAdj=[] is a genuine defect. NUANCE CORRECTING THE CLAIM: its adult argument overstates the case. A 70 kg adult does get 350 mg q6h = 1400 mg/day, and that is 1.4x the 'usual' 1 g/day — but the label expressly sanctions 'Higher doses such as 500 mg four times a day' (2 g/day) for severe or non-responding infections, so 1400 mg/day sits inside the label's overall adult span rather than outside it. The adult limb is therefore a poor default, not an overdose. The paediatric under-dose and the missing age guard are the real findings. SEVERITY: high (irreversible dental harm in under-8s with no guard; sub-therapeutic dosing in potentially fatal rickettsial disease). Not critical only because neither consequence follows from a single administration. SUGGESTED FIX: kind=perKg, dose 6.25-12.5 mg/kg (store 6.25 as the conservative default), freq q6h, giving 25-50 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 500, maxDaily 2000; add ageAdj [[0,8,0]] to make under-8 contraindicated with an override note for anthrax; add an adult branch of fixed 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h (1 g/day usual, up to 500 mg q6h in severe infection) so the per-kg rule stops governing adults; add renalAdj reducing total daily dose with an explicit 'lower than usual total doses indicated, monitor BUN/creatinine' warning, since tetracycline (unlike doxycycline and minocycline) is renally cleared and is not dialyzable.
53.fix: 6.25 (kg başına), q6h, tek doz tavanı 250, günlük tavan 2000; 2 yaş bandı. Kaynak: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=b504e612-5aef-47fa-8f7b-dfb754011b9f&type=display (kaynaktan türetildi, bağımsız kontrolden geçti)

54.name: Minocycline
54.stored: kind=perKg, 2 mg/kg q12h -> 4 mg/kg/day; maxSingle 100, maxDaily 200; ageAdj []
54.source: DailyMed / FDA - Minocycline Hydrochloride Capsules, Dosage and Administration and Warnings (tooth development)
54.note: The stored numbers are correct and the recurring per-dose/per-day inversion is NOT present. The label's paediatric regimen for patients above 8 years is '4 mg/kg initially followed by 2 mg/kg every 12 hours, not to exceed the usual adult dose', so the stored 2 mg/kg q12h is exactly the labelled maintenance dose and 4 mg/kg/day is the correct daily total. (2) ageAdj is empty, and the label states 'Minocycline is not recommended for the use in children below 8 years of age unless the expected benefits of therapy outweigh the risks', with the tetracycline-class warning that use to age 8 may cause permanent yellow-gray-brown tooth discoloration. Add ageAdj [[0,8,0]] for 'not recommended below 8 years - permanent tooth discoloration', matching the rule added to tetracycline. 61.name: Piperasilin/Tazobaktam (Piperacillin/Tazobactam)
61.stored: kind=perKg, dose=100 mg/kg, freq=q8h (daily total 300 mg/kg/day), maxSingle=4500 mg, maxDaily=18000 mg, ageAdj=[], renalAdj=[]
61.source: FDA prescribing information, ZOSYN (piperacillin and tazobactam) injection — DailyMed, section 2 Dosage and Administration (Table 2 pediatric dosing, Table 1 renal impairment)
61.note: The daily-total check PASSES — this record does not have the per-dose/per-day confusion. 100 mg/kg x 3 doses = 300 mg/kg/day of the piperacillin component, which is exactly the labelled paediatric dose for appendicitis/peritonitis in patients >9 months: '112.5 mg/kg (100 mg piperacillin and 12.5 mg tazobactam) every 8 hours'. Adult behaviour also lands correctly: a 70 kg adult computes 7000 mg, clamps to maxSingle 4500 mg q8h = 13.5 g/day combined, which equals the labelled adult total ('3.375 g every six hours [totaling 13.5 g (12.0 g piperacillin and 1.5 g tazobactam)]'). Add ageAdj [[0.167, 0.75, 0.8]] (80 mg pip/kg q8h for 2-9 months) and [[0, 0.167, 0]] (not established under 2 months). Add renalAdj [[20, 40, 0.67], [0, 20, 0.67 with interval extended to q8h]] per Table 1. Prefer q6h as the adult default interval.

62.name: Meropenem
62.stored: kind=perKg, dose=20 mg/kg, freq=q8h (daily total 60 mg/kg/day), maxSingle=2000 mg, maxDaily=6000 mg, ageAdj=[], renalAdj=[]
62.source: FDA prescribing information, meropenem for injection — DailyMed, Dosage and Administration (adult and paediatric dose tables, renal impairment table)
62.note: The per-kg number itself is correct and there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error: 20 mg/kg q8h is exactly the labelled paediatric dose for complicated intra-abdominal infection. The defect is the CEILING. The label caps that indication at 1 gram per dose (10 mg/kg max 500 mg for cSSSI; 20 mg/kg max 1 g for cIAI; 40 mg/kg max 2 g for meningitis), and states that patients over 50 kg receive fixed adult dosing — 500 mg q8h for cSSSI, 1 g q8h for cIAI, 2 g q8h for meningitis. With maxSingle set to the meningitis-only value of 2000 mg, a 70 kg adult is shown 1400 mg q8h = 4.2 g/day against a labelled 3 g/day for the default indication (40% over), and a 100 kg patient is shown 2 g q8h = 6 g/day, i.e. the full meningitis regimen, from a record whose default is not meningitis. Separately, renalAdj is empty although the label mandates adjustment below CrCl 50 (26-50: same dose q12h; 10-25: half dose q12h; <10: half dose q24h). A patient with CrCl 10-25 shown the unadjusted 20 mg/kg q8h receives roughly 3x the labelled exposure, and meropenem seizure risk is exposure-related — this is the more clinically dangerous half of the finding.
62.suggestedFix: Default (intra-abdominal) entry: dose 20 mg/kg q8h, maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 3000 mg. Add a separate meningitis entry: 40 mg/kg q8h, maxSingle 2000 mg, maxDaily 6000 mg. Add ageAdj [[0, 0.25, 0]] (label covers >=3 months). Add renalAdj [[26, 50, 1.0 with interval q12h], [10, 25, 0.5 with interval q12h], [0, 10, 0.5 with interval q24h]].
62.refuteReason:
NOT REFUTED — I independently confirmed the claim from the label itself, and from a second jurisdiction. Verdict MISMATCH, severity high.

What I retrieved from the DailyMed meropenem label's Dosage and Administration: paediatric (3 months and older) table reads cSSSI 10 mg/kg max 500 mg q8h; intra-abdominal 20 mg/kg max 1 gram q8h; meningitis 40 mg/kg max 2 grams q8h. Immediately below: 'Pediatric Patients Weighing >50 kg: Administer adult dosing' — 500 mg q8h (cSSSI), 1 g q8h (intra-abdominal), 2 g q8h (meningitis). Adult cIAI is 1 g q8h = 3 g/day. Renal table: CrCl >50 full dose q8h; 26-50 full dose q12h; 10-25 half dose q12h; <10 half dose q24h.

I cross-checked the UK/EU SmPC (https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/10969/smpc), which gives the same picture independently: adult 500 mg or 1 g q8h for cIAI, cUTI, cSSTI and severe pneumonia; 2 g q8h reserved for acute bacterial meningitis and broncho-pulmonary infection in cystic fibrosis; 'Children over 50 kg: the adult dose should be administered'; identical renal table.

So the per-kg number (20 mg/kg q8h) is right and there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error — the claim correctly says so. The defects it names are real: (1) the record extrapolates per-kg past 50 kg where both labels switch to fixed adult dosing, so a 70 kg adult is shown 1400 mg q8h = 4.2 g/day against 3 g/day, and a 100 kg patient is clamped to 2 g q8h = 6 g/day, i.e. the meningitis/CF-only regimen, from a record whose default is not meningitis; (2) renalAdj is empty although both labels mandate adjustment at CrCl <=50, and at CrCl 10-25 the unadjusted rule delivers roughly 4x the labelled exposure, which matters because meropenem neurotoxicity/seizure risk is exposure-related.

One imprecision in the claim, not enough to refute it: 2000 mg is not strictly 'the meningitis-only value' — the EU SmPC also licenses 2 g q8h for cystic-fibrosis broncho-pulmonary infection. The substantive point is unaffected: 2 g q8h is not the adult dose for this record's default indication.

Suggested fix: keep kind=perKg dose=20 mg/kg q8h, set maxSingle=1000 mg and maxDaily=3000 mg (the cIAI ceiling), add a weight/age rule switching to fixed 1 g q8h above 50 kg, add renalAdj [[26,50,1.0 with interval q12h],[10,25,0.5 q12h],[0,9,0.5 q24h]] — note the label adjusts the INTERVAL as well as the dose, so a pure multiplicative factor cannot express it and the engine needs a frequency override. Add a note that meningitis and CF use 40 mg/kg q8h (max 2 g).
62.fix: 20 (kg başına), q8h, tek doz tavanı 1000, günlük tavan 3000; 2 yaş bandı; 4 böbrek bandı. Kaynak: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=092ebd9b-77a0-4877-afc3-dd8211730f71 (kaynaktan türetildi, bağımsız kontrolden geçti)

63.name: Vankomisin (Vancomycin)
63.stored: kind=perKg, dose=15 mg/kg, freq=q12h (daily total 30 mg/kg/day), maxSingle=2000 mg, maxDaily=4000 mg, ageAdj=[], renalAdj=[]
63.source: FDA prescribing information, VANCOMYCIN injection — DailyMed, section 2 Dosage and Administration; plus the 2020 ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP revised consensus guideline (Rybak et al., Clin Infect Dis 2020;71(6):1361-4) as quoted in the cited paediatric study

70.name: Kotrimoksazol (Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole)

The adult default the app would display is therefore 70 kg x 5 = 350 mg TMP q12h = 700 mg TMP/day, against the labelled adult regimen of 1 DS tablet q12h = 160 mg TMP q12h = 320 mg TMP/day — 2.2x; a 100 kg patient is shown 500 mg TMP q12h, 3.1x. Only the Pneumocystis regimen ('75 to 100 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole and 15 to 20 mg/kg trimethoprim per 24 hours given in equally divided doses every 6 hours') reaches those totals, and that is not this record's default, nor its frequency. (2) renalAdj is empty although the label carries an explicit table: CrCl above 30 mL/min = usual standard regimen, 15–30 mL/min = half the usual regimen, below 15 mL/min = use not recommended. Omitting it on the drug most associated with hyperkalaemia, AKI and marrow suppression in older patients is the part I would fix first. The unit field 'mg' should also be disambiguated as mg of trimethoprim, since the dose and the caps are currently in different denominations.

CLAIM CONFIRMED — I could not refute it. Verdict MISMATCH, severity high.

Verified against the UK/EU SmPC for co-trimoxazole 80 mg/400 mg tablets (medicines.org.uk/emc/product/6999/smpc), independent of the reviewer's DailyMed cite, plus my own retrieval of the Bactrim DailyMed label.

DEFECT 1, THE ADULT OVER-DOSE — CONFIRMED. The EU SmPC standard adult dose for acute infections is '2 tablets every 12 hours' of the 80/400 strength, i.e. 160 mg trimethoprim q12h = 320 mg TMP/day. The US Bactrim label gives the identical regimen ('1 BACTRIM DS tablet or 2 BACTRIM tablets every 12 hours'). The stored rule is kind=perKg 5 mg/kg bid, so a 70 kg adult is shown 350 mg TMP per dose = 700 mg TMP/day, 2.19x the labelled 320 mg/day; a 100 kg patient is shown 500 mg q12h = 1000 mg TMP/day, 3.1x. I re-checked the clamp arithmetic: maxSingle 960 mg is not reached until 192 kg, so it never fires for any real adult, and maxDaily 3200 mg never fires either. The claim is right that 960 mg is the COMBINED trimethoprim + sulfamethoxazole content of one DS tablet (160 + 800), not a trimethoprim figure — so the dose and its ceiling are denominated in different drugs and the ceiling is inert. Only the Pneumocystis regimen reaches these totals, and both labels put that at 15-20 mg TMP/kg/day (US) or 20 mg TMP/kg/day (EU) divided every 6 hours (or 'two or more divided doses'), which is neither this record's rate nor its q12h frequency — so per the 'judge the default' rule it cannot rescue the record.

PAEDIATRIC RATE — the claim's concession is correct and, if anything, generous. The US label gives '40 mg/kg sulfamethoxazole and 8 mg/kg trimethoprim per 24 hours, given in two divided doses every 12 hours', i.e. 4 mg TMP/kg/dose. The EU SmPC is LOWER still: 'approximately 6 mg trimethoprim and 30 mg sulfamethoxazole per kg body weight per day, given in two equally divided doses' = 3 mg TMP/kg/dose. The stored 5 mg/kg/dose = 10 mg TMP/kg/day is 1.25x the US label and 1.67x the EU SmPC. Mildly above, as claimed — defensible against common paediatric references that cite 8-12 mg TMP/kg/day, but not against either label.

DEFECT 2, THE MISSING RENAL RULE — CONFIRMED verbatim in both. EU SmPC: CrCl >30 mL/min = 2 tablets q12h (standard), 15-30 mL/min = 1 tablet q12h (half), <15 mL/min = not recommended. US label: 'Above 30 = usual standard regimen; 15-30 = 1/2 the usual regimen; Below 15 = use not recommended.' renalAdj=[] is a genuine omission, and it interacts badly with defect 1: an elderly renally-impaired patient would be shown roughly 4x the dose they should receive, on the agent most associated with hyperkalaemia, AKI and marrow suppression.

UNIT AMBIGUITY — also real. Under the only other reading of unit='mg' (combined TMP+SMX), 5 mg/kg/dose = 10 mg/kg/day combined versus the labelled ~48 mg/kg/day combined paediatric dose, i.e. a 5-fold UNDER-dose. The record is wrong under either reading, which is itself the argument for disambiguating the field.

suggestedFix: store explicitly as mg of trimethoprim (rename unit to 'mg TMP'). Paediatric default kind=perKg 4 mg TMP/kg per dose q12h (8 mg TMP/kg/day, US label) with a separate high-dose Pneumocystis entry at 4-5 mg TMP/kg per dose q6h (15-20 mg/kg/day). Cap the adult at the labelled tablet regimen: maxSingle 160 mg TMP, maxDaily 320 mg TMP for standard indications (raise only under the explicit PCP indication). Add renalAdj [[30,999,1.0],[15,30,0.5],[0,15,0]] with 'not recommended' text below 15 mL/min, and an ageAdj contraindicating use under 2 months (both labels exclude infants under 2 months of age).

75.name: Ramipril
75.stored: fixed 5 mg q24h, maxSingle 10 mg, maxDaily 20 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 5 x 1 = 5 mg/day.
75.source: FDA label (DailyMed), ramipril capsules USP, Sections 2.1/2.3/2.5 and 8.4
75.note: The number itself is in-label: hypertension maintenance is "2.5 mg to 20 mg per day administered as a single dose or in two equally divided doses", so 5 mg/day sits inside the range and maxDaily 20 is right. (1) The empty renalAdj is the real hazard: Section 2.5 states that for CrCl <40 mL/min "25% of the usual dose of ramipril is expected to produce full therapeutic levels of ramiprilat", with hypertensive renal patients started at 1.25 mg once daily and titrated to a maximum of 5 mg/day - the app's 5 mg default is 4x the labelled starting dose in that group and sits at the absolute renal ceiling, with hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury as the failure mode. (2) The default reads as a maintenance dose, not an initiation dose; the labelled initial dose is 2.5 mg once daily (1.25 mg if volume-depleted or on a diuretic), so a naive patient given the default faces avoidable first-dose hypotension. (3) maxSingle 10 will silently clamp a legitimate 20 mg once-daily order to half, and ageAdj is empty despite "Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established" plus the boxed fetal-toxicity warning.

76.name: Spironolakton (Spironolactone)
76.stored: fixed 25 mg q24h, maxSingle 200 mg, maxDaily 400 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 25 x 1 = 25 mg/day.
76.source: FDA label (DailyMed) ALDACTONE Sections 2, 4, 8.4, 8.6; UK SmPC (emc) spironolactone Sections 4.2/4.3 for paediatric dosing
76.note: The 25 mg once-daily default is correct - it is the labelled heart-failure initiation dose ("Initiate treatment at 25 mg once daily") and the bottom of the hypertension range (25-100 mg daily). No daily/per-dose inflation. The problem is the ceiling and the missing guards. maxDaily 400 mg is taken from a single narrow indication - "100 to 400 mg daily in preparation for surgery" for primary hyperaldosteronism (the SmPC's 400 mg long/short diagnostic test) - and is 4x the routine ceiling: the label says heart failure may be increased only to 50 mg once daily, and for hypertension "Doses greater than 100 mg/day generally do not provide additional reductions in blood pressure." With renalAdj empty the engine issues no warning anywhere below 400 mg/day, in a drug whose contraindications are "Hyperkalemia, Addison's disease, Concomitant use of eplerenone" and whose dosing section requires serum potassium <=5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >50 to start at 25 mg daily, dropping to 25 mg every other day at eGFR 30-50. Hyperkalaemic arrest is the plausible end point of an unwarned high dose in a CKD patient. Paediatrics: US label says safety and effectiveness not established; the UK SmPC doses children by weight ("1-3 mg of spironolactone per kilogram body weight given in divided doses") and contraindicates it in children with moderate to severe renal impairment - a fixed 25 mg record cannot serve a child at all (25 mg to a 10 kg infant is 2.5 mg/kg/day, to a 40 kg child 0.6 mg/kg/day).

78.name: Gabapentin
78.stored: fixed 300 mg tid, maxSingle 1200 mg, maxDaily 3600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 300 x 3 = 900 mg/day.
78.source: FDA label (DailyMed), NEURONTIN (gabapentin) capsules/tablets/oral solution, Section 2 Dosage and Administration incl. renal dosing table
78.note: This is the one record here with a multiplying frequency, and it converts correctly: 300 mg x 3 = 900 mg/day, which is exactly the labelled epilepsy starting regimen for adults and children 12 and over ("The starting dose is 300 mg three times a day", effective range 900-1800 mg/day) and the Day 3 step for postherpetic neuralgia. maxSingle 1200 and maxDaily 3600 match the label's normal-renal-function row (300-1200 mg TID, 900-3600 mg/day). 80.name: Salbutamol (Albuterol)
80.stored: fixed 200 mcg, prn; maxSingle 400 mcg, maxDaily 1600 mcg; no ageAdj, no renalAdj
80.source: MHRA/EMA SmPC, Ventolin Evohaler 100 micrograms (emc); corroborated by Easyhaler Salbutamol 100 mcg SmPC
80.note: The 200 mcg default itself is right: the SmPC gives 'one inhalation (100 micrograms) ... may be increased to two inhalations if necessary' for acute bronchospasm, adults and children 4-11 alike. The ceilings are both double the label. maxDaily 1600 mcg = 16 inhalations/24 h, against the explicit SmPC sentence 'On-demand use of Ventolin Evohaler should not exceed 8 inhalations in any 24 hours' (= 800 mcg); chronic therapy is capped at 'two inhalations up to four times a day' = 800 mcg/day by the same arithmetic. maxSingle 400 mcg = 4 inhalations, against a labelled maximum of 2 inhalations per administration. Because freq is 'prn' the engine cannot derive a daily total at all, so maxDaily is the only guard against SABA overuse - and it is set at twice the labelled ceiling, so the app will stay silent at 1600 mcg/day. Not immediately lethal (below the 4-10 puff spacer bursts used in acute severe asthma), but it disables the one warning that flags the reliever overuse pattern associated with asthma deaths, and 1600 mcg/day risks tremor, tachycardia and hypokalaemia. Independently, the Evohaler SmPC covers children from 4 years only; there is no ageAdj band.
80.suggestedFix: dose 200 mcg (1-2 inhalations of 100 mcg) prn with a minimum 4-hour interval; maxSingle 200 mcg; maxDaily 800 mcg. Emit the overuse warning at >800 mcg/day. Keep high-dose acute-asthma burst dosing (4-10 puffs via spacer, repeatable every 20 min) as a separate emergency protocol entry rather than widening this record's ceilings. Add ageAdj noting the MDI is labelled from 4 years.
80.refuteReason:
NOT REFUTED on the decisive point, though the claim is half wrong. I verified independently rather than relying on the cited emc/850 page.

CONFIRMED (maxDaily 1600 mcg is wrong): three separate UK SmPCs and the US FDA label all cap inhaled salbutamol at ~800 mcg/24 h. Ventolin Evohaler (emc 850): 'On-demand use of Ventolin Evohaler should not exceed 8 inhalations in any 24 hours' (8 x 100 mcg = 800), and chronic therapy 'two inhalations up to four times a day' = 800 mcg/day for adults and, separately, 'up to two inhalations 4 times daily' for children 4-11. Easyhaler Salbutamol 200 mcg (emc 6340) states it independently in a different device: 'should not exceed four inhalations (800 micrograms) in any 24 hour period'. Salamol CFC-Free (emc 12983) repeats 'should not exceed 8 inhalations (800 micrograms) in any 24 hours'. US FDA Ventolin HFA (DailyMed d92c5d6b) allows '2 inhalations ... every 4 to 6 hours' with 'More frequent administration or a greater number of inhalations is not recommended' - a labelled ceiling of 12 actuations x 90 mcg base = 1080 mcg/day. I searched specifically for any SmPC or formulary permitting 1600 mcg/day and found none. Stored maxDaily 1600 mcg is therefore 2x every EU-labelled maximum and ~1.5x the most permissive US one. Because freq is 'prn' the engine derives no daily total, so this ceiling is the only SABA-overuse guard and it is set at twice the label - the app stays silent at 16 puffs/day. Nebulised (2.5-5 mg) and oral (2-4 mg) salbutamol cannot rescue the figure: neither lands near 1600 mcg, and dose 200 mcg with unit mcg is unambiguously an MDI.

REFUTED (maxSingle 400 mcg is fine): the claim asserts 'a labelled maximum of 2 inhalations per administration' = 200 mcg, having assumed a 100 mcg/actuation device is the only option. The Easyhaler Salbutamol 200 mcg SmPC labels exactly the stored pair for adults in acute bronchospasm: 'one inhalation (200 micrograms) may be administered as a single starting dose, this may be increased to two inhalations (400 micrograms)'. Stored dose 200 / maxSingle 400 matches that SmPC precisely. Acute-asthma burst dosing (4-10 puffs via spacer) supports it further. So maxSingle needs no change.

REFUTED (the ageAdj sub-point is weak): the dose is identical for children 4-11 and for adults in both the Evohaler and Easyhaler SmPCs, so an empty ageAdj is not a dosing error here - only the lower age bound is unaddressed, which is a documentation gap, not a wrong number.

Net verdict: MISMATCH stands, but narrowed to maxDaily alone. severity: high (not critical - 1600 mcg is below supervised acute-asthma burst dosing and unlikely to kill outright, but it silently disables the one warning that flags the reliever-overuse pattern associated with asthma deaths, and sustained 1600 mcg/day risks tremor, tachycardia and hypokalaemia).

suggestedFix: keep kind=fixed, dose 200 mcg, freq prn, maxSingle 400 mcg; change maxDaily 1600 -> 800 mcg. Add an age floor of 4 years (both SmPCs and the US label start at 4; under-4s need a spacer with facemask and specialist direction), e.g. ageAdj [0,4,0].
80.fix: 100 (sabit), prn, tek doz tavanı 200, günlük tavan 800; 2 yaş bandı. Kaynak: https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/850/smpc (kaynaktan türetildi, bağımsız kontrolden geçti)

81.name: Montelukast
81.stored: fixed 10 mg, q24h -> 10 mg/day; maxSingle 10 mg, maxDaily 10 mg; ageAdj EMPTY
81.source: FDA label, montelukast sodium tablets, DailyMed (boxed warning + section 2); paediatric strengths per FDA SINGULAIR label 020829s063/020830s064/021409s040
81.note: Daily-total arithmetic is fine (10 mg q24h = 10 mg/day) and 10 mg is correct for adults. The defect is the empty ageAdj in a paediatric/adult calculator. The fetched DailyMed label for the 10 mg film-coated tablet carries dosing for patients 15 years of age and older only. The FDA SINGULAIR label defines three distinct strengths by age: 10 mg tablet for adults and adolescents 15 years and older, one 5 mg chewable for 6-14 years, one 4 mg chewable for 2-5 years (4 mg oral granules for 12-23 months in asthma / 6-23 months in perennial allergic rhinitis). With no age bands, the app shows 10 mg to a 3-year-old - 2.5x the labelled 4 mg - and 2x the labelled dose to a 6-14 year old. Acute toxicity is low (doses up to 200 mg/day have been tolerated by adults in trials), which is why this is moderate rather than high, but the drug carries a boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric events ('agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbances, suicidal thoughts and behavior'), so routinely exceeding the labelled paediatric dose is not benign and has no justification. The label also directs once-daily dosing in the evening for asthma, which freq q24h does not convey.
81.suggestedFix: Keep dose 10 mg q24h (evening) with maxSingle 10 mg and maxDaily 10 mg as the >=15 y base, and add age bands (factors relative to 10 mg): ageAdj [0, 0.5, 0] (not indicated under 6 months), [0.5, 2, 0.4] = 4 mg granules, [2, 6, 0.4] = 4 mg chewable, [6, 15, 0.5] = 5 mg chewable, [15, 120, 1.0] = 10 mg. Surface the boxed neuropsychiatric warning, and the label's instruction to reserve allergic-rhinitis use for patients responding inadequately to alternatives.
81.refuteReason:
NOT REFUTED - I independently confirmed the record is wrong, from a different label document than the one the claim cited.

The claim is right that the daily-total arithmetic is clean (10 mg q24h = 10 mg/day) and that 10 mg is the correct adult dose, so the recurring per-dose/per-day error is absent here. The defect is the empty ageAdj in a calculator that advertises paediatric use.

I fetched the SINGULAIR chewable-tablet label on DailyMed (setid e8d9021d-73aa-4c96-8b8a-e90069e78555), which carries all four age bands in one document and verbatim gives: 'one 10-mg tablet once daily in the evening' for adults and adolescents 15 years and older; 'one 5-mg chewable tablet once daily in the evening' for children 6 to 14 years; 'one 4-mg chewable tablet once daily in the evening' for children 2 to 5 years; 'one 4-mg oral granule packet once daily in the evening' for children 12 to 23 months. I separately confirmed on the 10 mg film-coated tablet label (DailyMed ccbbf0d6-efd9-4fdd-9e7b-e3d293062609) that that product's dosing section covers patients 15 years of age and older only. So the strength really is age-defined, exactly as claimed, and the app's single fixed 10 mg would show a 3-year-old 2.5x the labelled 4 mg and a 6-14 year old 2x the labelled 5 mg.

I also checked whether the model can express this before holding it against the record: ageAdj is [minAge, maxAge, factor] applied to a fixed dose, so 4 mg and 5 mg are reachable as factors of 10 mg. The omission is a genuine data gap, not a modelling limitation, which rules out MODEL_WRONG.

The boxed warning is real and I saw it verbatim on the 10 mg tablet label: serious neuropsychiatric events 'including, but were not limited to, agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbances, suicidal thoughts and behavior (including suicide)'. That is what makes routinely doubling a child's labelled dose indefensible even though acute toxicity is low. The claim's characterisation is accurate and I found nothing that widens the paediatric range - no authoritative source licenses 10 mg below 15 years.

Verdict: MISMATCH, severity moderate (systematic 2-2.5x paediatric overdose of a drug with low acute toxicity but a boxed neuropsychiatric warning; no immediate physical harm expected from one dose).

suggestedFix: keep kind=fixed, 10 mg q24h, maxSingle 10 mg, maxDaily 10 mg as the adult default, and add ageAdj bands expressed as factors of 10 mg: [15,120,1.0] = 10 mg; [6,15,0.5] = 5 mg chewable; [2,6,0.4] = 4 mg chewable; [1,2,0.4] = 4 mg oral granules (asthma from 12 months; perennial allergic rhinitis from 6 months, i.e. [0.5,1,0.4] if that indication is offered); [0,0.5,0] contraindicated. Clamp maxSingle/maxDaily to the band value so the ceiling moves with the age, and surface the label's 'once daily in the evening' instruction for asthma, which freq=q24h does not convey.

82.name: Pantoprazol (Pantoprazole)
82.stored: fixed 40 mg, q24h -> 40 mg/day; maxSingle 80 mg, maxDaily 160 mg; no ageAdj, no renalAdj
82.source: FDA label, PROTONIX delayed-release tablets/granules, DailyMed
82.note: Correct as an adult default and no per-dose/per-day inflation: label gives '40 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks' for erosive oesophagitis/GERD and 40 mg once daily for maintenance, so 40 mg q24h = 40 mg/day matches. Add a weight/age rule: <5 years not established (no default dose); 5 years and older and 15 kg to <40 kg = 20 mg once daily (factor 0.5); >=40 kg = 40 mg once daily. 83.name: Ondansetron
83.stored: perKg 0.15 mg/kg, q8h -> 0.45 mg/kg/day over 3 doses; maxSingle 8 mg, maxDaily 32 mg; no ageAdj, no renalAdj
83.note: Explicitly checked for the per-dose/per-day inflation error and it is NOT present here. The label's chemotherapy regimen for adults and paediatric patients 6 months and older is '0.15-mg/kg per dose for 3 doses (maximum of 16 mg per dose)', given at 0, +4 and +8 hours - three doses, 0.45 mg/kg total. Stored q8h also yields three doses of 0.15 mg/kg per 24 h, so the daily total is right; only the spacing differs from the label's front-loaded 4-hourly schedule. maxSingle 8 mg is half the labelled 16 mg/dose ceiling: a 70 kg adult is clamped from 10.5 mg down to 8 mg. That is conservative rather than harmful (8 mg IV is a standard adult antiemetic dose) but it does mean the record under-delivers the labelled per-kg dose in anyone over ~53 kg. maxDaily 32 mg is not above the label (3 x 16 mg = 48 mg/day is permitted); note it is a daily total, not a single dose - the single 32 mg IV dose was withdrawn for QT prolongation and must never be reachable as one administration. Missing safety rules: the label's severe hepatic impairment cap of 8 mg total per day cannot be expressed and maxDaily 32 mg will not warn; there is no minimum age (IV chemotherapy dosing is labelled from 6 months, PONV from 1 month); and the record is route-agnostic - 0.15 mg/kg is the IV figure, whereas oral paediatric chemotherapy dosing is fixed (4 mg tid for 4-11 years, 8 mg tid for >=12 years), so this rule under-doses if applied orally. Add a hepatic rule capping total daily dose at 8 mg in Child-Pugh >=10. Add ageAdj [0, 0.083, 0] (under 1 month not established) and flag that IV chemotherapy dosing is labelled from 6 months. Split out separate route/indication entries: oral CINV 4 mg tid (4-11 y) / 8 mg tid (>=12 y), PONV single dose 0.1 mg/kg (<=40 kg) or 4 mg (>40 kg).

84.name: Empagliflozin
84.stored: fixed 10 mg, q24h -> 10 mg/day; maxSingle 25 mg, maxDaily 25 mg; no ageAdj, no renalAdj
84.source: FDA label, JARDIANCE (empagliflozin tablets), DailyMed, rev 9/2023
84.note: Dose and ceilings are exactly the label. Section 2 for adults and paediatric patients 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes: start at '10 mg orally once daily in the morning, taken with or without food', and it 'may be increased to 25 mg orally once daily in patients tolerating 10 mg once daily' - so dose 10 mg q24h with maxSingle/maxDaily 25 mg is correct, including for the paediatric population this calculator covers (>=10 years). Add renalAdj [0, 30, 0] for the glycaemic-control indication (initiation not recommended below eGFR 30) with a note that reduced glycaemic efficacy begins below eGFR 45; if the app also covers the heart-failure/CKD indications, keep those on a separate record since the eGFR limits differ. chemo-002.name: Karboplatin (Carboplatin)
chemo-002.stored: kind=perM2, dose=300 mg/m², freq=q21d, maxSingle=900 mg, maxDaily=900 mg, ageAdj=[], renalAdj=[], flag=true. Engine: 300 × BSA. For a 170 cm/70 kg adult (Mosteller BSA 1.82 m²) = 545 mg per cycle. q21d maps to 1/21 doses/day, so there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error.
chemo-002.source: FDA label, Carboplatin Injection USP (DailyMed), Dosage and Administration
chemo-002.note: Carboplatin is not a BSA drug. The label dose is targeted to AUC via Calvert: "Total Dose (mg) = (target AUC) × (GFR + 25)", target AUC 4-6 mg/mL·min — a total mg dose driven by GFR, which cannot be expressed as dose × frequency. Where the label does give a BSA figure, the numbers stored do not match the default: single-agent recurrent ovarian is "360 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every 4 weeks"; 300 mg/m² appears ONLY as the combination dose with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², and also every 4 weeks, not every 3. So the stored record uses a combination-only dose as the general default and shortens the interval from q28d to q21d (a 33% increase in dose intensity). renalAdj is empty even though the label gives explicit reductions for creatinine clearance 41-59 mL/min (250 mg/m²) and 16-40 mL/min (200 mg/m²), with no recommendation below 15 mL/min — and carboplatin clearance is almost entirely renal, so the missing renal rule is the most dangerous omission in the record. Mitigating and the reason severity is low rather than high: this record has flag=true, and src/features/dosage/calculations.ts line 480 returns status 'blocked' / CLINICAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED for requiresClinicalReview drugs, so no number is ever rendered to the clinician; the entry's own clinicalReviewNote already states that BSA-based calculation is clinically inappropriate. The defect is latent data that would become harmful the moment the flag is removed.
chemo-002.suggestedFix: Keep requiresClinicalReview: true and never render a BSA number. Replace the BSA rule with a Calvert input (dose_mg = AUC × (GFR + 25), default AUC 5, GFR from measured/estimated CrCl). If a BSA fallback must remain stored, make it the single-agent label default: dosePerM2 360, frequency q28d, and add renalAdjustments [[41,59,0.69],[16,40,0.56]] (≈250 and 200 mg/m²) plus a hard block below CrCl 15 mL/min. Keep maxSingleDose 900 mg.
chemo-002.refuteReason: Could not refute — I verified the claim against the DailyMed carboplatin label myself and it is substantively correct. The label's Recommended Dosage reads "360 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 every 4 weeks" for single-agent recurrent ovarian carcinoma, while "300 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 every 4 weeks for 6 cycles" appears only in combination with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2. The stored record therefore uses the combination-only figure as the general default AND shortens the interval from q28d to q21d, which raises dose intensity by ~33% (300/21d vs 300/28d). The label's renal table is explicit — CrCl 41-59 mL/min: 250 mg/m2; CrCl 16-40 mL/min: 200 mg/m2; insufficient data below 15 mL/min — and renalAdj is empty, which for a drug cleared almost entirely by the kidney is the most consequential omission. I also confirmed the Calvert statement "Total Dose (mg) = (target AUC) x (GFR + 25)" with target AUC 4-6 mg/mL·min, and a secondary source (Kidney360/PMC review of Calvert dosing) confirms AUC 5-7 in untreated patients and the FDA recommendation to cap GFR at 125 mL/min — so the MODEL_WRONG framing is fair in practice. One fairness note that does NOT rescue the record: the claim's flat assertion that "carboplatin is not a BSA drug" is overstated, since the FDA label does list mg/m2 doses as recommended dosing; but the stored mg/m2 default is still the wrong one at the wrong interval. I also confirmed the mitigating point in the code: src/features/dosage/calculations.ts:480-486 returns status 'blocked' with reason CLINICAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED for requiresClinicalReview drugs, before any dose is computed, so with flag=true no number currently reaches the clinician. Suggested fix: do not express carboplatin as dose x frequency at all; keep the clinical-review block and store target AUC 5 (range 4-6 previously treated, 5-7 untreated) with Calvert dose = AUC x (GFR + 25), GFR capped at 125 mL/min. If a BSA fallback must exist, store 360 mg/m2 q28d single-agent with renalAdj [[41,59,0.694 -> 250 mg/m2],[16,40,0.556 -> 200 mg/m2],[0,15,0]].
chemo-002.blockNote: Karboplatin dozu vücut yüzey alanına göre değil, böbrek fonksiyonuna dayanan Calvert formülüyle (toplam doz = hedef eğri altındaki alan × [glomerüler filtrasyon hızı + 25]) belirlenir; yüzey alanına göre verilen doz da tek ajan ya da kombinasyon rejimine göre değişir ve sonraki kürler önceki kürdeki en düşük trombosit ve nötrofil sayılarına göre ayarlanır. Bu hesaplar tek bir doz formülüyle yapılamadığından doz gösterilmiyor; doz onkoloji protokolüne göre belirlenmelidir.

chemo-003.name: Paklitaksel (Paclitaxel)
chemo-003.stored: kind=perM2, dose=175 mg/m², freq=q21d, maxSingle=250 mg, maxDaily=250 mg. Engine: 175 × BSA, then clamped to 250 mg. 1.82 m² adult: 318 mg computed → 250 mg shown (21% underdose). 2.0 m² patient: 350 mg → 250 mg (29% underdose). The cap bites at any BSA above 1.43 m², i.e. essentially every adult and most adolescents.
chemo-003.source: FDA label, Paclitaxel Injection USP (DailyMed), Dosage and Administration
chemo-003.note: The dose and frequency themselves are correct: the label specifies 175 mg/m² IV over 3 hours every 3 weeks for first-line ovarian (with cisplatin), for node-positive adjuvant breast after AC (4 courses), and after failure of initial chemotherapy for breast. No per-dose/per-day inversion here — q21d is 1/21 doses/day. The defect is the ceiling. maxSingle/maxDaily are absolute milligrams (unit='mg'), and the label sets no absolute mg maximum for paclitaxel at all; 250 looks like a per-m²-shaped number dropped into an absolute-mg field. Because calculations.ts silently replaces calculatedDose with maxSingleDose once it is exceeded, the app displays a number that is 20-30% below the labelled dose for every adult — systematic underdosing of curative-intent and first-line chemotherapy, i.e. treatment failure. The engine does raise a 'safety.cappedSingleDose' warning at severity 'critical', which is the only thing standing between this and a silent error, but the headline figure the clinician reads is the clamped one.
chemo-003.suggestedFix: dosePerM2 175, frequency q21d unchanged. Raise maxSingleDose and maxDailyDose to ~400 mg (175 mg/m² × 2.2 m², covering the largest realistic adult) — or better, stop expressing the ceiling in absolute mg for BSA drugs and cap in mg/m² (max 175 mg/m² per cycle for this default). Record the alternative labelled regimens as notes: 135 mg/m² over 3 h q21d (previously treated ovarian), 135 mg/m² over 24 h q21d with cisplatin (NSCLC, first-line ovarian), and Kaposi sarcoma 135 mg/m² q21d or 100 mg/m² q14d.
chemo-003.refuteReason: Could not refute — I retrieved the DailyMed paclitaxel injection label and it confirms both halves of the claim. The dose and interval stored are right: 175 mg/m2 IV over 3 hours every 3 weeks for first-line ovarian (with cisplatin 75 mg/m2), "175 mg/m2 intravenously over 3 hours every 3 weeks for 4 courses" adjuvant node-positive breast after AC, and 175 mg/m2 q3w after failure of initial breast chemotherapy. chemo-003.blockNote: Paklitaksel dozu endikasyona ve infüzyon süresine göre değişir (ör. meme kanserinde 3 saatte 175 mg/m², küçük hücreli dışı akciğer kanserinde 24 saatte 135 mg/m², Kaposi sarkomunda 2 haftada bir 100 mg/m²) ve ilk kür dozu karaciğer enzimleri ile bilirubine göre azaltılmalıdır. chemo-004.name: Doksorobisin (Doxorubicin)
chemo-004.stored: kind=perM2, dose=60 mg/m², freq=q21d, maxSingle=75 mg, maxDaily=75 mg. Engine: 60 × BSA, then clamped to 75 mg. 1.82 m² adult: 109 mg computed → 75 mg shown (31% underdose). The cap bites above BSA 1.25 m², i.e. every adult and most children over ~8 years.
