chemo-005.name: 5-Florourasil (5-Fluorouracil)
chemo-005.stored: kind=perM2, dose=500 mg/m², freq=q24h, maxSingle=1000 mg, maxDaily=1000 mg. q24h = 1 dose/day, so the engine presents 500 mg/m² EVERY DAY with no cycle limit: 909 mg/day for a 1.82 m² adult, i.e. 3,500 mg/m² per week. maxDaily 1000 mg does not fire at that BSA, so no warning is shown.
chemo-005.source: FDA label, Fluorouracil Injection (DailyMed), section 2 Recommended Dosage
chemo-005.note: This is the recurring per-dose/per-day inversion, in its frequency form. 500 mg/m² is a genuine labelled 5-FU bolus dose, but it is a WEEKLY one: the colorectal bolus regimen is "500 mg/m² by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, and 36 in 8-week cycles", and the breast regimen is "500 mg/m² or 600 mg/m² intravenously on Days 1 and 8 every 28 days for 6 cycles". The label's other regimens are infusional and structurally different (colorectal and pancreatic: 400 mg/m² bolus Day 1 then 2400-3000 mg/m² as a 46-hour continuous infusion every two weeks; gastric: 200-1000 mg/m² as a 24-hour continuous infusion within a platinum regimen). I checked specifically and the label describes no regimen of 500 mg/m² once daily continuously. Applying q24h on top of a weekly bolus number multiplies weekly exposure roughly sevenfold (3,500 vs 500 mg/m²/week). Bolus 5-FU repeated daily without a cycle break produces severe and potentially fatal myelosuppression, mucositis and diarrhoea within days; the hazard is amplified in undiagnosed DPD deficiency, for which the label directs DPYD genotyping before treatment and states that no dose has been proven safe in complete DPD deficiency. The record's own productInfo already describes the correct regimens ("Bolus: 400-600 mg/m². Sürekli infüzyon: 2400 mg/m² 46 saatte"), so the dosageFormula contradicts the monograph text shipped alongside it.
chemo-005.suggestedFix: Change frequency from q24h to q7d and keep dosePerM2 500 (Roswell-Park-type weekly bolus, 6 doses in an 8-week cycle) — that alone removes the 7x error. Better: set requiresClinicalReview: true as with carboplatin, because the clinically dominant regimens (mFOLFOX6/FOLFIRI/de Gramont: 400 mg/m² bolus + 2400 mg/m² over 46 h q14d) are a loading dose plus an infusion and cannot be expressed as one dose × frequency. Drop the flat 1000 mg ceilings (they neither reflect the label nor fire in time); add a blocking DPYD/DPD-deficiency check and an explicit cycle-length field.
chemo-005.refuteReason: Could not refute — this is the most dangerous of the six and I confirmed it directly. The DailyMed fluorouracil injection label lists, for colorectal: infusional "400 mg/m2 by intravenous bolus on Day 1, followed by 2400 mg/m2 to 3000 mg/m2 intravenously as a continuous infusion over 46 hours every two weeks", and bolus "500 mg/m2 by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, and 36 in 8-week cycles"; for breast "500 mg/m2 or 600 mg/m2 intravenously on Days 1 and 8 every 28 days for 6 cycles"; gastric 200-1000 mg/m2 as a 24-hour continuous infusion; pancreatic 400 mg/m2 bolus then 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours q2w. I asked the label specifically whether any regimen gives 500 mg/m2 once daily on consecutive days and the answer is no — the 500 mg/m2 bolus is a WEEKLY dose. The stored q24h therefore applies a weekly bolus number every single day: 909 mg/day at BSA 1.82 m2, about 3,500 mg/m2/week against a labelled 500 mg/m2/week, roughly sevenfold weekly exposure, and maxDaily 1000 mg does not fire so no warning is raised. I went looking for a daily regimen that might rescue the entry and found only the historical package-insert regimen of 12 mg/kg IV once daily for four successive days with the daily dose not to exceed 800 mg — which is time-limited to 4 days, followed by alternate-day reduced dosing, and capped below the 909 mg this record would display; it does not make open-ended daily 500 mg/m2 defensible. Repeated daily bolus 5-FU without a cycle break causes severe myelosuppression, mucositis and diarrhoea within days, amplified in DPD deficiency — the label directs DPYD testing before initiation and says to avoid fluorouracil in complete DPD deficiency. The record's own productInfo already describes the correct bolus/infusional regimens, so the formula contradicts the monograph shipped with it. Suggested fix: 500 mg/m2 with freq q7d (weekly bolus, Days 1/8/15/22/29/36 of 8-week cycles), or model the standard infusional regimen as 400 mg/m2 bolus q14d plus a separate 2400 mg/m2/46h infusion entry; add a DPYD pre-treatment check and clinical-review flag, and set ceilings from the regimen rather than a flat 1000 mg.
chemo-005.blockNote: 5-FU şemaları tanıya göre değişir ve en sık kullanılanlar 400 mg/m2 bolus ardından 46 saatlik sürekli infüzyon şeklindedir; haftalık bolus şeması ise 8 haftalık kür içinde ara verilerek uygulanır. Tek bir doz ve uygulama sıklığı bu şemaları karşılayamadığı, ayrıca tedavi öncesi DPYD/DPD eksikliği değerlendirmesi gerektiği için doz gösterilmemektedir.

chemo-006.name: Gemsitabin (Gemcitabine)
chemo-006.stored: kind=perM2, dose=1000 mg/m², freq=q7d, maxSingle=1500 mg, maxDaily=1500 mg. Engine: 1000 × BSA, then clamped to 1500 mg. 1.82 m² adult: 1818 mg computed → 1500 mg shown (17.5% underdose). 2.0 m² patient: 2000 mg → 1500 mg (25% underdose). The cap bites above BSA 1.5 m², i.e. every adult.
chemo-006.source: FDA label, Gemcitabine for Injection (DailyMed), section 2 Dosage and Administration
chemo-006.note: The dose and the weekly frequency are defensible as a default: the label's pancreatic single-agent regimen is 1000 mg/m² over 30 minutes weekly for 7 weeks, then a one-week rest, then weekly on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; ovarian is 1000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle with carboplatin; NSCLC is 1000 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles with cisplatin. q7d = 1/7 doses/day in the engine, so there is no per-dose/per-day multiplication error. The defect is again the absolute-mg ceiling: I checked the label specifically and it specifies no absolute maximum dose in milligrams — dosing is expressed only in mg/m². A flat 1500 mg cap therefore under-doses every adult by 17-25%, and the shortfall grows with body size, which is the opposite of what a BSA rule is for. What the record is missing instead of a mg cap are the label's real safety brakes: dose reduction or omission by absolute neutrophil and platelet count on each treatment day, and the prolonged-infusion hazard (infusions beyond 60 minutes increase toxicity).
chemo-006.suggestedFix: dosePerM2 1000, frequency q7d unchanged. Raise maxSingleDose/maxDailyDose to ~2200 mg (1000 mg/m² × 2.2 m²), or 2750 mg if the record is also meant to cover the 1250 mg/m² breast/NSCLC regimens; ideally cap in mg/m² rather than mg. Add the cycle structure (weekly ×7, one week rest, then Days 1/8/15 of 28-day cycles) and a day-of-treatment ANC/platelet check, and warn that infusion duration must not exceed 30-60 minutes.
chemo-006.refuteReason: Could not refute — I retrieved the DailyMed gemcitabine label and it supports the claim on every point. Dosing is expressed exclusively in mg/m2: pancreatic "1000 mg/m2 over 30 minutes once weekly for the first 7 weeks, then one week rest, then once weekly for 3 weeks" (of each 28-day cycle); ovarian "1000 mg/m2 over 30 minutes on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle" with carboplatin; NSCLC "1000 mg/m2 over 30 minutes on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle" or 1250 mg/m2 on Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; breast 1250 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8. So dose=1000 mg/m2 at q7d is a defensible default and there is no per-dose/per-day inversion. I checked the label specifically for an absolute milligram maximum and it states none. The flat 1500 mg ceiling therefore has no label basis, and because calculations.ts lines 560-571 clamp calculatedDose to maxSingleDose, a 1.82 m2 adult is shown 1500 mg instead of 1818 mg (17.5% under) and a 2.0 m2 patient 1500 mg instead of 2000 mg (25% under) — the shortfall grows with body size, defeating the purpose of a BSA rule. The label's real brakes, both absent from the record, are the day-of-treatment modification by absolute granulocyte and platelet count (100% dose at >=1500 and >=100,000; 50% of the full dose at 1000-1499 or 75,000-99,999; hold below that), and the infusion-duration hazard: "Prolongation of the infusion time beyond 60 minutes ... resulted in an increased incidence of clinically significant hypotension, severe flu-like symptoms, myelosuppression, and asthenia." Suggested fix: dose=1000 mg/m2 q7d (with the 7-weeks-then-1-week-rest and Day 1/8/15 cycle structure documented); remove the 1500 mg absolute ceiling or raise it to a non-binding value (e.g. 2600 mg, ~1250 mg/m2 at 2.1 m2); add ANC/platelet-based dose modification and a 30-60 minute infusion-duration constraint.
chemo-006.fix: 1000 (m2 başına), q7d, tek doz tavanı 3000, günlük tavan 3000; 2 yaş bandı. Kaynak: Gemsitabin etiketi (DailyMed, Hospira/Fresenius): 1000 mg/m2, mutlak mg tavanı yok. 3000 mg tavan klinik bir sınır değil, 3,0 m2 karşılığı girdi güvencesidir; gerçekçi hastada devreye girmez.

supp-001.name: D Vitamini (Kolekalsiferol / Vitamin D3)
supp-001.stored: kind=fixed, dose=1000 units, freq=q24h, maxSingle=10000, maxDaily=10000, ageAdj=[]. Daily total = 1000 units/day at every age from newborn to adult — no per-dose/per-day inversion, the frequency is consistent with the intent, but there is no age banding at all.
supp-001.source: IOM/NAM Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D, Tolerable Upper Intake Level table (NCBI Bookshelf); StatPearls Cholecalciferol monograph
supp-001.note: For an adult the stored 1000 units/day is reasonable (IOM RDA 600-800 IU/day; StatPearls cites 800-1000 IU/day for adults 50+ per the National Osteoporosis Foundation and 600-1000 IU/day for ages 1-18 per the Endocrine Society and IOM). The problem is that this is a paediatric/adult calculator with kind=fixed and an empty ageAdj, so a neonate or infant is shown the same 1000 units/day. The standard infant prophylaxis dose is 400 IU/day (the AI for 0-12 months, and the AAP recommendation for breastfed and partially breastfed infants), so the app shows 2.5x that — and 1000 IU/day sits exactly ON the IOM Tolerable Upper Intake Level for 0-6 months (25 µg/day = 1000 IU/day; 6-12 months is 38 µg = ~1500 IU/day). Second defect: the 10,000 unit ceilings. The UL is 100 µg/day = 4000 IU/day for ages 9 and above, 75 µg = 3000 IU for 4-8 y, 63 µg = 2500 IU for 1-3 y. A maxDaily of 10,000 units is 2.5x the adult UL and 10x the 0-6 month UL, so the engine will silently accept and never warn about a chronically toxic intake — and the record's own warnings array already says "Toksik doz: >10.000 IU/gün uzun süreli", i.e. the ceiling is set precisely at the dose the monograph calls toxic, which means the warning can only fire above the harmful threshold, never at it. Harm is cumulative (hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis) rather than from one dose, hence moderate rather than high.
supp-001.suggestedFix: Keep fixedDose 1000 units q24h as the adult maintenance default, and add ageAdjustments in years: [0, 1, 0.4] → 400 IU/day for infants, [1, 18, 0.6] → 600 IU/day for children and adolescents. Lower maxSingleDose/maxDailyDose from 10000 to 4000 units (the ≥9 y UL) and age-band the ceiling: 1000 units (0-6 months), 1500 (6-12 months), 2500 (1-3 y), 3000 (4-8 y), 4000 (≥9 y). Treatment of documented deficiency at higher doses (e.g. 2000-6000 IU/day, or 50,000 IU weekly) should be a separate, review-flagged entry requiring a serum 25(OH)D level, not a bump to this default.
supp-001.refuteReason: Could not refute — I verified both defects against the IOM/NASEM Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D directly. Table 5-3 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK56056, ch5.t8) gives the vitamin D Adequate Intake for 0-6 months and 6-12 months as "400 IU (10 ug)" per day, with an RDA of 600 IU (15 ug) for ages 1-70 and 800 IU (20 ug) above 70; the AAP's rickets-prevention guidance likewise sets 400 IU/day for breastfed and partially breastfed infants from the first days of life. The UL summary table (NBK56068, summarytables.t7) gives 25 ug/d for 0-6 months, 38 ug/d for 6-12 months, 63 ug/d for 1-3 y, 75 ug/d for 4-8 y and 100 ug/d for 9 y through adult — i.e. 1000, 1500, 2500, 3000 and 4000 IU/day at 40 IU per ug, exactly the figures the claim used. With kind=fixed, dose=1000 units and ageAdj=[], the app shows a neonate 1000 IU/day: 2.5x the recommended infant dose and sitting exactly ON the 0-6 month Tolerable Upper Intake Level. I confirmed neonates are in scope — the engine accepts age from 0 (calculations.ts validates only age < PATIENT_LIMITS.age.min / > max, and other records in this data set carry ageAdj bands starting at minAge 0). The record also refutes itself: its own productInfo.pediatricUse reads "Yenidogan: 400 IU/gun. Cocuk: 600 IU/gun (RDA)", contradicting the stored formula. The second defect holds too: maxSingle/maxDaily = 10000 units is 2.5x the adult UL and 10x the 0-6 month UL, and the entry's own warnings array says "Toksik doz: >10.000 IU/gun uzun sureli" — so the ceiling is set at the dose the monograph itself calls toxic and can only fire above the harmful threshold, never at it. Harm is cumulative (hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis) rather than from a single dose, so moderate severity is the right call. Suggested fix: ageAdj bands giving 400 units/day for 0-1 y, 600 units/day for 1-70 y and 800 units/day for >70 y (store dose=400 with factors 1.0/1.5/2.0, or age-banded fixed doses); set maxDaily by age to the UL — 1000 units 0-6 mo, 1500 units 6-12 mo, 2500 units 1-3 y, 3000 units 4-8 y, 4000 units 9 y and above — and route deficiency-treatment doses (1000-5000 IU/day, or high-dose loading) through a clinical-review flag with 25(OH)D and serum calcium monitoring.
supp-001.fix: 600 (sabit), q24h, tek doz tavanı 4000, günlük tavan 4000; 3 yaş bandı. Kaynak: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK56068/table/summarytables.t2/ (kaynaktan türetildi, bağımsız kontrolden geçti)

85.name: Semaglutid (Semaglutide)
85.stored: kind=fixed, dose 0.5 mg, freq q7d, maxSingle 2 mg, maxDaily 2 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Weekly total = 0.5 mg; engine's 'daily' total = 0.5/7 = 0.07 mg/day.
85.source: FDA label, Ozempic (semaglutide) injection, DailyMed — sections 2.2 Recommended Dosage and 8.4 Pediatric Use
85.note: The number itself is a real labelled dose, but semaglutide cannot be represented as one dose x frequency. The label requires a mandatory fixed escalation: 'Initiate OZEMPIC with a dosage of 0.25 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks', then 0.5 mg weekly, then (after >=4 weeks at each step) 1 mg, then 2 mg; 'The maximum recommended dosage is 2 mg once weekly.' A clinician reading a single default of 0.5 mg q7d would start a treatment-naive patient one step above the required initiation dose, skipping the 4-week 0.25 mg run-in that exists specifically to limit GI adverse reactions (nausea, vomiting, dehydration, and prerenal AKI; hypoglycaemia risk if combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea). Three further defects: (1) ageAdj is empty, so this paediatric/adult calculator will happily compute semaglutide for a child, while section 8.4 states 'Safety and efficacy of OZEMPIC have not been established in pediatric patients' (only semaglutide 2.4 mg for weight management is studied down to 12 years, a different product and a different ceiling). (2) maxSingle 2 mg is the Ozempic (type 2 diabetes) ceiling; it is wrong for the 2.4 mg once-weekly weight-management indication, so the max is indication-dependent and a single stored value cannot be right for both. (3) maxDaily=2 is semantically meaningless with q7d — 2 mg is a per-WEEK ceiling, and with the engine's daily-total arithmetic (0.07 mg/day) the maxDaily guard can never fire. Not immediately life-threatening, hence moderate rather than high.
85.suggestedFix: Do not model semaglutide as one dose x frequency. Either (a) store it as an explicit titration schedule: 0.25 mg SC once weekly x 4 weeks -> 0.5 mg once weekly x >=4 weeks -> 1 mg once weekly x >=4 weeks -> 2 mg once weekly (max for T2DM), or (b) if a single record must be kept, set dose = 0.25 mg, freq q7d, and attach a mandatory escalation note. Set maxSingle = 2 mg per week for the T2DM product and label it 'per week', not per day; drop or rename maxDaily. Add ageAdj [0, 18, 0] (contraindicated / not established under 18) for the Ozempic record; if the 2.4 mg weight-management product is wanted, store it as a separate record with its own escalation and ageAdj [0, 12, 0]. Keep renalAdj empty but flag that oral semaglutide (3/7/14 mg ONCE DAILY) is a different product entirely and must never be served from this record.
85.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED. I retrieved the Ozempic label independently and section 2.2 reads: 'Initiate OZEMPIC with a dosage of 0.25 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks'; 'After 4 weeks on the 0.25 mg dosage, increase the dosage to 0.5 mg once weekly'; 'If additional glycemic control is needed after at least 4 weeks on the 0.5 mg dosage, the dosage may be increased to 1 mg once weekly'; then the same >=4-week rule before 2 mg; 'The maximum recommended dosage is 2 mg once weekly.' Section 8.4: 'Safety and efficacy of OZEMPIC have not been established in pediatric patients.' A single stored fixed dose x frequency cannot express a four-step, time-gated, mandatory escalation, so MODEL_WRONG is the correct verdict, and the stored 0.5 mg default would start a treatment-naive patient one full step above the required 4-week 0.25 mg run-in that exists to limit GI toxicity. The empty ageAdj is also a genuine defect in a paediatric calculator given 8.4. Two of the claim's secondary points are weaker than stated and I do not endorse them: (a) maxSingle 2 mg is NOT wrong for this record, which is categorised Antidiabetics (i.e. the Ozempic 2 mg ceiling is exactly right; the 2.4 mg weight-management ceiling belongs to a different product that this record does not purport to cover); (b) the maxDaily 2 mg / q7d semantic mismatch is cosmetic. The core verdict and the moderate severity still stand on the escalation requirement alone. Suggested fix: represent as an escalation schedule (0.25 mg q7d x 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg q7d, then 1 mg q7d, then 2 mg q7d, each step >=4 weeks), maxSingle 2 mg per WEEK, and ageAdj [0, 18, 0].
85.blockNote: Semaglutid sabit tek bir doz olarak kullanılmaz: haftada bir 0,25 mg ile başlanır, en az 4 haftalık aralarla kan şekeri yanıtına göre 0,5 mg, 1 mg ve en fazla 2 mg'a çıkılır; obezite için kullanılan üründe ise hedef doz, üst sınır ve onaylı yaş grubu farklıdır. Hastanın hangi titrasyon basamağında olduğu ve hangi endikasyonla kullandığı bilinmeden doğru doz hesaplanamayacağı için doz gösterilmiyor.

87.name: Amyodaron (Amiodarone)
87.stored: kind=perKg, dose 5 mg/kg, freq prn, maxSingle 300 mg, maxDaily 2200 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. 70 kg adult -> 350 mg computed, clamped to 300 mg. 20 kg child -> 100 mg.
87.source: FDA label, Amiodarone HCl Injection, DailyMed (Dosage and Administration; Pediatric Use), cross-checked against StatPearls 'Amiodarone' for the ACLS/PALS arrest doses
87.note: The stored numbers correspond to CARDIAC ARREST bolus dosing only, and the record gives the clinician no way to know that. PALS/ACLS: pediatric pulseless VF/VT is 5 mg/kg IV/IO bolus, maximum 300 mg per dose; adult pulseless VF/pVT is a single 300 mg IV/IO push — so 5 mg/kg clamped to 300 mg reproduces the arrest dose correctly. But the FDA label's actual regimen for a patient WITH a pulse is a loading dose plus infusion that this model cannot express: '150 mg in 100 mL (in D5W) infused over 10 minutes', then '1 mg/min for 6 hours', then '0.5 mg/min thereafter', totalling about 1000 mg over the first 24 hours, with the warning that 'the initial infusion rate should not exceed 30 mg/minute' and that mean daily doses above about 2100 mg were associated with increased hypotension. The danger is the undeclared indication with freq='prn': a clinician treating stable wide-complex tachycardia or new AF would be shown 300 mg and no rate, i.e. double the labelled 150 mg load and with no instruction to run it over 10 minutes. A 300 mg IV push into a perfusing patient causes profound hypotension, bradycardia and can precipitate arrest — that is the high-severity failure mode. The same applies to paediatric perfusing tachyarrhythmias, where 5 mg/kg must be infused over 20-60 minutes, not pushed. Also: maxDaily 2200 mg is unreachable by any dose x frequency the engine can produce (it is an infusion total), so the ceiling is decorative; and the FDA label states 'The safety and effectiveness of amiodarone in pediatric patients have not been established; therefore, the use of amiodarone in pediatric patients is not recommended', with benzyl alcohol in the preserved formulation linked to fatal gasping syndrome in neonates — yet ageAdj is empty.
87.suggestedFix: Split into indication-specific records and carry the administration rate, because one dose x frequency cannot express this drug. (1) Cardiac arrest (pulseless VF/pVT): perKg 5 mg/kg IV/IO rapid bolus, maxSingle 300 mg, may repeat up to 2 further doses, cumulative cap 15 mg/kg or 2.2 g/24 h — label it 'PULSELESS ONLY'. (2) Perfusing wide-complex tachycardia / AF, adult: fixed 150 mg IV over 10 minutes (never a push), then 1 mg/min x 6 h, then 0.5 mg/min, max 2.2 g/24 h; store as a loading-dose-plus-infusion record, not perKg. (3) Perfusing tachyarrhythmia, paediatric: 5 mg/kg IV over 20-60 minutes, maxSingle 300 mg. Replace freq='prn' with an explicit repeat rule and a mandatory infusion-duration field. Add a neonatal warning for the benzyl-alcohol-preserved formulation and a note that paediatric use is off-label per the FDA label.
87.refuteReason: CLAIM REFUTED. The stored numbers are not an undeclared fragment of an infusion regimen; they are the authoritative cardiac-arrest bolus dose, correct for BOTH populations, in a record whose category is already 'Emergency'. StatPearls (amiodarone) states the pulseless VF/VT dose as: children '5 mg/kg per dose through the IV or IO route as a single administration, with a maximum limit of 300 mg per dose'; adults 'a single dose of 300 mg of amiodarone is administered IV or intraosseously (IO)'. The stored rule reproduces both exactly: a 20 kg child gets 100 mg, and a 70 kg adult computes 350 mg and is clamped to 300 mg, which is precisely the adult ACLS dose. freq=prn is the correct encoding for a bolus repeated as needed in arrest, not a missing frequency. The claim's charge that maxDaily 2200 mg is 'unreachable' and 'decorative' because 'it is an infusion total' is wrong on both counts: 2.2 g/24 h is the recognised cumulative 24-hour ceiling for amiodarone given by repeat bolus, and the FDA injection label independently supports a ceiling in that region, stating 'in controlled clinical trials, mean daily doses above 2100 mg were associated with an increased risk of hypotension'. With freq=prn and repeat dosing, that is exactly the right guard to store. The empty ageAdj is also defensible here rather than a defect: although the FDA label says 'The safety and effectiveness of amiodarone in pediatric patients have not been established; therefore, the use of amiodarone in pediatric patients is not recommended', StatPearls notes 'All pediatric indications of amiodarone are considered off-label. For precise dosing protocols, healthcare professionals should refer to institutional PALS guidelines' - and PALS affirmatively recommends 5 mg/kg in paediatric arrest, so setting a contraindication factor of 0 for children would make an emergency calculator refuse the one paediatric dose that is actually indicated. What remains legitimate is narrower than the claim and is a free-text/metadata gap, not a wrong stored value: the record carries no route, no infusion-rate note, and no indication string, so it does not tell the user that for a PERFUSING tachyarrhythmia the adult load is '150 mg in 100 mL (in D5W) infused over 10 minutes' and the paediatric 5 mg/kg must be infused over 20-60 minutes rather than pushed; the benzyl-alcohol 'gasping syndrome' warning for neonates is likewise absent. I would add an indication label ('pulseless VF/pVT - arrest bolus'), a route/rate field, and a neonatal benzyl-alcohol flag, but I cannot confirm the stored dose, cap or daily ceiling as wrong - they are right.

88.name: Atropin (Atropine)
88.stored: kind=perKg, dose 0.02 mg/kg, freq prn, maxSingle 1 mg, maxDaily 3 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. 70 kg adult -> 1.4 mg, clamped to 1 mg. 30 kg child -> 0.6 mg. 10 kg child -> 0.2 mg.
88.source: FDA label, Atropine Sulfate Injection (PLR format), DailyMed — Table 1 (adults) and Table 2 (paediatric), 'Symptomatic bradycardia' rows
88.note: The stored per-kg default is exactly the labelled figure. The paediatric table gives, for 'Symptomatic bradycardia due to increased vagal tone or primary AV conduction block': initial dose '0.02 mg/kg IV/IO', continued treatment 'Repeat as needed every 5 minutes', maximum single dose '<12 years: 0.5 mg; 12+ years: 1 mg'. The adult table gives 'Symptomatic bradycardia ... 0.5 mg IV/IM ... As needed every 3 to 5 minutes ... Maximum Total Dose 3 mg', so the stored maxDaily of 3 mg matches the adult cumulative cap. No per-dose/per-day multiplication error here: freq is prn, so the engine does not multiply anything up. Two residual defects, both minor rather than harmful. (1) maxSingle is a single age-blind 1 mg, but the label caps the paediatric single dose at 0.5 mg under 12 years. 0.02 mg/kg crosses 0.5 mg at 25 kg, so any child above roughly 25 kg but under 12 years (a 30 kg eight-year-old gets 0.6 mg, a 40 kg eleven-year-old 0.8 mg) is shown a dose above the labelled paediatric single-dose ceiling. The consequence is anticholinergic excess — sinus tachycardia, flushing, dry mouth, occasionally delirium — not a life-threatening event, which is why I rate this low rather than moderate. (2) The 3 mg total ceiling is the adult figure; a small child should not receive 3 mg cumulatively (the paediatric total caps in the adjacent antisialagogue row are 1 mg under 12 years and 2 mg at 12+). (3) Note for completeness that this record is correct for bradycardia only — organophosphate/carbamate poisoning uses 1-6 mg in adults and 0.02-0.06 mg/kg in children, doubling with each administration and with 'No maximum total dose', so that indication must never be served from this record.
88.suggestedFix: Keep dose = 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO, freq 'repeat q5 min prn' (adults q3-5 min). Replace the flat maxSingle 1 mg with an age-dependent cap: 0.5 mg for age <12 years, 1 mg for age >=12 years. Replace the flat maxDaily 3 mg with a cumulative cap of 3 mg for adults, 1-2 mg for children (or 0.04 mg/kg, whichever is lower). Label the record explicitly 'symptomatic bradycardia' and create a separate record for organophosphorus/carbamate/muscarinic-mushroom poisoning (adult 1-6 mg IV, paediatric 0.02-0.06 mg/kg, repeat q5 min doubling until secretions dry, no maximum total dose, maintenance infusion 10-20% of the loading dose per hour). Note that the current AHA guidance no longer mandates a 0.1 mg minimum dose, so no minimum needs to be added.

89.name: Furosemid (Furosemide)
89.stored: kind=perKg, dose 1 mg/kg, freq q8h, maxSingle 80 mg, maxDaily 600 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 3 mg/kg/day. 70 kg adult -> 70 mg per dose x 3 = 210 mg/day. 20 kg child -> 20 mg per dose x 3 = 60 mg/day.
89.source: FDA labels, Furosemide Tablets/Oral Solution (DailyMed) and Furosemide Injection USP (accessdata, NDA 018902 s036), Dosage and Administration
89.note: The per-dose number is defensible for children but the q8h scheduling and the per-kg model make the ADULT default roughly three to ten times the labelled starting dose. Oral label: 'The usual initial dose of furosemide is 20 to 80 mg given as a single dose', repeat 'not sooner than 6 to 8 hours', and maintenance is 'The individually determined single dose should then be given once or twice daily (e.g., at 8 am and 2 pm)' — i.e. once or twice daily, NOT three times daily. IV label: adult initial '20 to 40 mg given as a single IV injection'. So a 70 kg adult is shown 70 mg IV per dose (about 2-3x the 20-40 mg labelled IV starting dose) on a fixed q8h schedule for 210 mg/day, against a usual adult daily requirement of 20-80 mg. The stored maxDaily of 600 mg does correspond to the label ('The dose of furosemide may be carefully titrated up to 600 mg/day in patients with clinically severe edematous states'), but that is a titration ceiling for severe refractory oedema, not a routine target, and because 210 mg/day sits well under it the engine issues no warning at all. Harm: hypovolaemia, prerenal AKI, hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia with arrhythmia risk, and ototoxicity — significant in elderly or heart-failure patients but not lethal from a single dose, hence moderate. A second, separate defect: maxSingle 80 mg is the oral adult tablet strength ceiling, whereas the IV paediatric label states '1 mg/kg IV, not to exceed 20 mg per single dose'. A 40 kg child would be shown 40 mg IV, double that paediatric IV single-dose cap. Also note there is no renalAdj, even though furosemide dosing in renal impairment is materially different (higher doses needed, and the 600 mg/day figure belongs to that population).
89.suggestedFix: Split by route and age rather than using one per-kg q8h rule. Paediatric oral: 2 mg/kg as a single initial dose, increase by 1-2 mg/kg no sooner than q6-8h, maxSingle 6 mg/kg. Paediatric IV: 1 mg/kg per dose, maxSingle 20 mg, repeat no sooner than 2 hours during titration (common practice q6-12h for maintenance, not q8h fixed). Adult oral: fixed 20-80 mg per dose, freq once or twice daily (q12-24h), maxSingle 80 mg, maxDaily 600 mg reserved for severe oedematous states with an explicit warning. Adult IV: fixed 20-40 mg per dose, repeat at 2 hours if no response, maxSingle 80 mg. At minimum, change freq from q8h to q12h and add ageAdj so the adult branch uses fixed rather than per-kg dosing; add a renal note that higher doses are used in renal impairment and that the 600 mg/day ceiling belongs to that setting.
89.refuteReason: CLAIM REFUTED. I pulled the FDA furosemide injection label text directly and the claim's central supporting quote does not exist in it. The label's paediatric statement is: 'The usual initial dose of Furosemide Injection (intravenously or intramuscularly) in pediatric patients is 1 mg/kg body weight administered slowly', with the only ceiling being 'Doses greater than 6 mg/kg body weight are not recommended.' There is NO '1 mg/kg IV, not to exceed 20 mg per single dose' anywhere in the label, so the claim's second 'separate defect' fails: a 40 kg child shown 40 mg IV is receiving exactly the labelled initial dose, not double a cap. Consequently the recurring per-day-entered-as-per-dose error is NOT present in this record - 1 mg/kg is the label's genuine PER-DOSE paediatric value, and the resulting 3 mg/kg/day is half the label's 6 mg/kg not-recommended threshold. The adult figures are also inside the labelled range once the right range is used. The oral label states 'The usual initial dose of furosemide is 20 to 80 mg given as a single dose', so the 70 mg per dose computed for a 70 kg adult sits inside the labelled initial single-dose band, not '2-3x' it; the claim reaches '3 to 10 times' only by comparing a 210 mg DAILY total against a 20 mg SINGLE-dose figure and by assuming an IV route that this record does not specify. The stored maxDaily 600 mg is the label's own figure ('The dose of furosemide may be carefully titrated up to 600 mg/day in patients with clinically severe edematous states'), and 210 mg/day is well beneath it, so no false reassurance is being given about a number the label itself sanctions. Two residual criticisms in the claim are fair and I would still act on them, but neither makes the stored default wrong: q8h is more frequent than the adult maintenance instruction 'Administer this individually determined single-dose once or twice daily' (the injection label also permits a repeat only '2 hours later'), and renalAdj is empty. I would soften freq to q12h with an adult fixed-dose override of 20-80 mg and add a renal rule, but the stored 1 mg/kg per dose is defensible as a default and the claim's evidence for a paediatric overdose is not in the source.

90.name: Metilprednizolon (Methylprednisolone)
90.stored: kind=perKg, dose 1 mg/kg, freq q8h, maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 1000 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. Daily total = 3 mg/kg/day. 70 kg adult -> 70 mg per dose x 3 = 210 mg/day. 20 kg child -> 20 mg per dose x 3 = 60 mg/day.
90.source: FDA label, Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate for Injection USP, DailyMed — Dosage and Administration
90.note: This is the recurring per-day-entered-as-per-dose error, confirmed by arithmetic against the label. The label states the paediatric range as '0.11 mg/kg/day to 1.6 mg/kg/day in three or four divided doses' — that is a DAILY figure already divided, so the correct PER-DOSE value at q8h is 0.037 to 0.53 mg/kg. The record stores 1.0 mg/kg as the per-dose value and then applies q8h on top, producing 3 mg/kg/day: about 1.9x the top of the labelled daily range, and about 2x the top of the labelled per-dose value. The adult side is worse: the label's adult starting range is '10 mg to 40 mg of methylprednisolone depending on the specific disease entity', while the record computes 70 mg per dose and 210 mg/day for a 70 kg adult — roughly 5 to 20 times the labelled adult initial dose. Even the most permissive common indication does not rescue the number: NHLBI asthma-exacerbation dosing is 1-2 mg/kg/DAY in single or divided doses (commonly capped at 60 mg/day), which 3 mg/kg/day with no 60 mg cap still exceeds. The ceilings give no protection: maxSingle 1000 mg is pulse-therapy territory (the label's high-dose regimen is '30 mg/kg administered intravenously over at least 30 minutes ... repeated every 4 to 6 hours for 48 hours', explicitly a short-course rescue regimen, not a default), and maxDaily 1000 mg means the engine will never warn at 210 mg/day. Harm from sustained 3 mg/kg/day: hyperglycaemia and DKA risk, hypertension, hypokalaemia, steroid psychosis, GI bleeding, immunosuppression with masked infection, and adrenal suppression on withdrawal — significant toxicity rather than single-dose death, hence high rather than critical.
90.suggestedFix: Store the labelled daily figure divided by the frequency. Paediatric anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive: dose 0.4 mg/kg PER DOSE (range 0.03-0.53 mg/kg/dose), freq q6-8h, giving 1.6 mg/kg/day at the top of the labelled range; maxDaily 1.6 mg/kg/day. If an asthma-exacerbation default is wanted instead: 1-2 mg/kg/DAY, i.e. 0.5-1 mg/kg per dose q12h, maxSingle 60 mg, maxDaily 60 mg. Adult: switch to fixed dosing, 10-40 mg IV per dose (label range), typically q6-24h depending on indication, maxDaily 250 mg for ordinary anti-inflammatory use. Keep pulse dosing (30 mg/kg IV over >=30 min, q4-6h for up to 48 h, or 500-1000 mg daily x 3-5 days) as a SEPARATE explicitly-labelled record so the 1000 mg ceiling cannot be reached from the routine record. Lower this record's maxSingle from 1000 mg to 60-125 mg accordingly, and add a taper/duration warning.
90.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED. I retrieved the methylprednisolone sodium succinate label independently and every load-bearing quote checks out. Paediatric: the 'range of initial doses is 0.11 mg/kg/day to 1.6 mg/kg/day in three or four divided doses' - that is unambiguously a DAILY figure that is then divided, so the correct per-dose value at q8h is 0.037 to 0.53 mg/kg. The record stores 1 mg/kg as the per-dose value and applies q8h on top, giving 3 mg/kg/day, which is 1.9x the top of the labelled daily range and about 2x the top of the labelled per-dose value. This is exactly the recurring per-day-entered-as-per-dose error, and the arithmetic confirms it rather than merely restating the claim. The adult side is worse: the label's 'initial dosage will vary from 10 mg to 40 mg of methylprednisolone depending on the specific disease', against 70 mg per dose and 210 mg/day computed for a 70 kg adult - roughly 5 to 20x the labelled adult initial dose. I checked whether a permissive indication rescues the number and it does not: the same label gives asthma as '1 mg/kg/day to 2 mg/kg/day in single or divided doses', also a DAILY figure, which 3 mg/kg/day still exceeds, and the record carries no 60 mg/day paediatric asthma cap. The 30 mg/kg regimen is not a defence either, since the label frames it as a short high-dose rescue course: '30 mg/kg administered intravenously over at least 30 minutes. This dose may be repeated every 4 to 6 hours for 48 hours.' The ceilings give no protection: maxDaily 1000 mg means the engine never warns at 210 mg/day. High severity is proportionate - sustained 3 mg/kg/day risks hyperglycaemia, hypertension, hypokalaemia, GI bleeding, immunosuppression and adrenal suppression rather than single-dose death. Suggested fix: store 0.5 mg/kg per dose q12h (1 mg/kg/day, within the labelled paediatric and asthma daily ranges), maxSingle 60 mg, maxDaily 60 mg for the routine anti-inflammatory/asthma default, with the 30 mg/kg q4-6h pulse held as a separate explicitly-labelled high-dose record and an adult fixed-dose override of 10-40 mg.
90.blockNote: Metilprednizolon dozu hastalığa ve hastanın yanıtına göre belirlenir: erişkinde başlangıç dozu 10-40 mg, çocukta 0,11-1,6 mg/kg/gün arasında değişir, puls steroid tedavisinde ve multipl skleroz atağında çok daha yüksek dozlar kullanılır. Tek bir kural bu farklılığı doğru karşılayamadığı için doz hesaplanmıyor.

chemo-001.name: Sisplatin (Cisplatin)
chemo-001.stored: kind=perM2, dose 75 mg/m2, freq q21d, maxSingle 120 mg, maxDaily 120 mg, no ageAdj, no renalAdj. BSA 1.6 m2 -> 120 mg (cap reached). BSA 1.82 m2 (70 kg / 170 cm) -> 136.5 mg computed, clamped to 120 mg = 12% underdose. BSA 2.0 m2 -> 150 mg computed, clamped to 120 mg = 20% underdose.
chemo-001.source: FDA label, Cisplatin Injection, DailyMed — section 2 Dosage and Administration, boxed warning, section 2.5 dose modifications, section 8.4 Pediatric Use
chemo-001.note: The 75 mg/m2 q21d default is itself a genuine labelled regimen — for advanced ovarian cancer the label states cisplatin 'has been administered at 75 mg/m2 to 100 mg/m2 intravenously per cycle once every 3 to 4 weeks on Day 1' — but the 120 mg absolute cap silently truncates it for essentially every adult. The cap binds at any BSA above 1.6 m2, which is smaller than an average adult; a typical 1.8-2.0 m2 patient loses 12-20% of a curative- or control-intent cytotoxic dose with no visible warning, and under-dosing platinum chemotherapy is a direct route to treatment failure and relapse. That is the primary defect. Three further problems: (1) the dose is strongly indication-dependent and one default cannot cover it — advanced testicular cancer is '20 mg/m2 intravenously daily for 5 days per cycle' (a completely different schedule that this q21d single-dose record would overdose about fourfold if applied per day), and advanced bladder cancer is '50 mg/m2 to 70 mg/m2 ... once every 3 to 4 weeks'. (2) renalAdj is empty despite a boxed warning for nephrotoxicity ('Nephrotoxicity, Peripheral Neuropathy, Nausea and Vomiting, and Myelosuppression') and section 2.5's instruction to 'Consider alternative treatments or dose reductions for patients with impaired creatinine clearance' — a calculator that returns a full dose regardless of creatinine clearance is unsafe for this drug. (3) The record carries none of the mandatory supportive care: the label requires pre-treatment hydration and maintenance of 'adequate hydration and urinary output for 24 hours after Cisplatin Injection administration', plus antiemetics; and section 8.4 warns ototoxicity 'may be more severe and detrimental in pediatric patients ... particularly in patients less than 5 years of age', with no paediatric dosing given in section 2 at all — yet ageAdj is empty in a paediatric calculator. Also note the label's pharmacist alert, 'Please call prescriber if dose is greater than 100 mg/m2 per cycle', which the app does not reproduce.
chemo-001.suggestedFix: Remove the absolute 120 mg cap or raise it well above any achievable BSA-based dose; a cytotoxic per-m2 rule should not carry a flat mg ceiling below the computed dose. Replace maxSingle/maxDaily with a per-m2 alert at >100 mg/m2 per cycle (mirroring the label's pharmacist alert) rather than a silent clamp. Split into indication-specific records: ovarian 75-100 mg/m2 IV on Day 1 q21-28d; bladder 50-70 mg/m2 IV q21-28d; testicular 20 mg/m2 IV daily x 5 days per cycle (a distinct schedule, not q21d). Add renalAdj: no cisplatin / use an alternative agent at CrCl <60 mL/min per institutional guidance, with mandatory CrCl, serum creatinine, BUN, electrolyte and magnesium checks before each cycle. Add a hard requirement flag for pre- and post-treatment hydration (1-2 L over 8-12 h before, urine output maintained 24 h after) and antiemetic prophylaxis. Add ageAdj or a paediatric warning: the FDA label gives no paediatric dosing and flags severe ototoxicity under 5 years; paediatric cisplatin should only be given on a protocol, so this record should not return a value for children.
chemo-001.refuteReason: CLAIM CONFIRMED. I retrieved the cisplatin label independently and verified every quote the claim relied on: advanced ovarian cancer '75 mg/m2 to 100 mg/m2 intravenously per cycle once every 3 to 4 weeks'; advanced testicular cancer '20 mg/m2 intravenously daily for 5 days per cycle'; advanced bladder cancer '50 mg/m2 to 70 mg/m2 intravenously per cycle once every 3 to 4 weeks'; the boxed warning 'NEPHROTOXICITY, PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY, NAUSEA AND VOMITING, and MYELOSUPPRESSION'; section 2.5 'Consider alternative treatments or dose reductions for patients with impaired creatinine clearance'; the hydration requirement 'Maintain adequate hydration and urinary output for 24 hours after' administration; and the pharmacist alert 'Please call prescriber if dose is greater than 100 mg/m2 per cycle.' The decisive point is that the label's only overdose guard is expressed PER SQUARE METRE (>100 mg/m2 per cycle) - there is no absolute milligram cap anywhere in it, so the stored 120 mg has no labelled basis. 120 mg / 75 mg/m2 = 1.60 m2, which is below average adult BSA, so the cap binds for essentially every adult and silently truncates a curative- or control-intent cytotoxic dose: 1.82 m2 computes 136.5 mg and is clamped to 120 mg (12% loss), 2.0 m2 computes 150 mg and is clamped to 120 mg (20% loss), with no warning because maxDaily equals maxSingle. Platinum dose-intensity reduction of that magnitude is a direct route to treatment failure, so CAP_UNDERDOSES is the correct verdict. The secondary points also hold: one default cannot cover schedules as different as 20 mg/m2 x 5 days and 75 mg/m2 q21d, and an empty renalAdj is indefensible against a boxed nephrotoxicity warning plus section 2.5, as is an empty ageAdj given section 8.4's statement that ototoxic effects 'may be more severe and detrimental in pediatric patients ... particularly in patients less than 5 years of age'. Suggested fix: remove the absolute 120 mg cap and replace it with a per-cycle guard at 100 mg/m2 (BSA-scaled, matching the pharmacist alert), make the regimen indication-selectable (ovarian 75-100 mg/m2 q21-28d; bladder 50-70 mg/m2 q21-28d; testicular 20 mg/m2 daily x5), add renalAdj tied to creatinine clearance with a hold/dose-reduce rule, add a paediatric ototoxicity flag under 5 years, and attach the mandatory pre/post hydration and antiemetic text.
chemo-001.blockNote: Sisplatin dozu ve uygulama şeması kanser türüne göre değişir (testis kanserinde 5 gün boyunca günde 20 mg/m², over kanserinde 3-4 haftada bir 75-100 mg/m², mesane kanserinde 3-4 haftada bir 50-70 mg/m²) ve her kürden önce böbrek fonksiyonu ile kan sayımı değerlendirilmelidir. Tek bir kural bunları doğru karşılayamadığı için doz hesaplanmıyor; dozu protokole göre belirleyin.

supp-003.name: B12 Vitamini (Siyanokobalamin) / Cyanocobalamin
supp-003.stored: fixed 1000 mcg q24h = 1000 mcg/day; maxSingle 1000 mcg, maxDaily 1000 mcg; no age or renal rules
supp-003.source: FDA-registered OTC label, B-12 (cyanocobalamin) 1000 mcg tablet (DailyMed); corroborated by NICE evidence review, Vitamin B12 deficiency in over 16s
supp-003.note: Daily-total check (the recurring error in this data set) is clean: q24h x 1000 mcg = 1000 mcg/day, which is exactly what the label directs - 'Adults 18 years or older: 1000 mcg (1 tablet) daily preferably with a meal'. The NICE evidence review (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK603292/) independently states that 'when cyanocobalamin 1000mcg tablets are prescribed, the starting dose is one tablet a day', and at least 1 mg/day for malabsorption. Ceilings are consistent with the dose. Two non-harmful caveats worth noting rather than downgrading the verdict: (1) the same label says 'Persons under 18 years of age: Consult your doctor' and NICE covers only over-16s, yet this record has no age band, so a paediatric calculator will show a flat adult 1000 mcg for an infant - clinically tolerated (B12 is water-soluble with no established upper intake level, and 1000 mcg oral is used in paediatric deficiency) but not label-supported; (2) for purely dietary-origin deficiency NICE notes '50-150 mcg may be suitable', so 1000 mcg is the high end for that subgroup. Neither creates a toxicity risk.
supp-003.suggestedFix: Keep dose 1000 mcg, freq q24h, maxSingle 1000 mcg, maxDaily 1000 mcg. Optional refinement only: add an ageAdj band for children (e.g. [0,12,0.15] giving ~150 mcg/day for dietary-origin deficiency) or a note that under-18 use should be prescriber-directed.

supp-004.name: Folik Asit / Folic Acid
supp-004.stored: fixed 1 mg q24h = 1 mg/day; maxSingle 5 mg, maxDaily 5 mg; no age or renal rules
supp-004.source: FDA label, Folic Acid Tablets USP 1 mg (DailyMed, full prescribing information)
supp-004.note: Daily-total check is clean: q24h x 1 mg = 1 mg/day. The label states 'The usual therapeutic dosage in adults and children (regardless of age) is up to 1 mg daily', so the stored default is exactly the labelled therapeutic dose and the explicit 'regardless of age' wording means the fixed (non-weight-based) model is correct here even in a paediatric calculator. Two caveats that do not change the verdict: (1) the 5 mg ceiling goes beyond the label's statement that 'Daily doses greater than 1 mg do not enhance the hematologic effect' - 5 mg/day is nevertheless a routine real-world dose for folate-deficient megaloblastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia and methotrexate cover, so the ceiling is permissive rather than wrong; (2) the label warns that doses above 0.1 mg should not be used 'unless anemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency has been ruled out or is being adequately treated' (folate alone can mask pernicious anaemia while neurological damage progresses) - the app shows 1 mg by default with no such warning flag, and note that flag is false on this record. Maintenance (not therapeutic) requirements are much lower per the same label: infants 0.1 mg, children under 4 up to 0.3 mg, 4+ and adults 0.4 mg, pregnancy/lactation 0.8 mg.
supp-004.suggestedFix: Keep dose 1 mg, freq q24h, maxSingle/maxDaily 5 mg. Add a warning flag (flag: true) carrying the label's B12 caveat: 'Rule out or treat B12 deficiency first - folate alone can mask pernicious anaemia.' Optionally add a separate maintenance/prophylaxis entry at 0.4 mg (0.8 mg in pregnancy).

supp-006.name: Omega-3 Yag Asitleri / Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA)
supp-006.stored: fixed 2 g q24h = 2 g/day; maxSingle 4 g, maxDaily 4 g; no age rule, no renal rule
supp-006.source: StatPearls, Omega-3 Fatty Acids (NCBI Bookshelf), reporting FDA intake limits and the approved prescription doses
supp-006.note: Daily-total check is clean (q24h x 2 g = 2 g/day) - this is not an instance of the per-dose/per-day multiplication error. The problem is the ceiling and the missing age guard. The source states: 'The FDA recommends that daily intake not exceed 3 g/d of EPA and DHA combined, with no more than 2 g/d deriving from supplements.' The stored maxDaily of 4 g therefore sits above the FDA's total ceiling of 3 g/day and at double the 2 g/day supplemental limit; 4 g/day is only correct as a PRESCRIPTION dose (icosapent ethyl '4 g/d, as 2 2-gram capsules twice daily'; omega-3-acid ethyl esters '4 g/d') for adults with severe hypertriglyceridaemia, which is not this record's default indication - exactly the 'only correct for one indication' case the brief says to treat as a mismatch. The 2 g/day default is itself the absolute supplemental maximum, not a typical supplemental dose, so the app leaves a clinician no headroom. Separately, the same source states 'The FDA does not approve omega-3 fatty acid therapy for patients younger than 18', yet ageAdj is empty, so this paediatric calculator will happily show 2 g/day to an infant. Finally the unit is ambiguous in a way that matters: 2 'g' of fish oil is roughly 600 mg of EPA+DHA, while 2 g of EPA+DHA is about 6-7 g of fish oil - a ~3x difference depending on how the clinician reads it.
supp-006.suggestedFix: Store explicitly as EPA+DHA combined, not as fish oil: dose 1 g, freq q24h (typical cardiovascular supplemental intake), maxSingle 2 g, maxDaily 2 g (the FDA supplemental ceiling), and rename the unit label to 'g EPA+DHA'. Add ageAdj [[0,18,0]] to contraindicate/flag under-18 use, and if a hypertriglyceridaemia mode is wanted, make it a separate prescription record (icosapent ethyl 2 g bid = 4 g/day, adults only, TG >=500 mg/dL).
supp-006.refuteReason: REFUTED. The claim's ceiling argument does not survive contact with the FDA label. I retrieved the DailyMed omega-3-acid ethyl esters label, which states: "The daily dose of omega-3-acid ethyl esters is 4 grams per day taken as a single 4-gram dose (4 capsules) or as two 2-gram doses (2 capsules given twice daily)." So maxSingle 4 g and maxDaily 4 g are not invented ceilings sitting above a limit - they are verbatim FDA-labelled values, and 2 g is itself a labelled single dose. The claim's arithmetic also conflates two different quantities: the same label gives ~465 mg EPA + 375 mg DHA per 1-gram capsule, so the label's "4 g" is 4 g of omega-3 product = ~3.4 g of EPA+DHA, not 4 g of EPA+DHA. Measured the way the FDA measures it, the record's ceiling is at, not above, the 3 g/d EPA+DHA advisory figure the claim quotes. On the default itself the claim refutes itself: its own source says the FDA permits up to 2 g/d from supplements, and the stored default IS 2 g/day - at the limit is inside the limit, which is MATCHES, not MISMATCH. The claim's characterisation of 2 g/day as leaving "no headroom" is also a US-only reading; EFSA, which outranks StatPearls in the source hierarchy, concluded that "supplemental intakes of EPA and DHA combined at doses up to 5 g/day...did not raise safety concerns" (2012 opinion, restated in the 2026 supplemental-DHA opinion, PMC12802091), so the stored 2 g default and 4 g ceiling both sit below the European safety threshold. The paediatric point is the claim's strongest but is overstated: the FDA label's actual wording is "Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established" - a data gap, not a contraindication - and the 2026 EFSA opinion explicitly retains the 1 g/day DHA safe level "for all population groups (i.e. infants, children, adolescents and adults, including pregnant and lactating women)." A factor-0 ageAdj would therefore be wrong; at most a soft paediatric note is warranted. The unit ambiguity is real but does not move the number out of range under either reading: 2 g of fish oil (~600 mg EPA+DHA) and 2 g of EPA+DHA are both within accepted supplemental amounts. Residual, non-mismatch gaps worth logging separately, both low severity: no lower age band at all, and no note distinguishing product grams from EPA+DHA grams.

supp-007.name: Kalsiyum Karbonat / Calcium Carbonate
supp-007.stored: fixed 500 mg bid = 1000 mg/day; maxSingle 1000 mg, maxDaily 2500 mg; no age rule, no renal rule
supp-007.source: StatPearls, Dietary Calcium and Supplementation (NCBI Bookshelf); corroborated by StatPearls, Calcium Carbonate
supp-007.note: Daily-total check is clean (500 mg x 2 = 1000 mg/day) - not the multiplication error. The defect is salt-vs-elemental. The record is named for the SALT (calcium carbonate) with unit mg, but its numbers are only coherent as ELEMENTAL calcium: the source states 'The established upper limit of calcium intake is 2500 mg for adults aged 19 to 50 and 2000 mg for adults aged 51 and older', which is where the stored maxDaily of 2500 obviously comes from, and that figure is elemental calcium. Calcium carbonate is only ~40% elemental (StatPearls Calcium Carbonate, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK562303/: 1000 mg of calcium carbonate = 400 mg elemental calcium). Read literally as written - 500 mg of calcium carbonate twice daily - the patient receives 400 mg of elemental calcium per day, roughly a third of the 1000-1200 mg/day adult requirement and far below the 1500-2000 mg/day elemental used in treatment. So the record is either a 2.5x underdose or silently mislabelled. Two secondary problems: maxSingle of 1000 mg contradicts the source's absorption guidance that 'calcium supplements should not exceed 500 mg of elemental calcium per dose'; and maxDaily 2500 exceeds the stated UL of 2000 mg for adults 51 and older (the group most likely to be prescribed calcium) with no ageAdj to handle it, and is far above infant upper limits. Harm is under-treatment/over-supplementation over time rather than acute toxicity, hence low severity.
supp-007.suggestedFix: State the basis explicitly. Store as elemental calcium: dose 500 mg elemental, freq q12h (=1000 mg/day), maxSingle 500 mg elemental (absorption limit), maxDaily 2000 mg elemental; and change the display name to make the conversion visible, e.g. 'Kalsiyum karbonat 1250 mg (= 500 mg elementer kalsiyum)'. Add ageAdj bands so the 51+ upper limit of 2000 mg and the much lower infant/child upper limits are respected rather than relying on a single adult ceiling.
supp-007.refuteReason: REFUTED, and the claim is internally self-contradicting. The claim asserts the record must be read as the SALT and is therefore a 2.5x underdose. I retrieved StatPearls Calcium Carbonate (NBK562303) - the very monograph the claim cites for the 40% conversion - and it expresses supplementation dosing as the salt, not as elemental calcium: "For calcium supplementation, 500 mg to 4 grams of calcium carbonate may be taken orally daily, divided, and with meals." The stored 500 mg bid = 1000 mg/day of calcium carbonate falls squarely inside that authoritative range, divided and taken with meals exactly as instructed. Read literally as its name and unit say, the record is correct, not a 2.5x underdose. The same monograph gives the antacid dose as "500 mg to 1000 mg" per dose, "should not exceed 7 grams daily" - again as the salt - so maxSingle 1000 mg is precisely the labelled single-dose top, not an error. The claim then judges that same maxSingle 1000 mg against the ELEMENTAL rule from its other source (NBK549792: "calcium supplements should not exceed 500 mg of elemental calcium per dose"), which is the opposite reading from the one it just insisted on. 1000 mg of calcium carbonate is 400 mg elemental, i.e. BELOW the 500 mg elemental per-dose rule - there is no contradiction. The maxDaily point fails the same way: 2500 mg of the salt is 1000 mg elemental, far below the 2000-2500 mg elemental UL for every adult group including the 51+ group the claim worries about, below the monograph's own 4 g/day salt supplementation ceiling, and below the infant elemental ULs (1000 mg at 0-6 months). The ceilings are conservative, not excessive. The claim cannot have the dose be salt and the ceilings be elemental. Residual genuine (low-severity) improvement, not a mismatch: the record would be clearer if it stated "calcium carbonate (= 400 mg elemental calcium/day)" so a clinician reconciling against an RDA expressed in elemental calcium is not left to convert.

extra-001.name: Ibuprofen Pediatrik Surup / Ibuprofen
extra-001.stored: fixed 100 mg q8h (=300 mg/day base); ageAdj [[0.5,1,0.5],[1,3,1],[4,6,1.5],[7,9,2],[10,12,3]]; maxSingle 400 mg, maxDaily 1200 mg; no renal rule
extra-001.source: FDA OTC Drug Facts, Children's Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (DailyMed); and FDA prescription label, Ibuprofen Oral Suspension (DailyMed)
extra-001.note: Daily-total check is clean - 100 mg is genuinely a per-dose figure, not a mg/kg/day figure re-entered per dose. The failures are elsewhere. (1) UNGUARDED INFANTS - the most dangerous defect. Both OTC labels say under 6 months / under 2 years 'ask a doctor' and the prescription label gives a 'Minimum Age: 6 months'. There is no ageAdj band below 0.5 years and no factor-0 contraindication entry, so with no matching band the engine applies no adjustment and a 2-month-old, 5 kg infant is shown 100 mg q8h = 20 mg/kg/dose and 60 mg/kg/day, against the prescription label's stated 'Maximum daily dose: 40 mg/kg'. (2) GAPS BETWEEN BANDS at ages 3-4, 6-7 and 9-10, which fall through to the unadjusted 100 mg. A 9.5-year-old (~30 kg) is therefore shown 100 mg (~3.3 mg/kg) where the OTC chart directs 250 mg (12.5 mL) for 9-10 years - a ~2.5x underdose and likely treatment failure. (3) BAND EDGES OFF THE CHART even where bands do match: the chart is 2-3y 100 mg, 4-5y 150 mg, 6-8y 200 mg, 9-10y 250 mg, 11y 300 mg, so 6-year-olds get 150 instead of 200, 9-year-olds 200 instead of 250, and 12-23-month-olds get 100 mg where the Infants' drops label directs 75 mg (1.875 mL of 50 mg/1.25 mL). (4) WRONG MODEL FOR THE ENGINE: the prescription label gives '5 mg/kg if the baseline temperature is less than 102.5F, or 10 mg/kg if 102.5F or greater' for fever and '10 mg/kg, every 6 to 8 hours' for pain, and the OTC chart itself says to use weight to dose where possible - yet kind=fixed discards the weight the calculator already has. (5) The q8h-only frequency means no band ever reaches maxDaily 1200 (the largest is 3 x 300 = 900 mg), so that ceiling never fires, while the real safety limit (40 mg/kg/day) cannot be expressed at all.
extra-001.suggestedFix: Switch to kind=perKg: dose 10 mg/kg, freq q6-8h, maxSingle 400 mg (OTC adult single dose), maxDaily 1200 mg OTC / 40 mg/kg/day whichever is lower - ideally add a weight-derived daily cap of 40 mg/kg. Add ageAdj [[0,0.5,0]] to contraindicate under 6 months (factor 0), and drop the age bands entirely once dosing is weight-based. If an age-band fallback must be kept for when weight is unknown, reproduce the OTC chart exactly and with no gaps: 6-11 mo 50 mg, 12-23 mo 75 mg, 2-3 y 100 mg, 4-5 y 150 mg, 6-8 y 200 mg, 9-10 y 250 mg, 11 y 300 mg, 12 y and over 200-400 mg, all q6-8h, max 4 doses in 24 hours.
extra-001.refuteReason: REFUTED. The stored bands are not approximations of a US OTC chart - they reproduce a European regulator's SmPC age table exactly. I retrieved the Nurofen for Children 3 months to 9 years 100 mg/5 ml SmPC (UK MHRA), section 4.2: 6-12 months 2.5 ml (50 mg) 3-4 times/24h; 1-3 years 5 ml (100 mg) 3 times/24h; 4-6 years 7.5 ml (150 mg) 3 times/24h; 7-9 years 10 ml (200 mg) 3 times/24h - which is exactly the stored 100 mg base at q8h with factors 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0. The band boundaries the claim calls "gaps" (3/4, 6/7, 9/10) are the SmPC's own boundaries. The 10-12 y factor 3.0 gives 300 mg tds = 900 mg/day, which at 30-43 kg is 21-30 mg/kg/day, inside the same SmPC's "recommended daily dose...20-30 mg per kg of body weight, divided into equal doses, with dosing intervals of 6 to 8 hours." So claim point (3) fails: 150 mg at 6 y and 200 mg at 9 y are label doses, not errors, and nothing is a 2.5x underdose. Claim point (2) also fails on the code. Bands are matched inclusively (calculations.ts:228-230, age >= minAge && age <= maxAge), and the age field is keyboardType="number-pad" with maxLength 3 (CalculatorScreen.tsx:845) while weight and height use decimal-pad - age is entered as whole numbers, so every integer 1-12 matches a band and the claim's "9.5-year-old shown 100 mg" is not reachable through the calculator. Claim point (1) also overstates the engine: when bands exist and none match, the engine does not silently proceed - it pushes safety.noMatchingAgeBand (calculations.ts:640-646). Separately, the claim's sourcing is defective: I fetched the setid it cites (c3c600dd-6eec-4304-868e-9642de5e1dac) and it is an OTC Children's Ibuprofen Drug Facts label containing the age/weight chart and "do not use more than 4 times a day" - it contains no "Minimum Age: 6 months", no "5 mg/kg...10 mg/kg...102.5F", and no "Maximum daily dose: 40 mg/kg". Those quotes are attributed to a prescription label the claim never cites. Points (4) and (5) are not defects: the SmPC itself publishes an age-band table precisely so it can be used without a weight, and maxDaily 1200 mg is the adult OTC ceiling, which correctly never binds on a paediatric band. The verdict MISMATCH is not sustained. One residual gap is genuine and should be logged on its own terms rather than as a mismatch: there is no factor-0 band below 6 months, so age 0 matches nothing and 100 mg is displayed with only a warning-severity message, whereas the SmPC says "Not suitable for children under 3 months of age. Do not use this product in children weighing less than 5 kg." Suggested addition (not a correction of the stored doses): ageAdj entry [0, 0.25, 0] plus a <5 kg guard. Also note age 1 matches both [0.5,1] and [1,3]; the engine takes the more restrictive factor 0.5 (50 mg), which is still inside 4-10 mg/kg/dose for a 10 kg child.

extra-002.name: Asiklovir Krem/Tablet / Acyclovir
extra-002.stored: fixed 400 mg tid = 1200 mg/day; maxSingle 800 mg, maxDaily 4000 mg; no age rule, renalAdj EMPTY
extra-002.source: FDA label, ZOVIRAX (acyclovir) capsules/tablets/suspension (accessdata.fda.gov); and FDA label, Acyclovir Tablets USP (DailyMed); CDC STI Treatment Guidelines, Genital Herpes
extra-002.note: Daily-total check is clean (400 x 3 = 1200 mg/day) - this is not the multiplication error - but oral acyclovir cannot be represented by one dose x frequency at all, and the single stored default is unsafe in both directions. The FDA label (confirmed on the generic acyclovir tablets label, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=6f1db9f0-9b41-4fb7-8798-44fdc2c128df) lists entirely different regimens per indication: herpes zoster '800mg every 4 hours orally, 5 times daily for 7 to 10 days' (4000 mg/day); initial genital herpes '200mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily for 10 days'; chronic suppression '400mg 2 times daily'; intermittent therapy '200mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily for 5 days'; chickenpox in children 2 years and over '20mg/kg per dose orally 4 times daily (80mg/kg/day) for 5 days', and 800 mg 4 times daily for adults and children over 40 kg. Notably, 400 mg three times daily appears NOWHERE on the FDA label; it is a CDC guideline regimen for ONE indication only - first-episode genital herpes, 'Acyclovir 400 mg orally 3 times/day for 7-10 days' (https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm). As the app's single default it under-treats herpes zoster by 3.3x (1200 vs 4000 mg/day), which in shingles risks dissemination and post-herpetic neuralgia, and it ignores weight entirely for paediatric varicella, where dosing is 20 mg/kg/dose. MISSING RENAL ADJUSTMENT is the other serious gap: renalAdj is empty although the label carries a mandatory creatinine-clearance table (CrCl >25: 800 mg every 4 hours 5x daily; CrCl 10-25: 800 mg every 8 hours; CrCl 0-10: 200 mg every 12 hours, plus an extra dose after each dialysis session). Acyclovir is renally cleared and accumulates in impairment, causing crystal nephropathy and neurotoxicity - an elderly patient with CrCl 8 given the unadjusted 1200 mg/day is at real risk. Lastly, the record name bundles cream with tablet: topical acyclovir cream is applied 5 times daily and has no mg dose, so it cannot share a record with oral dosing.
extra-002.suggestedFix: Split into indication-specific records rather than one default. Adults: herpes zoster 800 mg 5x/day (q4h while awake) x 7-10 days, maxDaily 4000 mg; first-episode genital herpes 400 mg tid x 7-10 days (CDC) or 200 mg 5x/day x 10 days (label); chronic suppression 400 mg bid; episodic recurrence 800 mg bid x 5 days. Paediatric varicella: kind=perKg, 20 mg/kg/dose qid x 5 days, maxSingle 800 mg, maxDaily 3200 mg, ageAdj contraindicating under 2 years without specialist advice. Add renalAdj to every oral record from the label table - approximately [[25,999,1],[10,25,0.5],[0,10,0.25]] with the dosing interval extended (q8h for CrCl 10-25, q12h for CrCl 0-10), plus a post-dialysis dose note. Remove the cream from this record and give topical acyclovir its own non-mg entry (apply 5 times daily).
extra-002.refuteReason: NOT REFUTED - I independently confirmed the record is wrong, on two regulators rather than one. FDA acyclovir tablet label (DailyMed, generic acyclovir tablets) DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: herpes zoster "800mg every 4 hours orally, 5 times daily for 7 to 10 days"; initial genital herpes "200mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily for 10 days"; chronic suppression "400mg 2 times daily for up to 12 months"; intermittent "200mg every 4 hours, 5 times daily for 5 days"; chickenpox "20mg/kg per dose orally 4 times daily for 5 days" in children 2+, "800mg 4 times daily for 5 days" for adults and children over 40 kg. I cross-checked the UK SmPC for Aciclovir 400 mg Tablets (medicines.org.uk/emc/product/2352/smpc): HSV treatment 200 mg five times daily (doubled to 400 mg only in the severely immunocompromised, still five times daily); suppression 200 mg four times daily, or 400 mg twice daily, or 200 mg thrice daily; varicella/zoster 800 mg five times daily; paediatric varicella 2-5 years 400 mg four times daily, 6 years and over 800 mg four times daily. 400 mg three times daily appears on neither label - it is a CDC genital-herpes regimen only, which is exactly the single-indication default the brief says to treat as wrong. The consequences are real in both directions: against zoster the default gives 1200 mg/day where the label gives 4000; against paediatric varicella - the likeliest use of a paediatric calculator - it gives 1200 mg/day where the label gives 1600 (2-5 y) or 3200 (6 y and over), and a fixed mg dose cannot express the label's 20 mg/kg/dose paediatric rule at all. The empty renalAdj is independently confirmed as a mandatory omission: the FDA label carries a dosage-adjustment table (200 mg q4h -> CrCl 0-10: 200 mg q12h; 400 mg q12h -> CrCl 0-10: 200 mg q12h; 800 mg q4h -> CrCl >25 unchanged, CrCl 10-25: 800 mg q8h, CrCl 0-10: 800 mg q12h) and states an additional dose is administered after each dialysis; the UK SmPC matches. One detail in the claim is loose - it reports CrCl 0-10 as "200 mg every 12 hours" for the 800 mg zoster regimen, where the label says 800 mg q12h - but 200 mg q12h is the correct 0-10 row for the record's own 400 mg dose level, so the conclusion holds. MODEL_WRONG stands. Suggested fix: split into indication-specific records - zoster 800 mg q4h 5x/day (maxDaily 4000); first-episode/recurrent genital herpes 400 mg tid (maxDaily 1200); suppression 400 mg bid; paediatric varicella perKg 20 mg/kg q6h, maxSingle 800 mg, maxDaily 3200 mg; and drop the cream from the record entirely (5x daily topical, no mg dose). Add renalAdj [[25,999,1],[10,25,0.33 with q8h override],[0,10,0.5 with q12h override]] scaled to whichever oral regimen is selected, with a post-dialysis note.
extra-002.blockNote: Oral asiklovirin dozu endikasyona göre birkaç kat değişir (zonada 800 mg günde 5 kez, genital herpeste 200 mg günde 5 kez, baskılama tedavisinde 400 mg günde 2 kez, suçiçeğinde 20 mg/kg günde 4 kez) ve böbrek yetmezliğinde her rejimin doz aralığı ayrı ayrı uzatılır. Bu rejimler tek bir doz ve sıklık kuralıyla doğru gösterilemediği, krem formunun da mg cinsinden dozu olmadığı için doz hesaplanmıyor.
